articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: This announcement comes as the Kolkata Corporation election remains stalled by the Calcutta High Court; Mamata-Trinamool says why not hold elections and appoint elected representatives
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Union Minister of State and Bharatiya Janata Party MP Sukanta Majumdar on Saturday (November 21) said that they are preparing to appoint coordinators for all 209 wards in Kolkata. The announcement by the senior BJP leader from West Bengal, who has been entrusted with responsibility for the civic polls by the party, comes as elections to the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) remain suspended after a stay by the Calcutta High Court. “We are preparing for all 209 wards. If needed, we will appoint coordinators in 209 wards. Appointing a coordinator is a temporary matter, so there should be no legal issue in it,” Mr. Majumdar said. Only a day before. Mr. Majumdar had said that they would appoint coordinators in the 144 wards, which was the number of wards before delimitation. Calcutta High Court had granted a stay on the announcement of dates of civic polls on a petition challenging that delimitation was not done as per established norms. Meanwhile, the Opposition have raised alarm over the BJP appointing its own people as civic body coordinators instead of legally appointing elected representatives. “BJP people becoming coordinators is unacceptable. If BJP people want to come to power, get elected and take the seats or increase the tenure of the previously elected representatives, or appoint government representatives,” Mamata-Trinamool Congress MLA Kunal Ghosh said. Communist Party of India (Marxist) leader Sujan Chakraborty said that this is the BJP using backdoor methods to get BJP people at the top of the civic bodies as coordinators and control the Corporation. “This is the backdoor policy to control the KMC, and it is a forceful acquisition of the civic body without a free and fair election,” Congress State general secretary Ashutosh Chatterjee told The Hindu on Saturday (November 21, 2026). On August 22, KMC published a draft list of 209 wards, increasing it from 144 wards. The Calcutta High Court on November 6 had restrained the West Bengal State Election Commission from issuing any notification for the KMC elections based on newly redrawn wards until a pending petition challenging the delimitation exercise is decided. The State government has filed a petition with the Supreme Court to ask it to lift the ban on holding the civic polls. The top court is likely to hear the matter of the KMC ward delimitation and civic poll petition on Monday (November 23).
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The last KMC election was held in 2021, in which the Trinamool Congress won 134 seats out of 144. The Trinamool Congress board at KMC was dissolved weeks after the BJP came to power in West Bengal on May 4, 2026. KMC Mayor Firhad Hakim resigned from his post, stating that he wanted a dignified exit from the post as the civic body has become “practically defunct” after the regime change in the State.

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The police complaint, was registered at city’s Kalighat Police station by Subhasish Chakraborty on behalf of Trinamool Congress; in the complaint, the loyalist of Mamata Banerjee has claimed that he has credible proofs that Nanoor police station officials conspired with Ritabrata Banerjee and Arup Roy to prepare false and fabricated affidavits

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Mamata Banerjee faction of the Trinamool Congress has filed a police complaint against Leader of Opposition in the West Bengal Assembly Ritabrata Banerjee, chairperson of Democratic Trinamool Congress Arup Roy and two officers of the Nanoor Police station for falsification, forging signatures of unsuspecting citizens and creation and fabrication of affidavits which have been filed before the Election Commission of India, The police complaint was registered at the city’s Kalighat Police Station by Subhasish Chakraborty on behalf of the Trinamool Congress. In the complaint, a loyalist of Mamata Banerjee has claimed that he has credible proof that Nanoor police station officials conspired with Ritabrata Banerjee and Arup Roy to prepare false and fabricated affidavits. “The material and evidence presently in my possession disclose that an organised exercise has been undertaken through the machinery of Nanoor Police Station for the preparation of fake affidavits in support of the rival faction, including affidavits purporting to show that ordinary members of the public recognise Arup Roy as the leader of the AITC and do not accept Smt. Mamata Banerjee as its leader,” reads the copy of the police complaint that has been accessed by The Hindu . The accusation in the police complaint dated November 20, that these individuals systematically fabricated, forged, and authenticated false affidavits using unauthorized notarial stamps and forged signatures of both citizens and a Notary Public. The development comes after Trinamool leader and Diamond Harbour Abhishek Banerjee, on November 5, claimed that he has video evidence which shows affidavits in support of Ritabrata Banerjee being filled out and prepared inside police station “I am prepared to submit this footage before the Supreme Court and provide copies to members of the media and the Election Commission. I am making this statement with responsibility, and I want the entire process of preparing these affidavits to be investigated,” Mr. Banerjee had said. 80 MLAs of the Trinamool Congress were elected to the West Bengal Assembly after the 2026 Assembly polls. 65 of the MLAs supported the claim of Ritabrata Banerjee to the Leader of Opposition, which the Mamata faction of the party has challenged. With both factions staking claim over the party, the Election Commission of India on September 17, 2026, had barred both factions, the Mamata Banerjee-led faction and the Ritabrata Banerjee-led faction of the party, from using the party symbol. The very next day, on September 18, the Mamata faction got the name ‘Mamata All India Trinamool Congress’ with ‘football player’ as its symbol, while the Ritabrata grouping was allotted the name ‘Democratic Trinamool Congress’ with the symbol ‘envelope’. Both factions of Trinamool Congress have submitted truckloads of affidavits to the ECI, which include support by party members MP and MLAs.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: police / All India Trinamool Congress / crime / Election Commission of India

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #11 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Police complaint against WB LoP, police officers for fabrication of affidavits before ECI

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 01:16:56 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The police complaint, was registered at city’s Kalighat Police station by Subhasish Chakraborty on behalf of Trinamool Congress; in the complaint, the loyalist of Mamata Banerjee has claimed that he has credible proofs that Nanoor police station officials conspired with Ritabrata Banerjee and Arup Roy to prepare false and fabricated affidavits

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Mamata Banerjee faction of the Trinamool Congress has filed a police complaint against Leader of Opposition in the West Bengal Assembly Ritabrata Banerjee, chairperson of Democratic Trinamool Congress Arup Roy and two officers of the Nanoor Police station for falsification, forging signatures of unsuspecting citizens and creation and fabrication of affidavits which have been filed before the Election Commission of India, The police complaint was registered at the city’s Kalighat Police Station by Subhasish Chakraborty on behalf of the Trinamool Congress. In the complaint, a loyalist of Mamata Banerjee has claimed that he has credible proof that Nanoor police station officials conspired with Ritabrata Banerjee and Arup Roy to prepare false and fabricated affidavits. “The material and evidence presently in my possession disclose that an organised exercise has been undertaken through the machinery of Nanoor Police Station for the preparation of fake affidavits in support of the rival faction, including affidavits purporting to show that ordinary members of the public recognise Arup Roy as the leader of the AITC and do not accept Smt. Mamata Banerjee as its leader,” reads the copy of the police complaint that has been accessed by The Hindu . The accusation in the police complaint dated November 20, that these individuals systematically fabricated, forged, and authenticated false affidavits using unauthorized notarial stamps and forged signatures of both citizens and a Notary Public. The development comes after Trinamool leader and Diamond Harbour Abhishek Banerjee, on November 5, claimed that he has video evidence which shows affidavits in support of Ritabrata Banerjee being filled out and prepared inside police station “I am prepared to submit this footage before the Supreme Court and provide copies to members of the media and the Election Commission. I am making this statement with responsibility, and I want the entire process of preparing these affidavits to be investigated,” Mr. Banerjee had said. 80 MLAs of the Trinamool Congress were elected to the West Bengal Assembly after the 2026 Assembly polls. 65 of the MLAs supported the claim of Ritabrata Banerjee to the Leader of Opposition, which the Mamata faction of the party has challenged. With both factions staking claim over the party, the Election Commission of India on September 17, 2026, had barred both factions, the Mamata Banerjee-led faction and the Ritabrata Banerjee-led faction of the party, from using the party symbol. The very next day, on September 18, the Mamata faction got the name ‘Mamata All India Trinamool Congress’ with ‘football player’ as its symbol, while the Ritabrata grouping was allotted the name ‘Democratic Trinamool Congress’ with the symbol ‘envelope’. Both factions of Trinamool Congress have submitted truckloads of affidavits to the ECI, which include support by party members MP and MLAs.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: police / All India Trinamool Congress / crime / Election Commission of India

A. The police complaint, was registered at city’s Kalighat Police station by Subhasish Chakraborty on behalf of Trinamool Congress; in the complaint,...

C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Police complaint against WB LoP, police offic' should be permanently discontinued.

✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. articles.title: Key takeaways from the Quad, ASEAN-India, and East Asia Summits in Manila | Explained
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Narendra Modi’s multilateral ASEAN engagements showed a growing desire to work more closely with the grouping at a time when global powers are working in a more unilateral manner

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Prime Minister Narendra Modi took part in three back-to-back multilateral meetings on the sidelines of the annual Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) summits in Manila this week. The ASEAN-India Summit, East Asia Summit, and Quad Summit, which was attended by U.S. President Donald Trump, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese apart from Mr. Modi, ended with several concrete announcements. They sent a deeper underlying message on India’s broad-basing of its “Act East” and Indo-Pacific policies, even as the world turned its attention to the Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral later in the week.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In 2025, Mr. Modi skipped the ASEAN summits in Kuala Lumpur over what was seen as a combination of domestic commitments around Deepavali and trade friction with U.S. President Donald Trump.

articles.title: How U.S. controls flow of advanced tech, chip, and compute to China | Explained

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The U.S. Commerce Department on November 16 issued an interim final rule barring data centre operators outside the U.S. equipped with advanced American AI chips from providing cloud service to businesses in two dozen countries, including China, Iran, and Russia

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The story so far: The battle for the most-sought-after commodity that underpins development of artificial intelligence technology just grew fiercer. On November 16, the U.S. Commerce Department issued an interim final rule (IFR) requiring companies to have licences to supply advanced American AI chips to data centre operators outside the U.S. with substantial computing power to businesses headquartered in two dozen countries, including China, Iran, and Russia. The new rule restricts American companies from freely shipping high-end AI chips to a set of five countries, including Indonesia, Malaysia, and Singapore, without the explicit approval of the U.S. government. China has censured the move, calling it “yet another case of the U.S. overstretching the concept of national security, and abusing export control measures to interfere in normal trade and tech cooperation between China and other countries and go after China’s high-tech industry”. The interim rule came just days ahead of the meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and China’s President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, China on the sidelines of the November 18-19 APEC Summit. The U.S. government’s policy on making advanced technology inaccessible to China has been a talking point among lawmakers in Washington for well over a decade, but Congress strengthened the extant legal framework only during the first Trump term when it passed the Export Control Reform Act in 2018. It strengthened the U.S. government’s authority to control the movement of advanced technology originating in the country, and included curbing exports of sensitive technologies, including top-tier chips, with dual-use — both commercial and military — applications to countries such as China, Russia, and Iran. A year later, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) placed Chinese telecom equipment maker Huawei and its affiliates on the Entity List, effectively blocking their access to high-end semiconductors.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Hindu Explains / semiconductors and active components / Artificial Intelligence / international relations / USA / China / technology (general)

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #28 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 How U.S. controls flow of advanced tech, chip, and compute to China | Explained

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 05:16:29 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The U.S. Commerce Department on November 16 issued an interim final rule barring data centre operators outside the U.S. equipped with advanced American AI chips from providing cloud service to businesses in two dozen countries, including China, Iran, and Russia

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The story so far: The battle for the most-sought-after commodity that underpins development of artificial intelligence technology just grew fiercer. On November 16, the U.S. Commerce Department issued an interim final rule (IFR) requiring companies to have licences to supply advanced American AI chips to data centre operators outside the U.S. with substantial computing power to businesses headquartered in two dozen countries, including China, Iran, and Russia. The new rule restricts American companies from freely shipping high-end AI chips to a set of five countries, including Indonesia, Malaysia, and Singapore, without the explicit approval of the U.S. government. China has censured the move, calling it “yet another case of the U.S. overstretching the concept of national security, and abusing export control measures to interfere in normal trade and tech cooperation between China and other countries and go after China’s high-tech industry”. The interim rule came just days ahead of the meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and China’s President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, China on the sidelines of the November 18-19 APEC Summit. The U.S. government’s policy on making advanced technology inaccessible to China has been a talking point among lawmakers in Washington for well over a decade, but Congress strengthened the extant legal framework only during the first Trump term when it passed the Export Control Reform Act in 2018. It strengthened the U.S. government’s authority to control the movement of advanced technology originating in the country, and included curbing exports of sensitive technologies, including top-tier chips, with dual-use — both commercial and military — applications to countries such as China, Russia, and Iran. A year later, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) placed Chinese telecom equipment maker Huawei and its affiliates on the Entity List, effectively blocking their access to high-end semiconductors.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Hindu Explains / semiconductors and active components / Artificial Intelligence / international relations / USA / China / technology (general)

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: ‘In an effort to pursue every option for forming a new government, Yashar Chair Gadi Eisenkot has instructed the party's negotiating team to invite its Likud counterparts to a marathon series of talks beginning with the meeting already scheduled for tomorrow’ read a statement

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Gadi Eisenkot , who is tasked with forming the next Israeli government, has invited the right-wing Likud party of caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for coalition talks, his party said on Saturday (November 21, 2026). Mr. Eisenkot's centrist Yashar party said the talks, scheduled to begin on Sunday (November 22), reflected a "genuine commitment to forming the broadest possible government". Former military chief Mr. Eisenkot has until next month to form a government to replace Mr. Netanyahu, after the October election failed to deliver a clear majority for either bloc. Saturday's (November 21) announcement comes as Mr. Eisenkot's wide-ranging anti-Netanyahu camp faces divisions on whether to forge alliances with the ultra-Orthodox parties and Arab-majority lists, or form a national unity government with Mr. Netanyahu's bloc. "In an effort to pursue every option for forming a new government, Yashar Chair Gadi Eisenkot has instructed the party's negotiating team to invite its Likud counterparts to a marathon series of talks beginning with the meeting already scheduled for tomorrow [November 22]," the party said in a statement. 📰 Eisenkot invites Netanyahu’s party for Israeli coalition talks

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 02:44:12 AM

1. Core Context & Background: ‘In an effort to pursue every option for forming a new government, Yashar Chair Gadi Eisenkot has instructed the party's negotiating team to invite its Likud counterparts to a marathon series of talks beginning with the meeting already scheduled for tomorrow’ read a statement

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Gadi Eisenkot , who is tasked with forming the next Israeli government, has invited the right-wing Likud party of caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for coalition talks, his party said on Saturday (November 21, 2026). Mr. Eisenkot's centrist Yashar party said the talks, scheduled to begin on Sunday (November 22), reflected a "genuine commitment to forming the broadest possible government". Former military chief Mr. Eisenkot has until next month to form a government to replace Mr. Netanyahu, after the October election failed to deliver a clear majority for either bloc. Saturday's (November 21) announcement comes as Mr. Eisenkot's wide-ranging anti-Netanyahu camp faces divisions on whether to forge alliances with the ultra-Orthodox parties and Arab-majority lists, or form a national unity government with Mr. Netanyahu's bloc. "In an effort to pursue every option for forming a new government, Yashar Chair Gadi Eisenkot has instructed the party's negotiating team to invite its Likud counterparts to a marathon series of talks beginning with the meeting already scheduled for tomorrow [November 22]," the party said in a statement. It added that it would "leave no stone unturned as it works to make bold moves possible and secure the breakthrough needed to form a government". Former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, an important figure in Mr. Eisenkot's camp, on Saturday (November 21) called for a "Zionist unity government headed by Eisenkot" and said his party would refuse to join up with Mr. Netanyahu or his bloc. In a statement, Mr. Bennett said he was "committed to ensuring that Netanyahu will not be the next Prime Minister of the State of Israel, and my party will not join him or his bloc under any circumstances", he added. Mr. Netanyahu has been pushing hard for a national unity government, which he says is needed to guarantee Israel's security.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Eisenkot has indicated he would be open to forming a government with members of Mr. Netanyahu's Likud, but has previously ruled out serving in a government led by Mr. Netanyahu himself.

articles.title: India, Bulgaria discuss bilateral ties, IMEC, Black Sea situation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: ‘Our teams have drawn up a detailed roadmap of cooperation, so we will be approving that today, and I think that will give a very clear pathway to our activities ahead,’ said S. Jaishankar

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: India and Bulgaria on Saturday (November 22, 2026) reviewed their bilateral cooperation in trade, security, technology and other areas, even as the two sides also held discussions on IMEC, the Black Sea situation and the Ukraine conflict. External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar held talks with his Bulgarian counterpart, Velislava Petrova, at the Hyderabad House in Delhi. "Pleased to meet FM Bulgaria @vpetrova_mfa this afternoon. Reviewed our bilateral cooperation, including in trade, connectivity, investments, technology, security and talent mobility. Appreciated growing P2P linkages & cultural exchanges between our two countries, as well as deepening India-EU ties," Mr. Jaishankar later posted on X. Agreed that the India-EU FTA should be followed through by "vigorous exchanges between our businesses". Also exchanged views on the prospects of IMEC (India Middle East Europe Economic Corridor) and other connectivity initiatives, he added. "Appreciated the discussion on the Black Sea situation and the Ukraine conflict," the EAM said in his post. In his opening remarks during their meeting, Mr. Jaishankar said, "Our teams have drawn up a detailed roadmap of cooperation, so we will be approving that today, and I think that will give a very clear pathway to our activities ahead." He said Ms. Petrova's visit was taking place when India is "also intensifying our relationship with the European Union, and we again thank you for all the support that you have extended to that process". The entry into force of the Free Trade Agreement (FTA), which India expects soon, will certainly provide a "new dynamism to that relationship, and when it comes to trade, technology, talent, we expect to do much more with Europe," the EAM said. Mr. Jaishankar, during the meeting, also conveyed to her India's condolences to the "families who lost their loved ones in the tragic road accident" recently and wished a speedy recovery to the injured.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: "I also want to take this opportunity to thank you for the support that your government has extended for the repatriation of our seafarers in the ships that were attacked in the Black Sea and looking after some of them who had sustained injuries," he added.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #12 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 India, Bulgaria discuss bilateral ties, IMEC, Black Sea situation

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 02:58:42 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: ‘Our teams have drawn up a detailed roadmap of cooperation, so we will be approving that today, and I think that will give a very clear pathway to our activities ahead,’ said S. Jaishankar

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: India and Bulgaria on Saturday (November 22, 2026) reviewed their bilateral cooperation in trade, security, technology and other areas, even as the two sides also held discussions on IMEC, the Black Sea situation and the Ukraine conflict. External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar held talks with his Bulgarian counterpart, Velislava Petrova, at the Hyderabad House in Delhi. "Pleased to meet FM Bulgaria @vpetrova_mfa this afternoon. Reviewed our bilateral cooperation, including in trade, connectivity, investments, technology, security and talent mobility. Appreciated growing P2P linkages & cultural exchanges between our two countries, as well as deepening India-EU ties," Mr. Jaishankar later posted on X. Agreed that the India-EU FTA should be followed through by "vigorous exchanges between our businesses". Also exchanged views on the prospects of IMEC (India Middle East Europe Economic Corridor) and other connectivity initiatives, he added. "Appreciated the discussion on the Black Sea situation and the Ukraine conflict," the EAM said in his post. In his opening remarks during their meeting, Mr. Jaishankar said, "Our teams have drawn up a detailed roadmap of cooperation, so we will be approving that today, and I think that will give a very clear pathway to our activities ahead." He said Ms. Petrova's visit was taking place when India is "also intensifying our relationship with the European Union, and we again thank you for all the support that you have extended to that process". The entry into force of the Free Trade Agreement (FTA), which India expects soon, will certainly provide a "new dynamism to that relationship, and when it comes to trade, technology, talent, we expect to do much more with Europe," the EAM said. Mr. Jaishankar, during the meeting, also conveyed to her India's condolences to the "families who lost their loved ones in the tragic road accident" recently and wished a speedy recovery to the injured.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: "I also want to take this opportunity to thank you for the support that your government has extended for the repatriation of our seafarers in the ships that were attacked in the Black Sea and looking after some of them who had sustained injuries," he added.

articles.title: Medicos warn against craze for fairness after 17-year-old Keralam girl diagnosed with kidney disorder
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Medical experts say that the use of fairness creams containing heavy metals such as mercury to lighten the skin is emerging as a major health hazard that can lead to serious conditions such as kidney failure if not diagnosed early

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The craze for fairness is more than skin-deep, and the trade-off can be costly. Inferior cosmetic products can end up harming your vital organs. A 17-year-old girl in Keralam’s Malappuram developed a serious kidney ailment allegedly after using a fairness cream purchased online following its promotion by social media influencers, according to the doctors treating her. The incident came to light after the authorities at the hospital that treated the teenager, who was diagnosed with membranous nephropathy, held a press conference on Friday. Lab tests had confirmed 1.25% mercury in the cosmetic product, according to the hospital sources. Medical experts say that the use of fairness creams containing heavy metals such as mercury to lighten the skin is emerging as a major health hazard that can lead to serious conditions such as kidney failure if not diagnosed early. Warning against following social media beauty trends and using topical creams seen online or bought over the counter without a prescription, M.M. Faizal, former president of the Indian Association of Dermatologists, Venereologists and Leprologists, says people lack awareness of how topical applications can enter the bloodstream. “People are obsessed with fair skin. We have observed a rise in the number of people buying steroid creams that are easily available over the counter and applying them to their faces. Such steroid-based applications and creams containing heavy metals such as mercury can damage your kidneys easily. The government needs to bring in some mechanisms to control this,” he says. A rise in the number of teenagers relying on spurious beauty products has forced the Keralam Drugs Control department to launch awareness campaigns targeting students in Classes XI and XII, an age group particularly vulnerable to online campaigns. Frequent inspections are carried out in marketplaces to confiscate spurious cosmetics. State Drugs Controller K. Sujith Kumar says raising awareness about such spurious cosmetic products is the only way forward. “We have seized cosmetics that have high mercury levels from offline markets. But there is no way to track or regulate online marketplaces,” he says.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Prolonged use of such creams can lead to kidney damage, says former secretary of the Nephrology Association of Kerala, Jayant Thomas Mathew, who has come across a few cases of kidney disorders among users. The condition could be detected early because the patients were aware of the symptoms.

📰 Medicos warn against craze for fairness after 17-year-old Keralam girl diagnosed with kidney disorder

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 01:44:51 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Medical experts say that the use of fairness creams containing heavy metals such as mercury to lighten the skin is emerging as a major health hazard that can lead to serious conditions such as kidney failure if not diagnosed early

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The craze for fairness is more than skin-deep, and the trade-off can be costly. Inferior cosmetic products can end up harming your vital organs. A 17-year-old girl in Keralam’s Malappuram developed a serious kidney ailment allegedly after using a fairness cream purchased online following its promotion by social media influencers, according to the doctors treating her. The incident came to light after the authorities at the hospital that treated the teenager, who was diagnosed with membranous nephropathy, held a press conference on Friday. Lab tests had confirmed 1.25% mercury in the cosmetic product, according to the hospital sources. Medical experts say that the use of fairness creams containing heavy metals such as mercury to lighten the skin is emerging as a major health hazard that can lead to serious conditions such as kidney failure if not diagnosed early. Warning against following social media beauty trends and using topical creams seen online or bought over the counter without a prescription, M.M. Faizal, former president of the Indian Association of Dermatologists, Venereologists and Leprologists, says people lack awareness of how topical applications can enter the bloodstream. “People are obsessed with fair skin. We have observed a rise in the number of people buying steroid creams that are easily available over the counter and applying them to their faces. Such steroid-based applications and creams containing heavy metals such as mercury can damage your kidneys easily. The government needs to bring in some mechanisms to control this,” he says. A rise in the number of teenagers relying on spurious beauty products has forced the Keralam Drugs Control department to launch awareness campaigns targeting students in Classes XI and XII, an age group particularly vulnerable to online campaigns. Frequent inspections are carried out in marketplaces to confiscate spurious cosmetics. State Drugs Controller K. Sujith Kumar says raising awareness about such spurious cosmetic products is the only way forward. “We have seized cosmetics that have high mercury levels from offline markets. But there is no way to track or regulate online marketplaces,” he says.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Prolonged use of such creams can lead to kidney damage, says former secretary of the Nephrology Association of Kerala, Jayant Thomas Mathew, who has come across a few cases of kidney disorders among users. The condition could be detected early because the patients were aware of the symptoms.

articles.summary: 1. Core Context & Background: Medical experts say that the use of fairness creams containing heavy metals such as mercury to lighten the skin is emerging as a major health hazard that can lead to serious conditions such as kidney failure if not diagnosed early
articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: Medical experts say that the use of fairness creams containing heavy metals such as mercury to lighten the skin is emerging as a major health hazard that can lead to serious conditions such as kidney failure if not diagnosed early
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The craze for fairness is more than skin-deep, and the trade-off can be costly. Inferior cosmetic products can end up harming your vital organs. A 17-year-old girl in Keralam’s Malappuram developed a serious kidney ailment allegedly after using a fairness cream purchased online following its promotion by social media influencers, according to the doctors treating her. The incident came to light after the authorities at the hospital that treated the teenager, who was diagnosed with membranous nephropathy, held a press conference on Friday. Lab tests had confirmed 1.25% mercury in the cosmetic product, according to the hospital sources. Medical experts say that the use of fairness creams containing heavy metals such as mercury to lighten the skin is emerging as a major health hazard that can lead to serious conditions such as kidney failure if not diagnosed early. Warning against following social media beauty trends and using topical creams seen online or bought over the counter without a prescription, M.M. Faizal, former president of the Indian Association of Dermatologists, Venereologists and Leprologists, says people lack awareness of how topical applications can enter the bloodstream. “People are obsessed with fair skin. We have observed a rise in the number of people buying steroid creams that are easily available over the counter and applying them to their faces. Such steroid-based applications and creams containing heavy metals such as mercury can damage your kidneys easily. The government needs to bring in some mechanisms to control this,” he says. A rise in the number of teenagers relying on spurious beauty products has forced the Keralam Drugs Control department to launch awareness campaigns targeting students in Classes XI and XII, an age group particularly vulnerable to online campaigns. Frequent inspections are carried out in marketplaces to confiscate spurious cosmetics. State Drugs Controller K. Sujith Kumar says raising awareness about such spurious cosmetic products is the only way forward. “We have seized cosmetics that have high mercury levels from offline markets. But there is no way to track or regulate online marketplaces,” he says.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Prolonged use of such creams can lead to kidney damage, says former secretary of the Nephrology Association of Kerala, Jayant Thomas Mathew, who has come across a few cases of kidney disorders among users. The condition could be detected early because the patients were aware of the symptoms.

articles.title: Clamour to reintroduce adequate number of air-conditioned buses in Kochi grows louder
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: While many of the AC buses were diverted to long-distance routes, the KSRTC had to scrap most of its non-AC low-floor counterparts due to improper upkeep

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The void created by the withdrawal of the KSRTC’s fleet of over 50 Volvo air-conditioned low-floor city buses from the city during the past decade has intensified the demand to reintroduce an adequate number of AC buses. While many of the AC buses were diverted to long-distance routes, the KSRTC had to scrap most of its non-AC low-floor counterparts due to improper upkeep. Barring the 15 AC feeder buses operated by Kochi Metro Rail Limited from select metro stations, such services are absent in the rest of Kochi and in suburban towns. Former Mayor K.J. Sohan, who is an avid votary of public transport buses, cited the need for AC buses of different sizes to operate services along both arterial and side roads, with smaller buses deployed along narrower byroads. “The AC low-floor buses were diverted to long-distance and inter-district routes, although they were designed exclusively for city use. With the commissioning of the Kochi metro in 2017, they would have come in handy to operate feeder trips from different parts of the city and its immediate suburbs to metro stations in the Aluva-M.G. Road-Thripunithura corridor. Then State government refused to hand over the buses to the Kochi Corporation, although councillors staged a dharna at the KSRTC bus station demanding it. On its part, the National Transportation Planning and Research Centre (NATPAC) conducted a study of potential routes for the civic body,” he said. With worsening congestion, reckless driving by private buses causing accidents, and frequent violent incidents involving bus crew, it is high time the State government permitted both the KSRTC and private bus operators to introduce AC buses in the city. A higher fare structure could be readied for this. Apart from intra-city routes that have limited or no bus connectivity, there is immense potential to roll out direct AC bus services from Fort Kochi to Thripunithura and Kakkanad, through the Kundannur Bridge-Vytilla stretch. Such comfortable buses could also be operated in the Chellanam-Munambam densely populated corridor since adequate public transport creates access to opportunities, he added. Echoing a similar view, Bijulal Ram, a former motor vehicle inspector, said a good share of traffic problems and accidents in cities like Kochi could be mitigated if an adequate number of passenger-friendly buses and AC city buses are introduced. “Care must be taken so that they adhere to the AIS-052 bus body code and have pneumatic doors. To top it all, digital fare collection and passenger information system will help wean away commuters from two-wheelers and cars to buses. This will in turn curb undue incidents between passengers and bus crew over fare collection,” he said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Yet another public transport enthusiast, Santosh Thannikkat, cited the need for a comprehensive plan to augment the public transport bus network in the city and the quality of service it offers. “It is also time buses that now operate mostly along arterial roads and even beneath the metro corridor extend their operations to other less connected corridors,” he said.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #10 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Clamour to reintroduce adequate number of air-conditioned buses in Kochi grows louder

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 01:37:35 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: While many of the AC buses were diverted to long-distance routes, the KSRTC had to scrap most of its non-AC low-floor counterparts due to improper upkeep

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The void created by the withdrawal of the KSRTC’s fleet of over 50 Volvo air-conditioned low-floor city buses from the city during the past decade has intensified the demand to reintroduce an adequate number of AC buses. While many of the AC buses were diverted to long-distance routes, the KSRTC had to scrap most of its non-AC low-floor counterparts due to improper upkeep. Barring the 15 AC feeder buses operated by Kochi Metro Rail Limited from select metro stations, such services are absent in the rest of Kochi and in suburban towns. Former Mayor K.J. Sohan, who is an avid votary of public transport buses, cited the need for AC buses of different sizes to operate services along both arterial and side roads, with smaller buses deployed along narrower byroads. “The AC low-floor buses were diverted to long-distance and inter-district routes, although they were designed exclusively for city use. With the commissioning of the Kochi metro in 2017, they would have come in handy to operate feeder trips from different parts of the city and its immediate suburbs to metro stations in the Aluva-M.G. Road-Thripunithura corridor. Then State government refused to hand over the buses to the Kochi Corporation, although councillors staged a dharna at the KSRTC bus station demanding it. On its part, the National Transportation Planning and Research Centre (NATPAC) conducted a study of potential routes for the civic body,” he said. With worsening congestion, reckless driving by private buses causing accidents, and frequent violent incidents involving bus crew, it is high time the State government permitted both the KSRTC and private bus operators to introduce AC buses in the city. A higher fare structure could be readied for this. Apart from intra-city routes that have limited or no bus connectivity, there is immense potential to roll out direct AC bus services from Fort Kochi to Thripunithura and Kakkanad, through the Kundannur Bridge-Vytilla stretch. Such comfortable buses could also be operated in the Chellanam-Munambam densely populated corridor since adequate public transport creates access to opportunities, he added. Echoing a similar view, Bijulal Ram, a former motor vehicle inspector, said a good share of traffic problems and accidents in cities like Kochi could be mitigated if an adequate number of passenger-friendly buses and AC city buses are introduced. “Care must be taken so that they adhere to the AIS-052 bus body code and have pneumatic doors. To top it all, digital fare collection and passenger information system will help wean away commuters from two-wheelers and cars to buses. This will in turn curb undue incidents between passengers and bus crew over fare collection,” he said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Yet another public transport enthusiast, Santosh Thannikkat, cited the need for a comprehensive plan to augment the public transport bus network in the city and the quality of service it offers. “It is also time buses that now operate mostly along arterial roads and even beneath the metro corridor extend their operations to other less connected corridors,” he said.

articles.title: Bahrain says Iran struck industrial site as tankers hit in Hormuz
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: “Our position is clear: as long as Iran's demands are not met, the discussion on the Strait of Hormuz and its opening is pointless,” Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Bahrain accused Iran of striking a civilian industrial facility on Saturday (November 21, 2026), causing a fire and damage but no casualties, while two tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz. "As a result of the heinous Iranian aggression, a civilian industrial facility was targeted, causing a fire at the site. Civil Defence is working to bring the fire under control," the Interior Ministry said on X, without specifying the location. Residents told AFP they saw smoke rising over Sitra Island, on Bahrain's east coast, home to several industrial sites including a refinery run by state oil company Bapco. Iran's Fars news agency reported the Revolutionary Guards had "attacked two U.S. bases, Sheikh Isa and Juffair, on the island of Bahrain in response to the illegal actions of the United States". The attacks came as two tankers were struck in the Strait of Hormuz, which has become the focus of the stalemated conflict, with Iran continuing in its efforts to blockade the strategic shipping line. The U.S. military, meanwhile, has been escorting ships through the strategic strait, which carried one-fifth of the world's oil before the war, and maintains its own counterblockade of Iranian ports. Iranian deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said on Saturday (November 21, 2026) that a Qatari delegation visited Tehran the previous evening and "held two hours of talks", without providing details. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said: "The ongoing talks in the region must be given a chance, and the blockade must be lifted rationally." "Our position is clear: as long as Iran's demands are not met, the discussion on the Strait of Hormuz and its opening is pointless," he said, quoted by state TV.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Iran's demands include ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing Iranian assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending the U.S. counter-blockade of Iranian ports.

📰 Bahrain says Iran struck industrial site as tankers hit in Hormuz

🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: “Our position is clear: as long as Iran's demands are not met, the discussion on the Strait of Hormuz and its opening is pointless,” Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Bahrain accused Iran of striking a civilian industrial facility on Saturday (November 21, 2026), causing a fire and damage but no casualties, while two tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz. "As a result of the heinous Iranian aggression, a civilian industrial facility was targeted, causing a fire at the site. Civil Defence is working to bring the fire under control," the Interior Ministry said on X, without specifying the location. Residents told AFP they saw smoke rising over Sitra Island, on Bahrain's east coast, home to several industrial sites including a refinery run by state oil company Bapco. Iran's Fars news agency reported the Revolutionary Guards had "attacked two U.S. bases, Sheikh Isa and Juffair, on the island of Bahrain in response to the illegal actions of the United States". The attacks came as two tankers were struck in the Strait of Hormuz, which has become the focus of the stalemated conflict, with Iran continuing in its efforts to blockade the strategic shipping line. The U.S. military, meanwhile, has been escorting ships through the strategic strait, which carried one-fifth of the world's oil before the war, and maintains its own counterblockade of Iranian ports. Iranian deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said on Saturday (November 21, 2026) that a Qatari delegation visited Tehran the previous evening and "held two hours of talks", without providing details. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said: "The ongoing talks in the region must be given a chance, and the blockade must be lifted rationally." "Our position is clear: as long as Iran's demands are not met, the discussion on the Strait of Hormuz and its opening is pointless," he said, quoted by state TV.

Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Bahrain accused Iran of striking a civilian industrial facility on Saturday (November 21, 2026), causing a fire and damage but no casualties, while two tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz. "As a result of the heinous Iranian aggression, a civilian industrial facility was targeted, causing a fire at the site. Civil Defence is working to bring the fire under control," the Interior Ministry said on X, without specifying the location. Residents told AFP they saw smoke rising over Sitra Island, on Bahrain's east coast, home to several industrial sites including a refinery run by state oil company Bapco. Iran's Fars news agency reported the Revolutionary Guards had "attacked two U.S. bases, Sheikh Isa and Juffair, on the island of Bahrain in response to the illegal actions of the United States". The U.S. military, meanwhile, has been escorting ships through the strategic strait, which carried one-fifth of the world's oil before the war, and maintains its own counterblockade of Iranian ports. Iranian deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said on Saturday (November 21, 2026) that a Qatari delegation visited Tehran the previous evening and "held two hours of talks", without providing details. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said: "The ongoing talks in the region must be given a chance, and the blockade must be lifted rationally." articles.title: Thousands march in Lisbon as living costs fuel anger
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The protest ⁠followed weeks of unrest, including housing activists’ tent camps in ⁠Lisbon and Porto, and comes amid a broader wave of demonstrations across Europe over ‌living costs and housing

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Thousands of people marched through central Lisbon on ​Saturday (November 21, 2026) despite heavy rain to protest against soaring living ‌costs, a deepening housing crisis and low wages. Organiser ​CGTP, Portugal’s largest trade union federation, called ⁠for higher wages and pensions, lower prices for essential goods and services, and measures to curb housing costs. The ‌CGTP said turnout reached “many thousands” as protesters carrying umbrellas and wearing hooded ponchos marched ‌along two of Lisbon’s main avenues. Police ‌did ⁠not provide an estimate. “We work more, we ⁠have more expenses and we don’t have money for day-to-day life,” said Manuel Gomes, 44, a factory worker, arguing that the ​centre-right government’s policies ‌had made matters worse. Protestors demanding affordable housing and carrying a banner with the words "Fight for our future, not in their wars" walks past a Christmas market in downtown Lisbon, on November 21, 2026. | Photo Credit: AP “Our wages are low, diesel and gasoline prices keep going up, and so do housing costs and everything else. We have ‌to change this,” Gomes said. Portugal’s average annual earnings ​in 2025 were 37% below the European Union average, according to Eurostat. Inflation ⁠hit 3.8% in October, driven by food and energy prices amid continuing tensions in the Middle East. Portugal is ‌also grappling with one of Europe’s most severe housing affordability crises. House prices have more than doubled since 2017, while rents for new leases have nearly doubled, hitting younger people particularly hard. Luis Russo (66), a retired IT technician, said he ‌was demonstrating to demand “higher wages and pensions and against speculation in ​the rental market”, accusing the government of serving “big interests” rather than ordinary people.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The protest ⁠followed weeks of unrest, including housing activists’ tent camps in ⁠Lisbon and Porto, and comes amid a broader wave of demonstrations across Europe over ‌living costs and housing. Turnout at largely peaceful protests in France on Saturday was lower than ​in previous weeks.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #24 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Thousands march in Lisbon as living costs fuel anger

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 06:58:36 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The protest ⁠followed weeks of unrest, including housing activists’ tent camps in ⁠Lisbon and Porto, and comes amid a broader wave of demonstrations across Europe over ‌living costs and housing

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Thousands of people marched through central Lisbon on ​Saturday (November 21, 2026) despite heavy rain to protest against soaring living ‌costs, a deepening housing crisis and low wages. Organiser ​CGTP, Portugal’s largest trade union federation, called ⁠for higher wages and pensions, lower prices for essential goods and services, and measures to curb housing costs. The ‌CGTP said turnout reached “many thousands” as protesters carrying umbrellas and wearing hooded ponchos marched ‌along two of Lisbon’s main avenues. Police ‌did ⁠not provide an estimate. “We work more, we ⁠have more expenses and we don’t have money for day-to-day life,” said Manuel Gomes, 44, a factory worker, arguing that the ​centre-right government’s policies ‌had made matters worse. Protestors demanding affordable housing and carrying a banner with the words "Fight for our future, not in their wars" walks past a Christmas market in downtown Lisbon, on November 21, 2026. | Photo Credit: AP “Our wages are low, diesel and gasoline prices keep going up, and so do housing costs and everything else. We have ‌to change this,” Gomes said. Portugal’s average annual earnings ​in 2025 were 37% below the European Union average, according to Eurostat. Inflation ⁠hit 3.8% in October, driven by food and energy prices amid continuing tensions in the Middle East. Portugal is ‌also grappling with one of Europe’s most severe housing affordability crises. House prices have more than doubled since 2017, while rents for new leases have nearly doubled, hitting younger people particularly hard. Luis Russo (66), a retired IT technician, said he ‌was demonstrating to demand “higher wages and pensions and against speculation in ​the rental market”, accusing the government of serving “big interests” rather than ordinary people.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The protest ⁠followed weeks of unrest, including housing activists’ tent camps in ⁠Lisbon and Porto, and comes amid a broader wave of demonstrations across Europe over ‌living costs and housing. Turnout at largely peaceful protests in France on Saturday was lower than ​in previous weeks.

A. The protest ⁠followed weeks of unrest, including housing activists’ tent camps in ⁠Lisbon and Porto, and comes amid a broader wave of demonstrations...

✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. articles.title: Three cyclones in three weeks: What’s happening in the Bay of Bengal? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Such a frequency is uncommon but not unique this year; there were around 1.8 cyclones a year in the post-monsoon period in 1982-2022, with the average increasing after 2001

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The story so far: Within 23 days this year, three cyclones formed over the Bay of Bengal. Of them, Cyclone Arnab made landfall near Yanam on the Andhra Pradesh coast on October 28 and Murasu on November 3 near Ongole. Cyclone Akvan formed on November 16 and made landfall near Gopalpur in Odisha on Friday morning (November 20, 2026). A cyclone requires an atmospheric disturbance, abundant moisture, and favourable winds. The Bay has two main cyclone seasons, April-May and October-December. During the southwest monsoon, strong winds blowing in different directions at different altitudes suppress cyclone formation. But as the monsoon withdraws, the vertical wind shear weakens even as the waters remain warm, creating more favourable conditions.

📰 Three cyclones in three weeks: What’s happening in the Bay of Bengal? | Explained

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 10:48:02 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

Of them, Cyclone Arnab made landfall near Yanam on the Andhra Pradesh coast on October 28 and Murasu on November 3 near Ongole. Cyclone Akvan formed on November 16 and made landfall near Gopalpur in Odisha on Friday morning (November 20, 2026). A cyclone requires an atmospheric disturbance, abundant moisture, and favourable winds. The Bay has two main cyclone seasons, April-May and October-December. During the southwest monsoon, strong winds blowing in different directions at different altitudes suppress cyclone formation. But as the monsoon withdraws, the vertical wind shear weakens even as the waters remain warm, creating more favourable conditions.

articles.title: FUJIFILM’s Spectrum tour enthrals visual creators, photography enthusiasts in Bengaluru
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The three-day event featured specialised experience zones focusing on distinct creative mediums, including vlogging, cinematography, street photography and portraiture

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A multi-city FUJIFILM India Spectrum Tour, bringing together of the brand’s entire range of imaging solutions from Instax cameras, digital cameras and lenses, concluded in Bengaluru recently. The three-day event, held at the Venkatappa Art Gallery, featured specialised experience zones focusing on distinct creative mediums, including vlogging, cinematography, street photography and portraiture, attracted a large number of people. Company executives highlighted the regional strategy behind selecting the city for this segment of the tour. "We are excited to connect with the city’s vibrant imaging community. Through Spectrum, we aim to bring our imaging heritage and cutting-edge technology closer to creators,"’ said Koji Wada, managing director of FUJIFILM India. The tour was in Bengaluru after Gurugram and Ahmedabad, attracting local photography enthusiasts, visual creators and students who prefer to have a hands-on experience with FUJIFILM product ranges. A central component involved educational masterclasses led by established industry practitioners. Photographers including Sudhir Ramachandran and Prashant Godbole were among the participants. Sessions covered architectural, landscape, and street photography. Other sessions led by technical experts covered niche genres such as astrophotography, wildlife documentation, and sports imaging. The event consolidated the company’s various product categories, including mirrorless camera systems, instant photography devices, and optical tools, under a unified interactive environment.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Arun Babu, associate director of the Imaging Solutions Division at FUJIFILM India, said, “In Bengaluru, through hands-on experiences, we encouraged visitors to experiment with our imaging solutions and discover new ways to express their creativity.”

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #9 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 FUJIFILM’s Spectrum tour enthrals visual creators, photography enthusiasts in Bengaluru

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 07:35:04 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The three-day event featured specialised experience zones focusing on distinct creative mediums, including vlogging, cinematography, street photography and portraiture

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A multi-city FUJIFILM India Spectrum Tour, bringing together of the brand’s entire range of imaging solutions from Instax cameras, digital cameras and lenses, concluded in Bengaluru recently. The three-day event, held at the Venkatappa Art Gallery, featured specialised experience zones focusing on distinct creative mediums, including vlogging, cinematography, street photography and portraiture, attracted a large number of people. Company executives highlighted the regional strategy behind selecting the city for this segment of the tour. "We are excited to connect with the city’s vibrant imaging community. Through Spectrum, we aim to bring our imaging heritage and cutting-edge technology closer to creators,"’ said Koji Wada, managing director of FUJIFILM India. The tour was in Bengaluru after Gurugram and Ahmedabad, attracting local photography enthusiasts, visual creators and students who prefer to have a hands-on experience with FUJIFILM product ranges. A central component involved educational masterclasses led by established industry practitioners. Photographers including Sudhir Ramachandran and Prashant Godbole were among the participants. Sessions covered architectural, landscape, and street photography. Other sessions led by technical experts covered niche genres such as astrophotography, wildlife documentation, and sports imaging. The event consolidated the company’s various product categories, including mirrorless camera systems, instant photography devices, and optical tools, under a unified interactive environment.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Arun Babu, associate director of the Imaging Solutions Division at FUJIFILM India, said, “In Bengaluru, through hands-on experiences, we encouraged visitors to experiment with our imaging solutions and discover new ways to express their creativity.”

articles.title: Kashmir’s famed saffron fields have been used as dumping grounds for three years: Mehbooba Mufti
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The former Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister says nearly 2,000 kanals of land have been damaged, threatening the livelihoods of 150 families; the NGT has directed a panel to inspect the site and recommend action

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Kashmir’s prized saffron fields in Pampore, Pulwama, have been used as a municipal dumping ground for the past three years, former Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) president Mehbooba Mufti said on Saturday (November 21, 2026). “For the past three years, Pampore’s priceless saffron fields have been used as a municipal dumping ground. Nearly 2,000 kanals were damaged, 150 families’ livelihoods threatened, and rats and rodents destroying crops. This is an outrageous assault on Kashmir’s saffron heritage. Such administrative negligence is indefensible. Our saffron fields are not dumping sites. They must be protected not poisoned,” Ms. Mufti said. Her statement came days after the National Green Tribunal (NGT) highlighted the “unscientific dumping of municipal solid waste in Patalbagh” in Pampore. The NGT bench, comprising chairperson Justice Prakash Shrivastava and expert member Dr. Afroz Alam, directed the constitution of a joint committee “to conduct an on-site inspection and submit a comprehensive factual and action-taken report within eight weeks”. It asked the Deputy Commissioner, Pulwama, to coordinate the inspection and facilitate the committee’s visit to the dumping site. Representatives of the Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology of Kashmir (SKUAST-K), the Regional Director of the Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, and a nominee of the Member Secretary, Jammu and Kashmir Pollution Control Committee, will be members of the committee.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The committee will examine the extent of pollution caused by the waste dumping, assess its impact on saffron cultivation spread over approximately 2,000 kanals of land and adjoining areas, and ascertain whether the dumping site has obtained the requisite statutory clearances, officials said

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #10 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Kashmir’s famed saffron fields have been used as dumping grounds for three years: Mehbooba Mufti

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 07:08:25 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The former Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister says nearly 2,000 kanals of land have been damaged, threatening the livelihoods of 150 families; the NGT has directed a panel to inspect the site and recommend action

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Kashmir’s prized saffron fields in Pampore, Pulwama, have been used as a municipal dumping ground for the past three years, former Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) president Mehbooba Mufti said on Saturday (November 21, 2026). “For the past three years, Pampore’s priceless saffron fields have been used as a municipal dumping ground. Nearly 2,000 kanals were damaged, 150 families’ livelihoods threatened, and rats and rodents destroying crops. This is an outrageous assault on Kashmir’s saffron heritage. Such administrative negligence is indefensible. Our saffron fields are not dumping sites. They must be protected not poisoned,” Ms. Mufti said. Her statement came days after the National Green Tribunal (NGT) highlighted the “unscientific dumping of municipal solid waste in Patalbagh” in Pampore. The NGT bench, comprising chairperson Justice Prakash Shrivastava and expert member Dr. Afroz Alam, directed the constitution of a joint committee “to conduct an on-site inspection and submit a comprehensive factual and action-taken report within eight weeks”. It asked the Deputy Commissioner, Pulwama, to coordinate the inspection and facilitate the committee’s visit to the dumping site. Representatives of the Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology of Kashmir (SKUAST-K), the Regional Director of the Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, and a nominee of the Member Secretary, Jammu and Kashmir Pollution Control Committee, will be members of the committee.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The committee will examine the extent of pollution caused by the waste dumping, assess its impact on saffron cultivation spread over approximately 2,000 kanals of land and adjoining areas, and ascertain whether the dumping site has obtained the requisite statutory clearances, officials said

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Environmental (Adjective)
पर्यावरण, प्रकृति और हमारे पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र (Ecosystem) से संबंधित।
✓ Syn: Ecological, Biospheric, Natural  |  ✖ Ant: Industrial, Polluting, Synthetic
Constitutional (Adjective)
संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप।
✓ Syn: Statutory, Legitimate, Lawful  |  ✖ Ant: Unconstitutional, Illegal, Arbitrary
Administrative (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Administrative' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Comprehensive (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Comprehensive' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile

A. The former Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister says nearly 2,000 kanals of land have been damaged, threatening the livelihoods of 150 families; the NGT...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Kashmir’s famed saffron fields have been used as' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Kashmir’s famed saffron fields have been used' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Kashmir’s famed saffron fields have been used' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The former Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister says nearly 2,000 kanals of land have been damaged, threatening the livelihoods of 150 families; the NGT..." (Hinglish Arth: जम्मू-कश्मीर के पूर्व मुख्यमंत्री का कहना है कि लगभग 2,000 कनाल भूमि क्षतिग्रस्त हो गई है, जिससे 150 परिवारों की आजीविका खतरे में पड़ गई है; एनजीटी ने एक पैनल को साइट का निरीक्षण करने और कार्रवाई की सिफारिश करने का निर्देश दिया है)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Kashmir’s famed saffron fields have been used as dumping grounds for three years: Mehbooba Mufti"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. The committee will examine the extent of pollution caused by the waste dumping, assess its impact on saffron cultivation spread over approximately...
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "The committee will examine the extent of pollution caused by the waste dumping, assess its impact on saffron cultivation spread over approximately..." fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The ICJ ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya is significant, but refugees continue to face the threat of violence and restrictions on humanitarian access, as the situation in their homeland remains precarious

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: T he International Court of Justice (ICJ), the UN’s top court, on November 19, ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya minority during the military’s 2017 clearance operations in Rakhine State. This was the first time the world court held a country responsible for committing genocide. The Rohingya, a predominantly Muslim ethnic minority, have faced decades of systematic discrimination in the Southeast Asian country, including the denial of citizenship, restrictions on movement and access to education, healthcare and livelihoods. In August 2017, a military crackdown involving mass killings, sexual violence, and the burning of villages forced more than 7,40,000 Rohingya to flee to neighbouring Bangladesh. They joined earlier waves of refugees who had escaped persecution. Nearly 1.2 million Rohingya now live in overcrowded camps in Bangladesh’s Cox’s Bazar. Rohingya refugees in other countries such as India, Malaysia and Indonesia also face uncertain legal status, discrimination, detention and the threat of deportation. Meanwhile, their homeland remains deeply troubled. Rakhine State has been engulfed in fighting between Myanmar’s military and the Arakan Army, a rebel group which now controls much of the region. The Rohingya, many of whom remain internally displaced, face renewed insecurity, restrictions on humanitarian access and the threat of violence from competing armed forces. And for the refugees, a return to their homeland is neither desirable nor practical. While the ICJ verdict is significant and sets a strong precedent, it is unlikely to ease the suffering of the Rohingya. Seeking safe harbour: The refugees being transported by a wooden boat to a temporary shelter in Krueng Raya, Aceh Besar, Indonesia, on April 8, 2013. The port has been a major landing point and temporary shelter site over the years. Fleeing the inferno: Rohingya refugees flee as fires in Myanmar, allegedly started by the military, burn in the background, near Bangladesh in 2017. Paddling into exile: Rohingya refugees cross the Naf River on an improvised raft to reach Bangladesh on November 12, 2017. Longing for justice: Rohingya refugees watch the live announcement of the verdict in a genocide case against Myanmar on November 19, 2026

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The agony of loss: Hamida, a Rohingya refugee, weeps as she holds her 40-day-old son, who died after their boat capsized before reaching the shore in Teknaf, Bangladesh, on September 14, 2017.
