articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: Bahrain said two people were wounded in an attack on “a civilian industrial site”, while Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said they targeted U.S. air defence systems.
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Bahrain on Sunday (November 22, 2026) said two people were wounded in an Iranian attack on Saturday (November 21, 2026) against “a civilian industrial site” in the kingdom, which has repeatedly come under attack in recent days. Iran’s Revolutionary Guards have repeatedly said they targeted U.S. facilities in Bahrain, where Iranian strikes resumed on November 13 after a lull since early September. “In the wake of the criminal Iranian attacks suffered yesterday (Saturday) by the Kingdom of Bahrain... a Bahraini national with a disability was wounded,” Bahrain’s Interior Ministry said on X. “His condition is stable. A Pakistani resident was also wounded and is in critical condition. Both are being treated in hospital.” Two residents told AFP they had seen smoke rising above Sitra Island, east of Manama, which hosts several industrial facilities, including a refinery operated by the state-owned oil company Bapco. In a statement carried by Iranian state media on Saturday evening, the Revolutionary Guards said they had attacked with missiles and drones U.S. Patriot air defence systems at the Al-Riffa and Awali bases in Bahrain, in response to the “continued violations of the airspace” of the Islamic Republic. Tehran said on Saturday it had intercepted a U.S. drone targeting Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, a strategic maritime corridor at the heart of the war in West Asia. Bahrain’s powerful neighbour Saudi Arabia on Sunday lambasted Tehran for its continued “brutal aggression” against Gulf countries. In a statement published on X, the Saudi Foreign Ministry expressed “the strongest condemnation and denunciation by the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia of the criminal Iranian attacks against a civilian industrial facility in the brotherly Kingdom of Bahrain”. Saudi Arabia also announced early on Sunday that it had intercepted a ballistic missile fired by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis in the west of the kingdom. The region is home to key energy infrastructure, including the oil terminal at the port of Yanbu, as well as the Jizan refinery, located in the far southwest of the country, near the border with Yemen.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Saudi Arabia has been battling a surge in attacks since fighting reignited in neighbouring Yemen’s civil war this summer, the latest front in the West Asia war.

articles.title: COP 31 talks fail as EU, others reject any climate deal without language on a fossil fuel phase-out
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: EU, Panama among about 130 parties that refuse to accept COP President’s consensus cover text, alleges that it “greenwashes” fossil fuels; India, China, Saudi Arabia are on the other side of the divide

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A standoff on a fossil fuel phase-out prevented countries at COP 31, the United Nations climate talks in Antalya, Turkiye, from achieving any consensus agreement on future climate action on Sunday (November 22, 2026), despite the conference running a record 48 hours into overtime. The European Union led objections to COP 31 President Murat Kurum’s consensus cover text that failed to include any explicit language about moving away from fossil fuels. The EU’s stance was reportedly supported by about 130 countries. On the other side of the divide, India is among the nations that supported the proposed cover text, as they want to keep using fossil fuels for the foreseeable future, with Environment Minister Bhupendra Yadav stressing that “climate ambition must go hand in hand with means of implementation.” “We express profound disappointment with the final draft COP31 cover decision or Antalya Pact. At a point where the world urgently needs action to avert disastrous levels of global warming, the draft cover decision falls well short,” Ireland’s Climate Minister Darragh O’Brien said, speaking on behalf of the EU. “We will not endorse a decision that does not respond to the science, that disregards the implementation gap, and that actually risks deepening the chasm between global commitments and the action required to correct the overshoot and bring 1.5 degrees back to within reach… We will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuel,” he added. A cover text is an overarching political decision that frames the outcome of a climate conference rather than settling any single agenda item. It is usually finalised last, and like every outcome, it needs the consensus of all parties. Panama also formally objected to the text, saying that as a country battling droughts and other perilous impacts of climate change, the lack of any commitment to keep the rise in temperatures below 1.5 degrees C with firm action on phasing out fossil fuels was “a setback”. “Panama cannot support this decision. One, because it repeats previously agreed commitments without closing the gap between reality and what science demands. Two, because it weighs too much upon technologies such as CCUS [carbon capture utilisation and storage] instead of calling for deep changes, and three, because it weakens language agreed in previous decisions. This is a setback, a rollback,” said Ana Aguilar, Panama’s chief climate negotiator. On the other side, Saudi Arabia, China, and India are among the countries that are against explicit language on fossil fuel and expressed comfort with the way the cover text language was framed, while also expressing misgivings about the lack of clarity on adaptation finance. The countries are part of the Like Minded Developing Countries (LMDC) coalition, who are insistent on the use of fossil fuel in the foreseeable future to further their economies, but have also significantly deployed renewable energy.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Indian Environment Minister Bhupendra Yadav said that India’s voice had shaped the draft COP 31 outcome, especially on food security, livelihoods, and cultural practices recognised in action on methane. However, in a post on X, he emphasised that “climate ambition must go hand in hand with means of implementation. Energy transitions must be nationally determined, just and equitable, backed by finance, technology and capacity-building for developing countries.”

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #23 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 COP 31 talks fail as EU, others reject any climate deal without language on a fossil fuel phase-out

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 09:53:23 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: EU, Panama among about 130 parties that refuse to accept COP President’s consensus cover text, alleges that it “greenwashes” fossil fuels; India, China, Saudi Arabia are on the other side of the divide

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A standoff on a fossil fuel phase-out prevented countries at COP 31, the United Nations climate talks in Antalya, Turkiye, from achieving any consensus agreement on future climate action on Sunday (November 22, 2026), despite the conference running a record 48 hours into overtime. The European Union led objections to COP 31 President Murat Kurum’s consensus cover text that failed to include any explicit language about moving away from fossil fuels. The EU’s stance was reportedly supported by about 130 countries. On the other side of the divide, India is among the nations that supported the proposed cover text, as they want to keep using fossil fuels for the foreseeable future, with Environment Minister Bhupendra Yadav stressing that “climate ambition must go hand in hand with means of implementation.” “We express profound disappointment with the final draft COP31 cover decision or Antalya Pact. At a point where the world urgently needs action to avert disastrous levels of global warming, the draft cover decision falls well short,” Ireland’s Climate Minister Darragh O’Brien said, speaking on behalf of the EU. “We will not endorse a decision that does not respond to the science, that disregards the implementation gap, and that actually risks deepening the chasm between global commitments and the action required to correct the overshoot and bring 1.5 degrees back to within reach… We will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuel,” he added. A cover text is an overarching political decision that frames the outcome of a climate conference rather than settling any single agenda item. It is usually finalised last, and like every outcome, it needs the consensus of all parties. Panama also formally objected to the text, saying that as a country battling droughts and other perilous impacts of climate change, the lack of any commitment to keep the rise in temperatures below 1.5 degrees C with firm action on phasing out fossil fuels was “a setback”. “Panama cannot support this decision. One, because it repeats previously agreed commitments without closing the gap between reality and what science demands. Two, because it weighs too much upon technologies such as CCUS [carbon capture utilisation and storage] instead of calling for deep changes, and three, because it weakens language agreed in previous decisions. This is a setback, a rollback,” said Ana Aguilar, Panama’s chief climate negotiator. On the other side, Saudi Arabia, China, and India are among the countries that are against explicit language on fossil fuel and expressed comfort with the way the cover text language was framed, while also expressing misgivings about the lack of clarity on adaptation finance. The countries are part of the Like Minded Developing Countries (LMDC) coalition, who are insistent on the use of fossil fuel in the foreseeable future to further their economies, but have also significantly deployed renewable energy.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Indian Environment Minister Bhupendra Yadav said that India’s voice had shaped the draft COP 31 outcome, especially on food security, livelihoods, and cultural practices recognised in action on methane. However, in a post on X, he emphasised that “climate ambition must go hand in hand with means of implementation. Energy transitions must be nationally determined, just and equitable, backed by finance, technology and capacity-building for developing countries.”

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Environmental (Adjective)
पर्यावरण, प्रकृति और हमारे पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र (Ecosystem) से संबंधित।
✓ Syn: Ecological, Biospheric, Natural  |  ✖ Ant: Industrial, Polluting, Synthetic
Implementation (Noun)
क्रियान्वयन / ज़मीनी स्तर पर लागू करना — किसी योजना या फैसले को असलियत में पूरा करना।
✓ Syn: Execution, Enforcement, Fulfillment  |  ✖ Ant: Abandonment, Neglect, Cancellation
Disappointment (Adjective)
निराशा — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Disappointment' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Utilisation (Noun)
उपयोग — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Utilisation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🌐 International & Geopolitics passage on "COP 31 talks fail as EU, others reject any climate deal without language on a fossil fuel phase-out", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. EU, Panama among about 130 parties that refuse to accept COP President’s consensus cover text, alleges that it “greenwashes” fossil fuels; India,...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'COP 31 talks fail as EU, others reject any clima' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'COP 31 talks fail as EU, others reject any cl' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'COP 31 talks fail as EU, others reject any cl' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "EU, Panama among about 130 parties that refuse to accept COP President’s consensus cover text, alleges that it “greenwashes” fossil fuels; India,..." (Hinglish Arth: यूरोपीय संघ, पनामा सहित लगभग 130 पार्टियों ने सीओपी अध्यक्ष के सर्वसम्मति कवर पाठ को स्वीकार करने से इनकार कर दिया, उनका आरोप है कि यह जीवाश्म ईंधन को "ग्रीनवॉश" करता है; भारत, चीन, सऊदी अरब विभाजन के दूसरी तरफ हैं)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "COP 31 talks fail as EU, others reject any climate deal without language on a fossil fuel phase-out"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Energy transitions must be nationally determined, just and equitable, backed by finance, technology and capacity-building for developing countries.”.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Energy transitions must be nationally determined, just and equitable, backed by finance, technology and capacity-building for developing countries.”." (Hinglish Arth: विकासशील देशों के लिए ऊर्जा परिवर्तन राष्ट्रीय स्तर पर निर्धारित, न्यायसंगत और वित्त, प्रौद्योगिकी और क्षमता-निर्माण द्वारा समर्थित होना चाहिए।)

articles.title: Giving India’s first practising woman doctor her due: Kadambini Ganguly​
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Kadambini Ganguly broke barriers to become one of India’s first women physicians to practise Western medicine

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: As far as trailblazers go, Kadambini Ganguly will figure right on top of several lists. She was a pioneering woman physician, the first to practise successfully in India, a gynaecologist and a social reformer who, equally efficiently, managed a large family as well. The story of Kadambini Ganguly is one of extraordinary achievement, and if told widely, will continue to inspire the young women of today.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In a profile published in Cureus in 2024, the authors point to the influence of the progressive Bramho Samaj movement, initiated by Raja Ram Mohan Roy, that helped Kadambini emerge from the shackles of conservative orthodoxy that might have stiffled her immense talent. “This environment, which championed the values of education and gender equality, contributed significantly to shaping her exemplary career and lifelong dedication to social justice,” the article reads. Records of her life acknowledge that she was partly recognised during her lifetime, but also mercilessly criticised and defamed for being a progressive, working woman. The full recognition of her contributions in medicine and the social sector came much later, only in recent decades.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #28 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Giving India’s first practising woman doctor her due: Kadambini Ganguly​

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 10:15:27 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Kadambini Ganguly broke barriers to become one of India’s first women physicians to practise Western medicine

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: As far as trailblazers go, Kadambini Ganguly will figure right on top of several lists. She was a pioneering woman physician, the first to practise successfully in India, a gynaecologist and a social reformer who, equally efficiently, managed a large family as well. The story of Kadambini Ganguly is one of extraordinary achievement, and if told widely, will continue to inspire the young women of today.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In a profile published in Cureus in 2024, the authors point to the influence of the progressive Bramho Samaj movement, initiated by Raja Ram Mohan Roy, that helped Kadambini emerge from the shackles of conservative orthodoxy that might have stiffled her immense talent. “This environment, which championed the values of education and gender equality, contributed significantly to shaping her exemplary career and lifelong dedication to social justice,” the article reads. Records of her life acknowledge that she was partly recognised during her lifetime, but also mercilessly criticised and defamed for being a progressive, working woman. The full recognition of her contributions in medicine and the social sector came much later, only in recent decades.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Environmental (Adjective)
पर्यावरण, प्रकृति और हमारे पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र (Ecosystem) से संबंधित।
✓ Syn: Ecological, Biospheric, Natural  |  ✖ Ant: Industrial, Polluting, Synthetic
Conservative (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Conservative' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Achievement (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Achievement' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Progressive (Adjective)
प्रगतिशील — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Progressive' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🚀 Science, Tech & Environment passage on "Giving India’s first practising woman doctor her due: Kadambini Ganguly​", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Kadambini Ganguly broke barriers to become one of India’s first women physicians to practise Western medicine.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Giving India’s first practising woman doctor her' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Giving India’s first practising woman doctor ' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Giving India’s first practising woman doctor ' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Kadambini Ganguly broke barriers to become one of India’s first women physicians to practise Western medicine." (Hinglish Arth: कादम्बिनी गांगुली ने बाधाओं को तोड़ते हुए पश्चिमी चिकित्सा का अभ्यास करने वाली भारत की पहली महिला चिकित्सकों में से एक बन गईं)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Giving India’s first practising woman doctor her due: Kadambini Ganguly​"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. The full recognition of her contributions in medicine and the social sector came much later, only in recent decades.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "The full recognition of her contributions in medicine and the social sector came much later, only in recent decades." (Hinglish Arth: चिकित्सा और सामाजिक क्षेत्र में उनके योगदान को पूर्ण मान्यता बहुत बाद में, हाल के दशकों में ही मिली।)

articles.title: Why a shortage of clinical psychologists in Keralam govt hospitals is leaving people with intellectual disabilities waiting for certificates
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: As per the last Kerala Disability Census in 2015, there are about 80,000 persons with various intellectual challenges. However, government hospitals and medical college hospitals in the State currently have only 22 clinical psychologists to conduct IQ assessment tests

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: People with intellectual disabilities in Keralam are struggling to obtain and renew disability certificates due to a severe shortage of clinical psychologists in government hospitals to conduct Intelligence Quotient (IQ) assessment tests.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: As per the latest disability assessment guidelines issued by the Union government’s Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, differently-abled children must undergo assessment tests at least thrice before they turn 18 to obtain permanent disability certificates. During all these assessment phases, an IQ test is a must. However, there are only 22 clinical psychologists under the Directorate of Health Services (DHS) and the Directorate of Medical Education (DME) put together – 17 under the DHS and the rest under the DME.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #29 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Why a shortage of clinical psychologists in Keralam govt hospitals is leaving people with intellectual disabilities waiting for certificates

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 07:50:32 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: As per the last Kerala Disability Census in 2015, there are about 80,000 persons with various intellectual challenges. However, government hospitals and medical college hospitals in the State currently have only 22 clinical psychologists to conduct IQ assessment tests

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: People with intellectual disabilities in Keralam are struggling to obtain and renew disability certificates due to a severe shortage of clinical psychologists in government hospitals to conduct Intelligence Quotient (IQ) assessment tests.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: As per the latest disability assessment guidelines issued by the Union government’s Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, differently-abled children must undergo assessment tests at least thrice before they turn 18 to obtain permanent disability certificates. During all these assessment phases, an IQ test is a must. However, there are only 22 clinical psychologists under the Directorate of Health Services (DHS) and the Directorate of Medical Education (DME) put together – 17 under the DHS and the rest under the DME.

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Rampur Bushahr’s Lavi Fair in Himachal Pradesh traces a Himalayan journey from wool and barter to women entrepreneurs and digital payments

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: What Disneyland is to children today, Lavi Fair in Rampur Bushahr, in Himachal Pradesh’s Shimla district, was to my family in the 1980s. I recall wandering through the fair as an eight-year-old, watching an old man smoking a chillum beside heaps of black sheep fleece and stacks of white woollen pattus (traditional garments of Kinnaur and Kullu women). Mother and her friends carefully chose shawls for their daughters’ and future daughters-in-law’s trousseaux. Years later, I received a beautiful black sheep wool and pashmina shawl for my wedding. Wool finds pride of place at the fair. The name Lavi is linked to “Loe”, a sheet of woollen cloth and the practice of shearing sheep.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Hindu Sunday Magazine / trade policy / trade dispute / trade agreements / international (foreign) trade / Himachal Pradesh / economy / business (general) / taxes and duties / travelogues / travel and commuting

articles.title: Must balance ‘economic patriotism’ with cultural heritage: GJC on PM Modi’s call to stop gold purchases
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) argued that the gold jewellery sector contributes nearly 7-8% to the economy and supports millions of livelihoods

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: While welcoming Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for prioritising locally-made products and reducing gold imports, the All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) has said that India must balance “economic patriotism” and its cultural traditions when it comes to gold jewellery. It argued that the sector contributes “nearly 7-8%” to the economy and supports “millions of livelihoods”. The GJC was reacting to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s recent and repeated appeal to all Indians to stop foreign trips and weddings, to buy local, and to only buy gold if necessary. “The Prime Minister’s appeal for economic patriotism and greater preference for Swadeshi products is timely and welcome,” Rajesh Rokde, Chairman of the All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) said. “While we fully support the Prime Minister’s call for restraint when gold is viewed purely as bullion or an investment instrument, jewellery consumption remains closely linked to culture, craftsmanship, and livelihoods,” Mr. Rokde added. He said that gold and jewellery hold a unique place in India’s cultural heritage, particularly during festive and wedding seasons, such as the period that India will soon enter in October-December. “The jewellery industry, contributing nearly 7-8% to the economy and supporting millions of livelihoods, is an integral part of India’s growth story,” Mr. Rokde asserted. ‘People bought less gold, prices fell’: Modi recalls year-old appeal

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “As a ₹10 lakh crore industry, the Indian jewellery sector must continue to grow responsibly, with greater transparency, value creation, and alignment with national priorities — balancing economic patriotism with India’s enduring cultural traditions,” he added.

📈 Economic, Banking & Finance Paragraph #14 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Must balance ‘economic patriotism’ with cultural heritage: GJC on PM Modi’s call to stop gold purchases

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 04:53:51 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) argued that the gold jewellery sector contributes nearly 7-8% to the economy and supports millions of livelihoods

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: While welcoming Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for prioritising locally-made products and reducing gold imports, the All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) has said that India must balance “economic patriotism” and its cultural traditions when it comes to gold jewellery. It argued that the sector contributes “nearly 7-8%” to the economy and supports “millions of livelihoods”. The GJC was reacting to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s recent and repeated appeal to all Indians to stop foreign trips and weddings, to buy local, and to only buy gold if necessary. “The Prime Minister’s appeal for economic patriotism and greater preference for Swadeshi products is timely and welcome,” Rajesh Rokde, Chairman of the All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) said. “While we fully support the Prime Minister’s call for restraint when gold is viewed purely as bullion or an investment instrument, jewellery consumption remains closely linked to culture, craftsmanship, and livelihoods,” Mr. Rokde added. He said that gold and jewellery hold a unique place in India’s cultural heritage, particularly during festive and wedding seasons, such as the period that India will soon enter in October-December. “The jewellery industry, contributing nearly 7-8% to the economy and supporting millions of livelihoods, is an integral part of India’s growth story,” Mr. Rokde asserted. ‘People bought less gold, prices fell’: Modi recalls year-old appeal

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “As a ₹10 lakh crore industry, the Indian jewellery sector must continue to grow responsibly, with greater transparency, value creation, and alignment with national priorities — balancing economic patriotism with India’s enduring cultural traditions,” he added.

✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Investment (Adjective)
निवेश — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Investment' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile

महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Instrument' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 📈 Economic, Banking & Finance passage on "Must balance ‘economic patriotism’ with cultural heritage: GJC on PM Modi’s call to stop gold purchases", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. The All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) argued that the gold jewellery sector contributes nearly 7-8% to the economy and supports...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Must balance ‘economic patriotism’ with cultural' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Must balance ‘economic patriotism’ with cultu' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Must balance ‘economic patriotism’ with cultu' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) argued that the gold jewellery sector contributes nearly 7-8% to the economy and supports..." (Hinglish Arth: ऑल इंडिया जेम एंड ज्वैलरी डोमेस्टिक काउंसिल (जीजेसी) ने तर्क दिया कि सोने के आभूषण क्षेत्र अर्थव्यवस्था में लगभग 7-8% योगदान देता है और लाखों आजीविका का समर्थन करता है।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Must balance ‘economic patriotism’ with cultural heritage: GJC on PM Modi’s call to stop gold purchases"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. “As a ₹10 lakh crore industry, the Indian jewellery sector must continue to grow responsibly, with greater transparency, value creation, and...
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "“As a ₹10 lakh crore industry, the Indian jewellery sector must continue to grow responsibly, with greater transparency, value creation, and..." (Hinglish Arth: “₹10 लाख करोड़ के उद्योग के रूप में, भारतीय आभूषण क्षेत्र को अधिक पारदर्शिता, मूल्य सृजन और राष्ट्रीय प्राथमिकताओं के साथ संरेखण के साथ जिम्मेदारी से बढ़ना जारी रखना चाहिए – भारत की आर्थिक देशभक्ति के साथ संतुलन बनाना चाहिए।”)

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Research institutions need timely funding, better teaching incentives, greater autonomy, leadership control, safeguards against quid pro quo, and reduced administrative burdens

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Modern science rightly prides itself on independent scrutiny, irrespective of where the scrutiniser is located. There is no reason seeking the assessment of someone outside India has to constitute colonialism. Yet this was the charge in a widely debated article by Sanjeev Sanyal, Satvik Dev, and Payal Sharma, respectively a Member, the Joint Director, and a Young Professional on the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Researchers write up a study and submit it as a manuscript to a journal. Editors at the journal assess the manuscript and send it out to other experts in the field, asking if the work is worth publishing, or needs to be revised or rejected. If the journal accepts the paper, it will be published, brought to the attention of scientists worldwide, and have a permanent record of it preserved.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #26 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Indian science needs fewer borders

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 11:51:56 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Research institutions need timely funding, better teaching incentives, greater autonomy, leadership control, safeguards against quid pro quo, and reduced administrative burdens

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Modern science rightly prides itself on independent scrutiny, irrespective of where the scrutiniser is located. There is no reason seeking the assessment of someone outside India has to constitute colonialism. Yet this was the charge in a widely debated article by Sanjeev Sanyal, Satvik Dev, and Payal Sharma, respectively a Member, the Joint Director, and a Young Professional on the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Researchers write up a study and submit it as a manuscript to a journal. Editors at the journal assess the manuscript and send it out to other experts in the field, asking if the work is worth publishing, or needs to be revised or rejected. If the journal accepts the paper, it will be published, brought to the attention of scientists worldwide, and have a permanent record of it preserved.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Institutional (Adjective)
संस्थागत — देश की संवैधानिक या सरकारी संस्थाओं के नियमों और ढांचे से जुड़ा हुआ।
✓ Syn: Systemic, Organizational, Constitutional  |  ✖ Ant: Individual, Informal, Unorganized

✓ Syn: Statutory, Legitimate, Lawful  |  ✖ Ant: Unconstitutional, Illegal, Arbitrary
Administrative (Adjective)

✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🚀 Science, Tech & Environment passage on "Indian science needs fewer borders", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Research institutions need timely funding, better teaching incentives, greater autonomy, leadership control, safeguards against quid pro quo, and...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Indian science needs fewer borders' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Indian science needs fewer borders' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Indian science needs fewer borders' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Research institutions need timely funding, better teaching incentives, greater autonomy, leadership control, safeguards against quid pro quo, and..." (Hinglish Arth: अनुसंधान संस्थानों को समय पर वित्त पोषण, बेहतर शिक्षण प्रोत्साहन, अधिक स्वायत्तता, नेतृत्व नियंत्रण, बदले की भावना के खिलाफ सुरक्षा उपाय और कम प्रशासनिक बोझ की आवश्यकता है)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Indian science needs fewer borders"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. If the journal accepts the paper, it will be published, brought to the attention of scientists worldwide, and have a permanent record of it preserved.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: India and France are charting a shared space future

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: For over 60 years, France and India have shared one of the longest-standing and most trusted space partnerships in the world. At a time when the international environment has become increasingly complex, this partnership matters more than ever before. Since 1998, their strategic partnership has reposed on defence cooperation — from the Alouette III/Chetak and Rafale aircraft to Scorpène submarines built in India — and people-to-people ties, expanding over time to include artificial intelligence, the blue economy, and much more. What is remarkable about their special global strategic partnership is that, at the core of their national security doctrine, they both share the concept of strategic autonomy. Strategic autonomy does not mean isolating oneself from partners. On the contrary, it means building up one’s own capacities, own analysis, and own decision-making process to be a useful and reliable partner. France has consistently backed India’s rise as a global power, including its permanent seat at the UN Security Council.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: India / France / space programme / defence equipment / Artificial Intelligence / economy / security measures / United Nations / technology (general) / oceans / climate change / ISRO / water / summit / weather science / science (general) / law

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #27 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Thumba to Kourou, over 60 years of space partnership

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 11:32:41 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: India and France are charting a shared space future

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: For over 60 years, France and India have shared one of the longest-standing and most trusted space partnerships in the world. At a time when the international environment has become increasingly complex, this partnership matters more than ever before. Since 1998, their strategic partnership has reposed on defence cooperation — from the Alouette III/Chetak and Rafale aircraft to Scorpène submarines built in India — and people-to-people ties, expanding over time to include artificial intelligence, the blue economy, and much more. What is remarkable about their special global strategic partnership is that, at the core of their national security doctrine, they both share the concept of strategic autonomy. Strategic autonomy does not mean isolating oneself from partners. On the contrary, it means building up one’s own capacities, own analysis, and own decision-making process to be a useful and reliable partner. France has consistently backed India’s rise as a global power, including its permanent seat at the UN Security Council.

articles.title: Russian attack near Ukraine’s capital strikes apartment building, killing two and wounding four others
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Rescuers evacuated nine people, including a child, from the destroyed five-storey building in Dymer, while 11 were believed to be trapped under the rubble

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A Russian attack struck an apartment building in a village near Ukraine’s capital on Sunday (November 22, 2026), killing at least two people and wounding four others, authorities said. Nearly a dozen people were feared trapped beneath the rubble. The morning strike destroyed the five-storey building in Dymer, which is north of Kyiv. Rescuers have evacuated nine people, including a child, authorities said, while another child was hospitalised with injuries. Search and rescue teams worked to find other survivors. Ukraine’s State Emergency Service said 11 people were believed to be trapped. “When (the explosion came), I literally flipped over in bed,” said Mykola Osadnyi, a relative of some of those trapped. “I live about 200 metres from here. Then we ran over here.” “My father-in-law … was screaming, ‘Save me, I’m burning!’” Mr. Osadnyi said. “And now we’re just waiting again to see what happens.” Another resident, Olena Kharkavliuk, recounted that “a terrifying sound woke us up, and then there was an explosion”. “My husband and I have been waiting here since about 4 am, because my older daughter’s classmate and her mother are in there,” Ms. Kharkavliuk told AP . Meanwhile, a rare air alert sounded in Kaliningrad, a Russian exclave near Poland and Lithuania, according to the local Governor, as claims circulated online of drone activity near a major naval base there. The alert late on Saturday (November 21, 2026) came hours after a drone strike in the Gulf of Finland set fire to a Russian cargo ship bound for the region, a key base for Russia’s Baltic Fleet. Finnish emergency services were still working to extinguish the blaze on Sunday (November 22, 2026). Photos and video posted online show drone activity around the city of Baltiysk, where much of the fleet is stationed, but AP could not immediately verify their authenticity. According to local media, air raid sirens were heard in Kaliningrad for the first time since Russia’s all-out invasion of Ukraine on February 24, 2022. Governor Alexei Bezprozvannykh said “a suspicious object coming from the direction of Lithuania” triggered the alert in the Nemansky district near the Lithuanian border, about 170 km north-east of Baltiysk. On Russian Telegram channels, posts by users saying they were Baltiysk residents described air defences working there during the night, with photos and videos of bright streaks against the night sky.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Kaliningrad authorities on Sunday (November 22, 2026) denounced as fake one photo, supposedly from Baltiysk, showing clouds of smoke rising into the night sky, telling Russian State media that it “had nothing to do with the region.” As of Sunday morning (November 22, 2026), Russian authorities reported no casualties or damage in Kaliningrad.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #23 of 30 (22 NOV)

📰 Russian attack near Ukraine’s capital strikes apartment building, killing two and wounding four others

📌 Published: 22 Nov 2026, 11:00:27 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Rescuers evacuated nine people, including a child, from the destroyed five-storey building in Dymer, while 11 were believed to be trapped under the rubble

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A Russian attack struck an apartment building in a village near Ukraine’s capital on Sunday (November 22, 2026), killing at least two people and wounding four others, authorities said. Nearly a dozen people were feared trapped beneath the rubble. The morning strike destroyed the five-storey building in Dymer, which is north of Kyiv. Rescuers have evacuated nine people, including a child, authorities said, while another child was hospitalised with injuries. Search and rescue teams worked to find other survivors. Ukraine’s State Emergency Service said 11 people were believed to be trapped. “When (the explosion came), I literally flipped over in bed,” said Mykola Osadnyi, a relative of some of those trapped. “I live about 200 metres from here. Then we ran over here.” “My father-in-law … was screaming, ‘Save me, I’m burning!’” Mr. Osadnyi said. “And now we’re just waiting again to see what happens.” Another resident, Olena Kharkavliuk, recounted that “a terrifying sound woke us up, and then there was an explosion”. “My husband and I have been waiting here since about 4 am, because my older daughter’s classmate and her mother are in there,” Ms. Kharkavliuk told AP . Meanwhile, a rare air alert sounded in Kaliningrad, a Russian exclave near Poland and Lithuania, according to the local Governor, as claims circulated online of drone activity near a major naval base there. The alert late on Saturday (November 21, 2026) came hours after a drone strike in the Gulf of Finland set fire to a Russian cargo ship bound for the region, a key base for Russia’s Baltic Fleet. Finnish emergency services were still working to extinguish the blaze on Sunday (November 22, 2026). Photos and video posted online show drone activity around the city of Baltiysk, where much of the fleet is stationed, but AP could not immediately verify their authenticity. According to local media, air raid sirens were heard in Kaliningrad for the first time since Russia’s all-out invasion of Ukraine on February 24, 2022. Governor Alexei Bezprozvannykh said “a suspicious object coming from the direction of Lithuania” triggered the alert in the Nemansky district near the Lithuanian border, about 170 km north-east of Baltiysk. On Russian Telegram channels, posts by users saying they were Baltiysk residents described air defences working there during the night, with photos and videos of bright streaks against the night sky.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Kaliningrad authorities on Sunday (November 22, 2026) denounced as fake one photo, supposedly from Baltiysk, showing clouds of smoke rising into the night sky, telling Russian State media that it “had nothing to do with the region.” As of Sunday morning (November 22, 2026), Russian authorities reported no casualties or damage in Kaliningrad.

articles.summary: 1. Core Context & Background: Rescuers evacuated nine people, including a child, from the destroyed five-storey building in Dymer, while 11 were believed to be trapped under the rubble
articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: Rescuers evacuated nine people, including a child, from the destroyed five-storey building in Dymer, while 11 were believed to be trapped under the rubble
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A Russian attack struck an apartment building in a village near Ukraine’s capital on Sunday (November 22, 2026), killing at least two people and wounding four others, authorities said. Nearly a dozen people were feared trapped beneath the rubble. The morning strike destroyed the five-storey building in Dymer, which is north of Kyiv. Rescuers have evacuated nine people, including a child, authorities said, while another child was hospitalised with injuries. Search and rescue teams worked to find other survivors. Ukraine’s State Emergency Service said 11 people were believed to be trapped. “When (the explosion came), I literally flipped over in bed,” said Mykola Osadnyi, a relative of some of those trapped. “I live about 200 metres from here. Then we ran over here.” “My father-in-law … was screaming, ‘Save me, I’m burning!’” Mr. Osadnyi said. “And now we’re just waiting again to see what happens.” Another resident, Olena Kharkavliuk, recounted that “a terrifying sound woke us up, and then there was an explosion”. “My husband and I have been waiting here since about 4 am, because my older daughter’s classmate and her mother are in there,” Ms. Kharkavliuk told AP . Meanwhile, a rare air alert sounded in Kaliningrad, a Russian exclave near Poland and Lithuania, according to the local Governor, as claims circulated online of drone activity near a major naval base there. The alert late on Saturday (November 21, 2026) came hours after a drone strike in the Gulf of Finland set fire to a Russian cargo ship bound for the region, a key base for Russia’s Baltic Fleet. Finnish emergency services were still working to extinguish the blaze on Sunday (November 22, 2026). Photos and video posted online show drone activity around the city of Baltiysk, where much of the fleet is stationed, but AP could not immediately verify their authenticity. According to local media, air raid sirens were heard in Kaliningrad for the first time since Russia’s all-out invasion of Ukraine on February 24, 2022. Governor Alexei Bezprozvannykh said “a suspicious object coming from the direction of Lithuania” triggered the alert in the Nemansky district near the Lithuanian border, about 170 km north-east of Baltiysk. On Russian Telegram channels, posts by users saying they were Baltiysk residents described air defences working there during the night, with photos and videos of bright streaks against the night sky.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Kaliningrad authorities on Sunday (November 22, 2026) denounced as fake one photo, supposedly from Baltiysk, showing clouds of smoke rising into the night sky, telling Russian State media that it “had nothing to do with the region.” As of Sunday morning (November 22, 2026), Russian authorities reported no casualties or damage in Kaliningrad.

articles.title: Woman delivers triplets after non-ART treatment at Telangana govt. hospital; premature babies discharged after NICU care
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: After a nine-year wait and unsuccessful fertility treatment at private hospitals, a couple welcomed triplet boys following treatment at Gandhi Hospital’s IVF Centre. The premature babies, who weighed between 1.4 kg and 1.5 kg at birth, spent over a month in the hospital’s Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU). They were discharged along with their 32-year-old mother after responding well to treatment.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Avanthi enrolled at Gandhi Hospital’s IVF Centre in January this year. Doctors opted for ovulation induction, a non-assisted reproductive treatment, and she conceived in the second cycle. After scans revealed a triplet pregnancy and a short cervix, doctors performed a McDonald’s cervical cerclage at 14 weeks. However, her water broke prematurely at 32 weeks, prompting doctors to deliver the babies on October 7. The newborns were admitted to the NICU, where they received treatment and close monitoring for over a month before being discharged with their mother. Director of Medical Education Vanii appreciated the efforts of the team, including head of the Department of Gynaecology Shobha, IVF specialists Krishnaveni and Fathima Rafi, embryologist Shiva Krishna, lab technician Ashok and counsellor Kavitha.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: IVF specialist Dr Krishnaveni said that they opted ovulation induction as a first line of treatment, which is not a In Vitro Fertilization (IVF) method. “We conduct evaluations to know if non-IVF methods can be used as first line of treatment to avoid burden on couples who are already in distress,” she said. Currently, over 500 couples have rolled for treatments at the government hospitals IVF centre.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #7 of 30 (21 NOV)

📰 Woman delivers triplets after non-ART treatment at Telangana govt. hospital; premature babies discharged after NICU care

📌 Published: 21 Nov 2026, 01:20:03 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: After a nine-year wait and unsuccessful fertility treatment at private hospitals, a couple welcomed triplet boys following treatment at Gandhi Hospital’s IVF Centre. The premature babies, who weighed between 1.4 kg and 1.5 kg at birth, spent over a month in the hospital’s Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU). They were discharged along with their 32-year-old mother after responding well to treatment.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Avanthi enrolled at Gandhi Hospital’s IVF Centre in January this year. Doctors opted for ovulation induction, a non-assisted reproductive treatment, and she conceived in the second cycle. After scans revealed a triplet pregnancy and a short cervix, doctors performed a McDonald’s cervical cerclage at 14 weeks. However, her water broke prematurely at 32 weeks, prompting doctors to deliver the babies on October 7. The newborns were admitted to the NICU, where they received treatment and close monitoring for over a month before being discharged with their mother. Director of Medical Education Vanii appreciated the efforts of the team, including head of the Department of Gynaecology Shobha, IVF specialists Krishnaveni and Fathima Rafi, embryologist Shiva Krishna, lab technician Ashok and counsellor Kavitha.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: IVF specialist Dr Krishnaveni said that they opted ovulation induction as a first line of treatment, which is not a In Vitro Fertilization (IVF) method. “We conduct evaluations to know if non-IVF methods can be used as first line of treatment to avoid burden on couples who are already in distress,” she said. Currently, over 500 couples have rolled for treatments at the government hospitals IVF centre.

✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Department (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Department' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Treatment (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Treatment' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Woman delivers triplets after non-ART treatment at Telangana govt. hospital; premature babies discharged after NICU care", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. After a nine-year wait and unsuccessful fertility treatment at private hospitals, a couple welcomed triplet boys following treatment at Gandhi...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Woman delivers triplets after non-ART treatment ' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Woman delivers triplets after non-ART treatme' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Woman delivers triplets after non-ART treatme' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "After a nine-year wait and unsuccessful fertility treatment at private hospitals, a couple welcomed triplet boys following treatment at Gandhi..." (Hinglish Arth: नौ साल के इंतजार और निजी अस्पतालों में असफल प्रजनन उपचार के बाद, एक जोड़े ने गांधी अस्पताल के आईवीएफ केंद्र में इलाज के बाद तीन बेटों का स्वागत किया।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Woman delivers triplets after non-ART treatment at Telangana govt. hospital; premature babies discharged after NICU care"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Currently, over 500 couples have rolled for treatments at the government hospitals IVF centre.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Currently, over 500 couples have rolled for treatments at the government hospitals IVF centre." (Hinglish Arth: वर्तमान में, 500 से अधिक जोड़े सरकारी अस्पतालों के आईवीएफ केंद्र में इलाज के लिए आए हैं।)

articles.title: IJCCI to lead business delegation to Japan from Nov. 30
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The Indo-Japan Chamber of Commerce and Industry (IJCCI) organised a business networking meeting with a 16-member business delegation from Osaka, Japan, to strengthen bilateral business ties and explore opportunities for trade, investment, and industrial collaboration between India and Japan.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The delegation was led by Hiromitsu Morishima, Chairperson, International Business Committee, Osaka Chamber of Commerce and Industry, and Yasushi Ninomiya, Director-General, JETRO Osaka. The companies spoke about their products and business opportunities. To strengthen bilateral economic relations, IJCCI is leading a 16-member delegation to Japan from November 30 to December 4. The delegation will visit Tokyo, Yokohama, Kochi, Fukuoka, Hiroshima, and Osaka. “We particularly look forward to strengthening our engagement with Osaka, which is one of Japan’s leading commercial and industrial centres,” said IJCCI president S. Padmanabhan. “India, with its large domestic market, growing manufacturing capabilities, and developing digital economy, offers significant opportunities for Japanese businesses,” Mr. Padmanabhan added.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: He further said that Indian companies can benefit from Japanese technology, management practices, and innovation.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #8 of 30 (21 NOV)

📰 IJCCI to lead business delegation to Japan from Nov. 30

📌 Published: 21 Nov 2026, 01:19:59 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The Indo-Japan Chamber of Commerce and Industry (IJCCI) organised a business networking meeting with a 16-member business delegation from Osaka, Japan, to strengthen bilateral business ties and explore opportunities for trade, investment, and industrial collaboration between India and Japan.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The delegation was led by Hiromitsu Morishima, Chairperson, International Business Committee, Osaka Chamber of Commerce and Industry, and Yasushi Ninomiya, Director-General, JETRO Osaka. The companies spoke about their products and business opportunities. To strengthen bilateral economic relations, IJCCI is leading a 16-member delegation to Japan from November 30 to December 4. The delegation will visit Tokyo, Yokohama, Kochi, Fukuoka, Hiroshima, and Osaka. “We particularly look forward to strengthening our engagement with Osaka, which is one of Japan’s leading commercial and industrial centres,” said IJCCI president S. Padmanabhan. “India, with its large domestic market, growing manufacturing capabilities, and developing digital economy, offers significant opportunities for Japanese businesses,” Mr. Padmanabhan added.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: He further said that Indian companies can benefit from Japanese technology, management practices, and innovation.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Bilateral (Adjective)
द्विपक्षीय — दो देशों के बीच आपसी समझौता, व्यापार या कूटनीतिक बातचीत।
✓ Syn: Reciprocal, Two-sided, Mutual  |  ✖ Ant: Unilateral, Multilateral, One-way
Collaboration (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Collaboration' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
International (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'International' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Delegation (Adjective / Verb)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Delegation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "IJCCI to lead business delegation to Japan from Nov. 30", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. The Indo-Japan Chamber of Commerce and Industry (IJCCI) organised a business networking meeting with a 16-member business delegation from Osaka,...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'IJCCI to lead business delegation to Japan from ' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'IJCCI to lead business delegation to Japan fr' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'IJCCI to lead business delegation to Japan fr' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The Indo-Japan Chamber of Commerce and Industry (IJCCI) organised a business networking meeting with a 16-member business delegation from Osaka,..." (Hinglish Arth: इंडो-जापान चैंबर ऑफ कॉमर्स एंड इंडस्ट्री (आईजेसीसीआई) ने द्विपक्षीय व्यापार संबंधों को मजबूत करने और अवसरों का पता लगाने के लिए ओसाका, जापान के 16 सदस्यीय व्यापार प्रतिनिधिमंडल के साथ एक व्यापार नेटवर्किंग बैठक का आयोजन किया।)

A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. He further said that Indian companies can benefit from Japanese technology, management practices, and innovation.

D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.

articles.title: Infra push and low base effect pushes core sector growth to series-high of 10.9% in October 2026
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: While the coal and electricity sectors saw growth shoot up, a large part of this was due to a statistical effect rather than growth in actual output. On the other hand, fuel-related sectors contracted again

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Growth in the core industrial sectors of the economy climbed to a series-high of 10.9% in October 2026, driven by a surge in electricity generation, and coal, cement, and iron ore production, and a low base effect, official data released on Friday (November 20, 2026) showed. Data released by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry on the Index of Core Industries shows that growth in October surpassed the 8.2% in September, the previous series high. The new index, released this year with a base year of 2022-23, has data that goes back only up to April 2024. However, the data also shows that the strong growth figure in October was also likely aided by the fact that the index grew a relatively poor 0.8% in October last year. “While core output surged by 10.9% in October 2026, the fastest pace in the new series, this was supported by a low base related to the shift in the festive calendar, with output having expanded by a marginal 0.8% in the year ago month,” Aditi Nayar, chief economist at ICRA said. “While the growth print for October 2026 signals a strong start for the third quarter of FY2027, this is largely optical,” Ms. Nayar added. “The average performance for October-November 2026 would provide a better assessment, as this would adjust for festive base effects.” Within the index, the coal sector saw growth accelerating to 23.05% in October 2026, far faster than the 10.7% registered in September. October’s performance, however, is likely also due to low base effect, since the sector contracted 8.4% in October last year. The growth in the index, however, is in line with what the industry itself has reported. Coal India, the country’s largest coal company, reported that production increased about 19% to 67.2 million tonnes (MT) in October. A major reason for the growth in coal production was likely demand from the power sector, which saw electricity generation jump by 21.6% in October 2026, up from 12.6% in the previous month. However, this sector too could have benefited from a low base effect, since it contracted nearly 7% in October 2025. Within the index, the infrastructure-related sectors were the only ones that grew strongly without the aid of a statistical low base effect.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The iron ore sector, for example, grew at a three-month high of 23.4% in October 2026, compared to 18.4% in September and 8.7% in October last year. One of the factors driving this strong growth was that steel production grew at 7.3% in October, the fastest rate in seven months.

📈 Economic, Banking & Finance Paragraph #17 of 30 (21 NOV)

📰 Infra push and low base effect pushes core sector growth to series-high of 10.9% in October 2026

📌 Published: 21 Nov 2026, 01:18:11 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: While the coal and electricity sectors saw growth shoot up, a large part of this was due to a statistical effect rather than growth in actual output. On the other hand, fuel-related sectors contracted again

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Growth in the core industrial sectors of the economy climbed to a series-high of 10.9% in October 2026, driven by a surge in electricity generation, and coal, cement, and iron ore production, and a low base effect, official data released on Friday (November 20, 2026) showed. Data released by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry on the Index of Core Industries shows that growth in October surpassed the 8.2% in September, the previous series high. The new index, released this year with a base year of 2022-23, has data that goes back only up to April 2024. However, the data also shows that the strong growth figure in October was also likely aided by the fact that the index grew a relatively poor 0.8% in October last year. “While core output surged by 10.9% in October 2026, the fastest pace in the new series, this was supported by a low base related to the shift in the festive calendar, with output having expanded by a marginal 0.8% in the year ago month,” Aditi Nayar, chief economist at ICRA said. “While the growth print for October 2026 signals a strong start for the third quarter of FY2027, this is largely optical,” Ms. Nayar added. “The average performance for October-November 2026 would provide a better assessment, as this would adjust for festive base effects.” Within the index, the coal sector saw growth accelerating to 23.05% in October 2026, far faster than the 10.7% registered in September. October’s performance, however, is likely also due to low base effect, since the sector contracted 8.4% in October last year. The growth in the index, however, is in line with what the industry itself has reported. Coal India, the country’s largest coal company, reported that production increased about 19% to 67.2 million tonnes (MT) in October. A major reason for the growth in coal production was likely demand from the power sector, which saw electricity generation jump by 21.6% in October 2026, up from 12.6% in the previous month. However, this sector too could have benefited from a low base effect, since it contracted nearly 7% in October 2025. Within the index, the infrastructure-related sectors were the only ones that grew strongly without the aid of a statistical low base effect.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The iron ore sector, for example, grew at a three-month high of 23.4% in October 2026, compared to 18.4% in September and 8.7% in October last year. One of the factors driving this strong growth was that steel production grew at 7.3% in October, the fastest rate in seven months.

🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 📈 Economic, Banking & Finance passage on "Infra push and low base effect pushes core sector growth to series-high of 10.9% in October 2026", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. While the coal and electricity sectors saw growth shoot up, a large part of this was due to a statistical effect rather than growth in actual output.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Infra push and low base effect pushes core secto' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Infra push and low base effect pushes core se' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Infra push and low base effect pushes core se' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "While the coal and electricity sectors saw growth shoot up, a large part of this was due to a statistical effect rather than growth in actual output." (Hinglish Arth: जबकि कोयला और बिजली क्षेत्रों में वृद्धि देखी गई, इसका एक बड़ा हिस्सा वास्तविक उत्पादन में वृद्धि के बजाय सांख्यिकीय प्रभाव के कारण था।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Infra push and low base effect pushes core sector growth to series-high of 10.9% in October 2026"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. One of the factors driving this strong growth was that steel production grew at 7.3% in October, the fastest rate in seven months.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "One of the factors driving this strong growth was that steel production grew at 7.3% in October, the fastest rate in seven months." (Hinglish Arth: इस मजबूत वृद्धि को चलाने वाले कारकों में से एक यह था कि अक्टूबर में इस्पात उत्पादन 7.3% की दर से बढ़ा, जो सात महीनों में सबसे तेज़ दर थी।)

articles.title: Following Cyclone Akvan, monsoon rain to resume over T.N. from tomorrow
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The RMC has forecast moderate rainfall in coastal districts, including Chennai and Cuddalore, and mild rainfall over adjoining areas; wet weather likely to last till the first week of December

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Following Cyclone Akvan’s passage on Friday morning, most parts of Tamil Nadu are likely to experience a brief break in monsoon activity, accompanied by a dip in night-time temperatures. Wet weather is expected to return on Sunday and intensify over the subsequent days. The break in rainfall is expected to raise day temperatures by two or three degrees Celsius in a few pockets of the State. The Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC) has also forecast ground frost at isolated places in the Nilgiris and Kodaikanal till Sunday. The absence of widespread rainfall has pushed various districts, including Tiruvarur, Thanjavur, Madurai, Salem, and Chengalpattu, into the rainfall deficit category. The State has so far received nearly 26 cm of monsoon rainfall, which is 14% lower than its seasonal share since October 1. RMC officials said Cyclone Akvan was expected to weaken into a depression on Friday, and gradually fade away. V.R. Durai, Head, Regional Weather Forecasting Centre, RMC, said dry and cold northwesterly winds and the absence of cloud cover and rainfall led to a rise in day temperatures and drop in minimum temperatures over most parts of the State. A trough in the easterly wave is likely to revive rainfall activity from Sunday and bring intense rainfall from Monday as it moves across the State. While coastal districts are expected to benefit more, interior Tamil Nadu is also likely to receive moderate rainfall till November 26. “We are expecting wet weather in the State till December first week, with a low pressure area likely to form then. The sustained rainfall activity may narrow rainfall deficit,” he said. The RMC has forecast moderate rainfall over coastal districts, including Chennai, Cuddalore, and Nagapattinam, on Sunday and mild rainfall over areas adjoining coastal districts.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: On Monday, rainfall is expected to intensify over 10 coastal districts, including Cuddalore, Thoothukudi, and Kanniyakumari.

hinglishTracks.en: The RMC has forecast moderate rainfall in coastal districts, including Chennai and Cuddalore, and mild rainfall over adjoining areas; wet weather likely to last till the first week of December
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — आरएमसी ने चेन्नई और कुड्डालोर सहित तटीय जिलों में मध्यम वर्षा और आसपास के क्षेत्रों में हल्की वर्षा का अनुमान लगाया है; गीला मौसम दिसंबर के पहले सप्ताह तक रहने की संभावना है।

hinglishTracks.en: Following Cyclone Akvan’s passage on Friday morning, most parts of Tamil Nadu are likely to experience a brief break in monsoon activity, accompanied by a dip in night-time temperatures.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — शुक्रवार की सुबह चक्रवात अकवन के गुजरने के बाद, तमिलनाडु के अधिकांश हिस्सों में रात के समय के तापमान में गिरावट के साथ, मानसून गतिविधि में एक संक्षिप्त विराम का अनुभव होने की संभावना है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Experience' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Experience' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Significant, Substantial, Strategic और Antonyms हैं: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial।

hinglishTracks.en: Wet weather is expected to return on Sunday and intensify over the subsequent days.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — रविवार को गीला मौसम लौटने और उसके बाद के दिनों में तेज़ होने की उम्मीद है।।

hinglishTracks.en: The break in rainfall is expected to raise day temperatures by two or three degrees Celsius in a few pockets of the State.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — बारिश में रुकावट से राज्य के कुछ इलाकों में दिन का तापमान दो या तीन डिग्री सेल्सियस बढ़ने की उम्मीद है।।

hinglishTracks.en: The Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC) has also forecast ground frost at isolated places in the Nilgiris and Kodaikanal till Sunday.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — क्षेत्रीय मौसम विज्ञान केंद्र (आरएमसी) ने भी रविवार तक नीलगिरी और कोडाइकनाल में अलग-अलग स्थानों पर बर्फ जमने की भविष्यवाणी की है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Meteorological' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: मौसम विज्ञान और वायुमंडलीय परिवर्तनों से संबंधित (Connected with weather forecasting and atmospheric shifts). इसके Synonyms हैं: Atmospheric, Climatic, Weather-related और Antonyms हैं: Geological, Subterranean, Terrestrial।

hinglishTracks.en: The absence of widespread rainfall has pushed various districts, including Tiruvarur, Thanjavur, Madurai, Salem, and Chengalpattu, into the rainfall deficit category.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — व्यापक वर्षा की अनुपस्थिति ने तिरुवरुर, तंजावुर, मदुरै, सेलम और चेंगलपट्टू सहित विभिन्न जिलों को वर्षा की कमी की श्रेणी में धकेल दिया है।।

hinglishTracks.en: The State has so far received nearly 26 cm of monsoon rainfall, which is 14% lower than its seasonal share since October 1.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — राज्य में अब तक लगभग 26 सेमी मानसूनी वर्षा हुई है, जो 1 अक्टूबर के बाद से इसके मौसमी हिस्से से 14% कम है।।

hinglishTracks.en: RMC officials said Cyclone Akvan was expected to weaken into a depression on Friday, and gradually fade away.

hinglishTracks.en: Durai, Head, Regional Weather Forecasting Centre, RMC, said dry and cold northwesterly winds and the absence of cloud cover and rainfall led to a rise in day temperatures and drop in minimum temperatures over most parts of the State.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — आरएमसी के क्षेत्रीय मौसम पूर्वानुमान केंद्र के प्रमुख दुरई ने कहा कि शुष्क और ठंडी उत्तर-पश्चिमी हवाएं और बादल और बारिश की अनुपस्थिति के कारण राज्य के अधिकांश हिस्सों में दिन के तापमान में वृद्धि हुई और न्यूनतम तापमान में गिरावट आई।।

hinglishTracks.en: A trough in the easterly wave is likely to revive rainfall activity from Sunday and bring intense rainfall from Monday as it moves across the State.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — पूर्वी लहर में एक ट्रफ रेखा के रविवार से वर्षा गतिविधि फिर से शुरू होने और सोमवार से तीव्र वर्षा होने की संभावना है क्योंकि यह पूरे राज्य में आगे बढ़ेगी।।

hinglishTracks.en: While coastal districts are expected to benefit more, interior Tamil Nadu is also likely to receive moderate rainfall till November 26.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — जबकि तटीय जिलों को अधिक लाभ होने की उम्मीद है, आंतरिक तमिलनाडु में भी 26 नवंबर तक मध्यम वर्षा होने की संभावना है।।

hinglishTracks.en: “We are expecting wet weather in the State till December first week, with a low pressure area likely to form then.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — “हम दिसंबर के पहले सप्ताह तक राज्य में गीले मौसम की उम्मीद कर रहे हैं, उसके बाद कम दबाव का क्षेत्र बनने की संभावना है।।

hinglishTracks.en: The sustained rainfall activity may narrow rainfall deficit,” he said.

hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — आरएमसी ने रविवार को चेन्नई, कुड्डालोर और नागापट्टिनम सहित तटीय जिलों में मध्यम बारिश और तटीय जिलों से सटे इलाकों में हल्की बारिश का अनुमान लगाया है।।
