articles.title: Iran says allies China, Russia oppose change in nuclear doctrine
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Iran has barred the International Atomic Energy Agency from inspecting its nuclear sites, citing security concerns and blaming the agency for failing to condemn U.S. and Israeli attacks on its nuclear facilities

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said China and Russia oppose a change in Tehran’s nuclear doctrine, amid domestic calls for a shift, state media reported. In an interview published on Saturday (November 21, 2026), Mr. Araghchi told the state-run Iran Daily newspaper that the issue was “broad, serious” and had its own “supporters and opponents”. “Russia and China are also opposed” to a change in Iran’s doctrine, he added. Both countries have strategic cooperation agreements with Iran. “What matters is that, up to this point, our doctrine has not changed, and our official positions remain the same as before,” Mr. Araghchi said. Debate over changing Iran’s nuclear doctrine has resurfaced in the country’s political circles, particularly among hardliners, following wars with Israel and the United States that saw Iranian nuclear facilities come under heavy attack. Some advocates of a shift argue that it would pave the way for Tehran to develop a nuclear weapon as a deterrent. Iran has barred the International Atomic Energy Agency from inspecting its nuclear sites, citing security concerns and blaming the agency for failing to condemn U.S. and Israeli attacks on its nuclear facilities. Last week, the UN nuclear watchdog urged Iran to take “incremental steps” to allow inspectors to return to key facilities, saying such access was “critical”. Iranian officials continue to cite a fatwa, or religious decree, issued by former supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei that prohibited the development of weapons of mass destruction, including nuclear weapons.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “There are those who believe the country’s nuclear doctrine should be maintained in its current form, and others who speak of the need to change it. Both sides have their own arguments and rationale,” Mr. Araghchi said.

Both countries have strategic cooperation agreements with Iran. “What matters is that, up to this point, our doctrine has not changed, and our official positions remain the same as before,” Mr. Araghchi said. articles.summary: 1. Core Context & Background: Iran has barred the International Atomic Energy Agency from inspecting its nuclear sites, citing security concerns and blaming the agency for failing to condemn U.S. and Israeli attacks on its nuclear facilities
articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: Iran has barred the International Atomic Energy Agency from inspecting its nuclear sites, citing security concerns and blaming the agency for failing to condemn U.S. and Israeli attacks on its nuclear facilities
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said China and Russia oppose a change in Tehran’s nuclear doctrine, amid domestic calls for a shift, state media reported. In an interview published on Saturday (November 21, 2026), Mr. Araghchi told the state-run Iran Daily newspaper that the issue was “broad, serious” and had its own “supporters and opponents”. “Russia and China are also opposed” to a change in Iran’s doctrine, he added. Both countries have strategic cooperation agreements with Iran. “What matters is that, up to this point, our doctrine has not changed, and our official positions remain the same as before,” Mr. Araghchi said. Debate over changing Iran’s nuclear doctrine has resurfaced in the country’s political circles, particularly among hardliners, following wars with Israel and the United States that saw Iranian nuclear facilities come under heavy attack. Some advocates of a shift argue that it would pave the way for Tehran to develop a nuclear weapon as a deterrent. Iran has barred the International Atomic Energy Agency from inspecting its nuclear sites, citing security concerns and blaming the agency for failing to condemn U.S. and Israeli attacks on its nuclear facilities. Last week, the UN nuclear watchdog urged Iran to take “incremental steps” to allow inspectors to return to key facilities, saying such access was “critical”. Iranian officials continue to cite a fatwa, or religious decree, issued by former supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei that prohibited the development of weapons of mass destruction, including nuclear weapons.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “There are those who believe the country’s nuclear doctrine should be maintained in its current form, and others who speak of the need to change it. Both sides have their own arguments and rationale,” Mr. Araghchi said.

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The diplomatic deadlock comes amid continuing tensions between Washington and Tehran, with both countries yet to reach an understanding on the future of Iran's nuclear programme

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Negotiations between the United States and Iran have stalled over disagreements concerning Tehran's enriched uranium stockpile , with mediators warning that they cannot guarantee a return to military escalation in West Asia. Washington is insisting on a clear roadmap and written guarantees from Iran that it will eliminate its enriched uranium stockpile and refrain from resuming uranium enrichment in the future, Al Arabiya English reported, citing a senior source. However, both sides have maintained firm positions on the issue despite several proposals put forward by mediators to bridge their differences, the report said. The diplomatic deadlock comes amid continuing tensions between Washington and Tehran, with both countries yet to reach an understanding on the future of Iran's nuclear programme. Earlier, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran would not accept an agreement with Washington merely to end the current diplomatic impasse, insisting that any settlement must protect Iran's national interests and provide assurances against another military confrontation. In an interview with an Iranian state-run newspaper, as reported by Al Jazeera , Mr. Araghchi said Iran was seeking a "good, honourable and lasting agreement" rather than remaining in a situation of "neither war nor peace". Questioning the durability of any potential understanding with Washington, he said, "What is the point of reaching an agreement today if it is violated two months later and war resumes?" Mr. Araghchi recalled that fighting had resumed just 15 days after the June ceasefire agreement, arguing that Tehran would not accept an arrangement simply to escape the current situation. Iran strikes U.S. air base in Kuwait, targets Bahrain amid wider Gulf attacks A step back: On Trump’s no-war, no-deal approach against Iran On the nuclear issue, the Iranian Foreign Minister said Tehran was open to negotiations over its stockpile of uranium enriched to 60% but ruled out transferring the material outside the country. He maintained that a fair formula could be reached on uranium enrichment, provided it formed part of a broader agreement addressing Iran's national interests and security concerns. Mr. Araghchi also confirmed that Tehran and Washington continued exchanging messages and proposals through mediators, including Qatar and Pakistan. "We are people of diplomacy, and we still have hope in diplomacy," he said. Meanwhile, he maintained that Iran remained willing to reopen the Strait of Hormuz if Washington fulfilled its conditions, underlining Tehran's position that any diplomatic settlement must address its nuclear programme, sanctions and security concerns.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Iran / USA / Israel-US strikes on Iran / nuclear weapons

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #24 of 30 (21 NOV)

📰 Iran-U.S. negotiations stalled over uranium enrichment dispute, mediators warn of renewed conflict, says reports

📌 Published: 21 Nov 2026, 04:08:24 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The diplomatic deadlock comes amid continuing tensions between Washington and Tehran, with both countries yet to reach an understanding on the future of Iran's nuclear programme

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Negotiations between the United States and Iran have stalled over disagreements concerning Tehran's enriched uranium stockpile , with mediators warning that they cannot guarantee a return to military escalation in West Asia. Washington is insisting on a clear roadmap and written guarantees from Iran that it will eliminate its enriched uranium stockpile and refrain from resuming uranium enrichment in the future, Al Arabiya English reported, citing a senior source. However, both sides have maintained firm positions on the issue despite several proposals put forward by mediators to bridge their differences, the report said. The diplomatic deadlock comes amid continuing tensions between Washington and Tehran, with both countries yet to reach an understanding on the future of Iran's nuclear programme. Earlier, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran would not accept an agreement with Washington merely to end the current diplomatic impasse, insisting that any settlement must protect Iran's national interests and provide assurances against another military confrontation. In an interview with an Iranian state-run newspaper, as reported by Al Jazeera , Mr. Araghchi said Iran was seeking a "good, honourable and lasting agreement" rather than remaining in a situation of "neither war nor peace". Questioning the durability of any potential understanding with Washington, he said, "What is the point of reaching an agreement today if it is violated two months later and war resumes?" Mr. Araghchi recalled that fighting had resumed just 15 days after the June ceasefire agreement, arguing that Tehran would not accept an arrangement simply to escape the current situation. Iran strikes U.S. air base in Kuwait, targets Bahrain amid wider Gulf attacks A step back: On Trump’s no-war, no-deal approach against Iran On the nuclear issue, the Iranian Foreign Minister said Tehran was open to negotiations over its stockpile of uranium enriched to 60% but ruled out transferring the material outside the country. He maintained that a fair formula could be reached on uranium enrichment, provided it formed part of a broader agreement addressing Iran's national interests and security concerns. Mr. Araghchi also confirmed that Tehran and Washington continued exchanging messages and proposals through mediators, including Qatar and Pakistan. "We are people of diplomacy, and we still have hope in diplomacy," he said. Meanwhile, he maintained that Iran remained willing to reopen the Strait of Hormuz if Washington fulfilled its conditions, underlining Tehran's position that any diplomatic settlement must address its nuclear programme, sanctions and security concerns.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Iran / USA / Israel-US strikes on Iran / nuclear weapons

🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🌐 International & Geopolitics passage on "Iran-U.S. negotiations stalled over uranium enrichment dispute, mediators warn of renewed conflict, says reports", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. The diplomatic deadlock comes amid continuing tensions between Washington and Tehran, with both countries yet to reach an understanding on the future...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Iran-U.S. negotiations stalled over uranium enri' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Iran-U.S. negotiations stalled over uranium e' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Iran-U.S. negotiations stalled over uranium e' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The diplomatic deadlock comes amid continuing tensions between Washington and Tehran, with both countries yet to reach an understanding on the future..." (Hinglish Arth: यह कूटनीतिक गतिरोध वाशिंगटन और तेहरान के बीच जारी तनाव के बीच आया है, दोनों देशों के बीच ईरान के परमाणु कार्यक्रम के भविष्य पर अभी तक कोई सहमति नहीं बन पाई है।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Iran-U.S. negotiations stalled over uranium enrichment dispute, mediators warn of renewed conflict, says reports"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Iran / USA / Israel-US strikes on Iran / nuclear weapons.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Iran / USA / Israel-US strikes on Iran / nuclear weapons." (Hinglish Arth: ईरान/अमेरिका/ईरान पर इजरायल-अमेरिका के हमले/परमाणु हथियार)

articles.title: Study highlights need for trauma-informed, community-based mental health support for refugees in India
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The study calls for mental health support rooted in refugee communities, with trained local workers and refugee leaders playing a central role in shaping care that responds to their lived realities, including legal uncertainty, social exclusion and difficult living conditions

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Mental health concerns among refugee communities are linked not only to past trauma, violence and forced displacement but also to legal uncertainty, limited work opportunities, poor living conditions and social isolation in host countries, finds a study of Sri Lankan Tamil and Rohingya communities in India, published in the International Journal of Migration, Health and Social Care.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Titled ‘Building mental health capacity in protracted refugee situations: Empirical pointers from Sri Lankan Tamil and Rohingya populations in India’, the study looks at common mental health concerns and barriers to accessing care. It calls for training community members and health workers to recognise psychological distress, provide basic support and facilitate access to professional mental health services.

articles.title: South Korea confirms first case of cholera in 10 years
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: It is the country's first case of cholera since 2016, when authorities identified three cases suspected to be caused by contaminated seafood. At least 162 people got sick in a larger outbreak in 2001

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: South Korea on Friday reported its first case of cholera in 10 years, with health authorities urging people to take precautionary measures, use only safe water and wash their food properly. The Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency said health workers confirmed cholera from test samples of a person who had visited a hospital emergency room in the southeastern port city of Changwon earlier this month, showing symptoms of vomiting and diarrhea. The agency said the unidentified person, who recovered and was discharged on Tuesday, had not travelled overseas in the past two months. It said health workers were trying to trace the source of infection and the people the person had been in contact with. It was the country's first case of cholera since 2016, when authorities identified three cases suspected to be caused by contaminated seafood. At least 162 people got sick in a larger outbreak in 2001.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The agency issued guidance urging people to stick to safe water and cooked food and to wash and peel fruits and vegetables. It also urged medical facilities to promptly test and report suspected cases.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #29 of 30 (21 NOV)

📰 South Korea confirms first case of cholera in 10 years

📌 Published: 21 Nov 2026, 05:02:25 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: It is the country's first case of cholera since 2016, when authorities identified three cases suspected to be caused by contaminated seafood. At least 162 people got sick in a larger outbreak in 2001

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: South Korea on Friday reported its first case of cholera in 10 years, with health authorities urging people to take precautionary measures, use only safe water and wash their food properly. The Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency said health workers confirmed cholera from test samples of a person who had visited a hospital emergency room in the southeastern port city of Changwon earlier this month, showing symptoms of vomiting and diarrhea. The agency said the unidentified person, who recovered and was discharged on Tuesday, had not travelled overseas in the past two months. It said health workers were trying to trace the source of infection and the people the person had been in contact with. It was the country's first case of cholera since 2016, when authorities identified three cases suspected to be caused by contaminated seafood. At least 162 people got sick in a larger outbreak in 2001.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The agency issued guidance urging people to stick to safe water and cooked food and to wash and peel fruits and vegetables. It also urged medical facilities to promptly test and report suspected cases.

articles.title: Strain-specific Ebola jab trials to start in DR Congo next week: WHO
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: A total of 5,568 deaths out of 11,376 cases have been confirmed in the vast central African country's worst-ever Ebola outbreak, according to the WHO

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Two potential vaccines against the deadly Ebola strain gripping the Democratic Republic of Congo are set to enter trials in the outbreak's epicentre next week, the World Health Organisation announced earlier this week. There are currently no vaccines or treatments for the less common Bundibugyo species of Ebola behind the explosive outbreak declared in May, triggering an international public health emergency. A total of 5,568 deaths out of 11,376 cases have been confirmed in the vast central African country's worst-ever Ebola outbreak, according to the WHO. "We expect two candidate vaccines developed specifically for Bundibugyo virus to begin testing as early as next week," WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus told a press conference at the UN health agency's headquarters in Geneva. The so-called Tumaini trial in the DRC is a single framework that can test the safety, efficacy and ability to trigger an immune response of multiple vaccines. The trial uses ring vaccination: immunising contacts deemed to be at high risk of infection. Ervebo, a vaccine already approved for use against the more common Zaire strain of Ebola, kicked off the Tumaini trial on October 23, at the full-scale Phase 3 level, to determine if it also offers any protection against Bundibugyo. The trial will now also incorporate the two Bundibugyo-specific candidate vaccines, which have both gone through earlier-stage, smaller-scale Phase 1 clinical trials. One is a ChAdOx1 adenoviral vector jab developed by the University of Oxford; the other, mRNA-1469, was developed by the US-based Moderna group using the mRNA technology made famous during the Covid-19 pandemic. Meg Doherty, head of the WHO's science for health department, said Phase 2 clinical trials with the candidate vaccines are scheduled to begin on November 26 or 27 in Bunia, the capital of the DRC's northeastern Ituri province at the epicentre of the outbreak.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: If the safety and immune response data from the Phase 2 trial pass the next stage of review, the candidate jabs can move forward to a full-scale Phase 3 trial.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #30 of 30 (21 NOV)

📰 Strain-specific Ebola jab trials to start in DR Congo next week: WHO

📌 Published: 21 Nov 2026, 05:00:57 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: A total of 5,568 deaths out of 11,376 cases have been confirmed in the vast central African country's worst-ever Ebola outbreak, according to the WHO

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Two potential vaccines against the deadly Ebola strain gripping the Democratic Republic of Congo are set to enter trials in the outbreak's epicentre next week, the World Health Organisation announced earlier this week. There are currently no vaccines or treatments for the less common Bundibugyo species of Ebola behind the explosive outbreak declared in May, triggering an international public health emergency. A total of 5,568 deaths out of 11,376 cases have been confirmed in the vast central African country's worst-ever Ebola outbreak, according to the WHO. "We expect two candidate vaccines developed specifically for Bundibugyo virus to begin testing as early as next week," WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus told a press conference at the UN health agency's headquarters in Geneva. The so-called Tumaini trial in the DRC is a single framework that can test the safety, efficacy and ability to trigger an immune response of multiple vaccines. The trial uses ring vaccination: immunising contacts deemed to be at high risk of infection. Ervebo, a vaccine already approved for use against the more common Zaire strain of Ebola, kicked off the Tumaini trial on October 23, at the full-scale Phase 3 level, to determine if it also offers any protection against Bundibugyo. The trial will now also incorporate the two Bundibugyo-specific candidate vaccines, which have both gone through earlier-stage, smaller-scale Phase 1 clinical trials. One is a ChAdOx1 adenoviral vector jab developed by the University of Oxford; the other, mRNA-1469, was developed by the US-based Moderna group using the mRNA technology made famous during the Covid-19 pandemic. Meg Doherty, head of the WHO's science for health department, said Phase 2 clinical trials with the candidate vaccines are scheduled to begin on November 26 or 27 in Bunia, the capital of the DRC's northeastern Ituri province at the epicentre of the outbreak.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: If the safety and immune response data from the Phase 2 trial pass the next stage of review, the candidate jabs can move forward to a full-scale Phase 3 trial.

🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🚀 Science, Tech & Environment passage on "Strain-specific Ebola jab trials to start in DR Congo next week: WHO", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. A total of 5,568 deaths out of 11,376 cases have been confirmed in the vast central African country's worst-ever Ebola outbreak, according to the WHO.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Strain-specific Ebola jab trials to start in DR ' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Strain-specific Ebola jab trials to start in ' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Strain-specific Ebola jab trials to start in ' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "A total of 5,568 deaths out of 11,376 cases have been confirmed in the vast central African country's worst-ever Ebola outbreak, according to the WHO." (Hinglish Arth: डब्ल्यूएचओ के अनुसार, विशाल मध्य अफ्रीकी देश में अब तक के सबसे भयानक इबोला प्रकोप में 11,376 मामलों में से कुल 5,568 मौतों की पुष्टि की गई है।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Strain-specific Ebola jab trials to start in DR Congo next week: WHO"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. If the safety and immune response data from the Phase 2 trial pass the next stage of review, the candidate jabs can move forward to a full-scale...
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "If the safety and immune response data from the Phase 2 trial pass the next stage of review, the candidate jabs can move forward to a full-scale..." (Hinglish Arth: यदि चरण 2 परीक्षण से सुरक्षा और प्रतिरक्षा प्रतिक्रिया डेटा समीक्षा के अगले चरण को पार कर जाता है, तो उम्मीदवार पूर्ण पैमाने पर चरण 3 परीक्षण के लिए आगे बढ़ सकते हैं।)

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The death adds to a worsening national measles outbreak that this week cost the ⁠United States its measles elimination status after 26 years

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Virginia reported its first measles-associated death of 2026 on Friday, November 20, 2026, involving ​a child who tested positive for measles, the state health ‌department said. The department said the child was between ​0 and 4 years old. It did ⁠not disclose additional details, including the child's vaccination status, citing the family's privacy. Measles can cause serious complications, including pneumonia, brain inflammation, ‌complications during pregnancy and death. Virginia has reported 220 measles cases so far in 2026, including 40 ‌among children aged 0 to 4 and ‌75 ⁠among those aged 5 to 12, state health ⁠department data showed as of November 19. Of those cases, 179 were in unvaccinated individuals, 39 were in people whose vaccination status was ​unknown and two ‌were in vaccinated individuals. Virginia health officials have reported increased measles activity driven largely by outbreaks in central region. Buckingham County has reported 127 cases, the highest in ‌the state, while neighbouring Charlotte County has recorded 34 ​cases. The death adds to a worsening national measles outbreak that this week cost the ⁠United States its measles elimination status after 26 years . articles.title: Bihar’s development list is so long that it cannot be counted in one visit to the State: PM
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: PM lays foundation stones for several other development projects in the State at an estimated cost of ₹34,470 crore

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Along with the completion of one year of the National Development Alliance (NDA) regime in Bihar, Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday (November 21, 2026) formally inaugurated the cable-based 9.76 km long six-lane bridge on the Ganga river, constructed at a cost of over ₹5,500 crore, connecting Kacchi Dargah of Patna district to Bidupur in neighbouring Vaishali district. Mr. Modi also laid the foundation stones for several other development projects in the State at an estimated cost of ₹34,470 crore. In his speech of approximately 15 minutes at the Jafarpatti Industrial Area under the Rajapakar block of Vaishali district, Mr. Modi slammed the previous Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) regime, without naming it, and the previous Congress governments at the Centre, for their “non-developmental approach” in the State and in the country, respectively. The PM expressed his happiness on the presence of a large number of youth at the meeting. “Bihar’s development list is so long that it cannot be counted in one visit to the State,” Mr. Modi said. He also listed achievements and welfare measures taken by the NDA government in the State. “Crores of people have come out from poverty in Bihar and in the country during the 12 years of the NDA regime,” he said. “In the Centre’s campaign against poverty, Bihar has played a big role...the lives of crores of people has been eased during the NDA regime in Bihar and at the Centre,” he said. “Over 200 degree colleges, including the Ma Sita Mahila College for women, has been opened in Bihar,” he added. Leaders from all five ruling NDA constituents were present, along with union leaders and senior Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leaders from Bihar. At the dais, Mr. Modi embraced Bihar Health Minister Nishant Kumar, son of former Chief Minister and Janata Dal-United (JD-U) leader Nitish Kumar. Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, Deputy CM Vijay Kumar Choudhary, and Union Minister and Hajipur MP Chirag Paswan also addressed the meeting. “Nitish Setu will make travel between north and south Bihar smoother and faster, offering significant benefits to the people of Patna, Vaishali and surrounding districts,” the CM said. “The decision of Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary to name the bridge Nitish Setu symbolises the immense affection, respect and gratitude that the people of Bihar have for our leader Nitish Kumar ji ,” the JD(U)’s national working president Sanjay Kumar Jha said. Mr. Modi was seen waving a towel at the gathered crowds while inaugurating the bridge, and from an open jeep as it made its way to the dais.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The PM arrived in inclement weather at the Patna airport in a Defence Services aircraft, where he was welcomed by Mr. Kumar. “The bridge is named Nitish Setu,” he said, inaugurating the new, cable-based bridge connecting north and south Bihar over the Ganga river.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #7 of 30 (21 NOV)

📰 Bihar’s development list is so long that it cannot be counted in one visit to the State: PM

📌 Published: 21 Nov 2026, 07:29:17 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: PM lays foundation stones for several other development projects in the State at an estimated cost of ₹34,470 crore

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Along with the completion of one year of the National Development Alliance (NDA) regime in Bihar, Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday (November 21, 2026) formally inaugurated the cable-based 9.76 km long six-lane bridge on the Ganga river, constructed at a cost of over ₹5,500 crore, connecting Kacchi Dargah of Patna district to Bidupur in neighbouring Vaishali district. Mr. Modi also laid the foundation stones for several other development projects in the State at an estimated cost of ₹34,470 crore. In his speech of approximately 15 minutes at the Jafarpatti Industrial Area under the Rajapakar block of Vaishali district, Mr. Modi slammed the previous Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) regime, without naming it, and the previous Congress governments at the Centre, for their “non-developmental approach” in the State and in the country, respectively. The PM expressed his happiness on the presence of a large number of youth at the meeting. “Bihar’s development list is so long that it cannot be counted in one visit to the State,” Mr. Modi said. He also listed achievements and welfare measures taken by the NDA government in the State. “Crores of people have come out from poverty in Bihar and in the country during the 12 years of the NDA regime,” he said. “In the Centre’s campaign against poverty, Bihar has played a big role...the lives of crores of people has been eased during the NDA regime in Bihar and at the Centre,” he said. “Over 200 degree colleges, including the Ma Sita Mahila College for women, has been opened in Bihar,” he added. Leaders from all five ruling NDA constituents were present, along with union leaders and senior Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leaders from Bihar. At the dais, Mr. Modi embraced Bihar Health Minister Nishant Kumar, son of former Chief Minister and Janata Dal-United (JD-U) leader Nitish Kumar. Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, Deputy CM Vijay Kumar Choudhary, and Union Minister and Hajipur MP Chirag Paswan also addressed the meeting. “Nitish Setu will make travel between north and south Bihar smoother and faster, offering significant benefits to the people of Patna, Vaishali and surrounding districts,” the CM said. “The decision of Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary to name the bridge Nitish Setu symbolises the immense affection, respect and gratitude that the people of Bihar have for our leader Nitish Kumar ji ,” the JD(U)’s national working president Sanjay Kumar Jha said. Mr. Modi was seen waving a towel at the gathered crowds while inaugurating the bridge, and from an open jeep as it made its way to the dais.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The PM arrived in inclement weather at the Patna airport in a Defence Services aircraft, where he was welcomed by Mr. Kumar. “The bridge is named Nitish Setu,” he said, inaugurating the new, cable-based bridge connecting north and south Bihar over the Ganga river.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Constitutional (Adjective)
संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप।
✓ Syn: Statutory, Legitimate, Lawful  |  ✖ Ant: Unconstitutional, Illegal, Arbitrary
Developmental (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Developmental' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Foundation (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Foundation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Completion (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Completion' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Bihar’s development list is so long that it cannot be counted in one visit to the State: PM", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. PM lays foundation stones for several other development projects in the State at an estimated cost of ₹34,470 crore.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Bihar’s development list is so long that it cann' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Bihar’s development list is so long that it c' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Bihar’s development list is so long that it c' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "PM lays foundation stones for several other development projects in the State at an estimated cost of ₹34,470 crore." (Hinglish Arth: पीएम ने राज्य में ₹34,470 करोड़ की अनुमानित लागत से कई अन्य विकास परियोजनाओं की आधारशिला रखी)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Bihar’s development list is so long that it cannot be counted in one visit to the State: PM"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. “The bridge is named Nitish Setu,” he said, inaugurating the new, cable-based bridge connecting north and south Bihar over the Ganga river.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "“The bridge is named Nitish Setu,” he said, inaugurating the new, cable-based bridge connecting north and south Bihar over the Ganga river." (Hinglish Arth: गंगा नदी पर उत्तर और दक्षिण बिहार को जोड़ने वाले नए, केबल-आधारित पुल का उद्घाटन करते हुए उन्होंने कहा, "पुल का नाम नीतीश सेतु रखा गया है।")

articles.title: Parel Marian Pilgrimage Centre in Keralam’s Kottayam declared basilica amid large gathering
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: It is the second basilica under the Changanassery Archdiocese. St Mary’s Forane Church at Champakulam was the first to receive the status

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Amid a large gathering of faithful who arrived from various parts of the State and beyond, the Parel Marian Pilgrimage Centre under the Changanassery Archdiocese was officially declared a basilica on Saturday. Archbishop Mar Thomas Tharayil made the formal proclamation at 5 p.m. The church will henceforth be known as Marth Mariam Immaculate Conception Shrine Basilica.The proclamation also coincided with the consecration anniversary of Parel Marth Mariam Valiyapally. The Archbishop described the recognition as a blessing for the region. The consecration ceremonies began at 2 p.m. with a Holy Mass presided over by Mar Joseph Perumthottam, followed by a sermon by Mar Joseph Kallarangatt. The Holy See had elevated the Parel Marian Pilgrimage Centre to the status of a basilica in the name of Pope Leo XIV. The Vatican’s Dicastery for Divine Worship and the Discipline of the Sacraments granted the status. It is the second basilica under the Changanassery Archdiocese. St Mary’s Forane Church at Champakulam was the first to receive the status.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Meanwhile, the District Collector has declared Parel church and the surrounding area within a five-kilometre radius a festival zone until December 13.

📰 Parel Marian Pilgrimage Centre in Keralam’s Kottayam declared basilica amid large gathering

🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: It is the second basilica under the Changanassery Archdiocese. St Mary’s Forane Church at Champakulam was the first to receive the status

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Amid a large gathering of faithful who arrived from various parts of the State and beyond, the Parel Marian Pilgrimage Centre under the Changanassery Archdiocese was officially declared a basilica on Saturday. Archbishop Mar Thomas Tharayil made the formal proclamation at 5 p.m. The church will henceforth be known as Marth Mariam Immaculate Conception Shrine Basilica.The proclamation also coincided with the consecration anniversary of Parel Marth Mariam Valiyapally. The Archbishop described the recognition as a blessing for the region. The consecration ceremonies began at 2 p.m. with a Holy Mass presided over by Mar Joseph Perumthottam, followed by a sermon by Mar Joseph Kallarangatt. The Holy See had elevated the Parel Marian Pilgrimage Centre to the status of a basilica in the name of Pope Leo XIV. The Vatican’s Dicastery for Divine Worship and the Discipline of the Sacraments granted the status. It is the second basilica under the Changanassery Archdiocese. St Mary’s Forane Church at Champakulam was the first to receive the status.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Meanwhile, the District Collector has declared Parel church and the surrounding area within a five-kilometre radius a festival zone until December 13.

articles.title: No new Aasara pensions are being given in State: BRS

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) alleged that the Congress government in the State is on yet another exercise to deceive people in the name of sanctioning new social security (Aasara) pensions as they are being given only in place of the beneficiaries who died and the number of total pensions is indeed lower now, compared to the past.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Speaking to newspersons here on Saturday, Huzurabad MLA Padi Kaushik Reddy said 1,029 pensions were removed in his constituency due to various reasons and no new beneficiary was sanctioned pension afresh. During the BRS regime, there were over 45 lakh Aasara pensioners, but the number was pruned after the Congress assumed power, he said.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: On Friday, Balkonda MLA V. Prashanth Reddy said only 13 persons were given new pensions in his constituency in place of those who died.

🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

2. During the BRS regime, there were over 45 lakh Aasara pensioners, but the number was pruned after the Congress assumed power, he said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: On Friday, Balkonda MLA V. Prashanth Reddy said only 13 persons were given new pensions in his constituency in place of those who died.

articles.title: Belagavi Winter Session to focus on development and North Karnataka issues; presiding officers stress smooth conduct of House proceedings
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The winter session of the Karnataka Legislature, scheduled to be held at the Suvarna Vidhana Soudha in Belagavi from December 2 to 11, will prioritise discussions on development and issues concerning North Karnataka, with the assembly speaker and council chairman calling for meaningful debates and smooth conduct of proceedings

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Winter Session of the Karnataka Legislature, scheduled to be held at the Suvarna Vidhana Soudha in Belagavi from December 2 to 11, will prioritise discussions on development and issues concerning North Karnataka, with the Assembly Speaker G.S. Patil and Legislative Council Chairman Saleem Ahmed calling for meaningful debates and smooth conduct of proceedings. Mr. Patil and Mr. Ahmed issued directions to officials at a preparatory meeting held in Belagavi on Saturday. Speaking to press persons later, Mr. Patil said arrangements relating to accommodation, food, transport, security, electricity and internet connectivity were being reviewed to ensure that the session proceeded without any disruption. All departments and committees had been asked to coordinate and discharge their responsibilities effectively. Emphasising the need to make the session more engaging, he announced plans to organise a book fair, yoga sessions for schoolchildren, interactive programmes using artificial intelligence (AI) for students and cultural events. On protests during the session, Mr. Patil said officials had been instructed to examine and resolve issues that could be addressed at the district and taluk levels. This would help prevent avoidable disruptions to legislative proceedings. He said priority would be given to discussions on development-related issues and necessary steps would be taken to ensure meaningful debates. He also said there was a proposal to construct a legislators’ residential complex on the lines of the Vidhana Soudha legislators’ quarters to provide better accommodation. The proposal would be discussed with the Chief Minister before taking a decision. Another proposal was to hold one House committee meeting every month at the Suvarna Vidhana Soudha to ensure greater utilisation of the building. Mr. Ahmed said the session would provide an opportunity for comprehensive discussions on the State’s development, with particular emphasis on the problems of North Karnataka. Both the ruling party and the Opposition should work together to find solutions to public issues and ensure meaningful proceedings, he said. While protests were an essential part of democracy, they should not affect the functioning of the House. Officials had been directed to hold discussions with those concerned and explore solutions before protests were organised. He said the subjects to be taken up for discussion would be decided after consultations with leaders of the ruling party and the Opposition. Steps would also be taken to improve the attendance of legislators during the session.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Ahmed said the proposal for a legislators’ residential complex was under consideration and a decision would be taken after detailed discussions.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #10 of 30 (21 NOV)

📰 Belagavi Winter Session to focus on development and North Karnataka issues; presiding officers stress smooth conduct of House proceedings

📌 Published: 21 Nov 2026, 07:26:11 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The winter session of the Karnataka Legislature, scheduled to be held at the Suvarna Vidhana Soudha in Belagavi from December 2 to 11, will prioritise discussions on development and issues concerning North Karnataka, with the assembly speaker and council chairman calling for meaningful debates and smooth conduct of proceedings

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Winter Session of the Karnataka Legislature, scheduled to be held at the Suvarna Vidhana Soudha in Belagavi from December 2 to 11, will prioritise discussions on development and issues concerning North Karnataka, with the Assembly Speaker G.S. Patil and Legislative Council Chairman Saleem Ahmed calling for meaningful debates and smooth conduct of proceedings. Mr. Patil and Mr. Ahmed issued directions to officials at a preparatory meeting held in Belagavi on Saturday. Speaking to press persons later, Mr. Patil said arrangements relating to accommodation, food, transport, security, electricity and internet connectivity were being reviewed to ensure that the session proceeded without any disruption. All departments and committees had been asked to coordinate and discharge their responsibilities effectively. Emphasising the need to make the session more engaging, he announced plans to organise a book fair, yoga sessions for schoolchildren, interactive programmes using artificial intelligence (AI) for students and cultural events. On protests during the session, Mr. Patil said officials had been instructed to examine and resolve issues that could be addressed at the district and taluk levels. This would help prevent avoidable disruptions to legislative proceedings. He said priority would be given to discussions on development-related issues and necessary steps would be taken to ensure meaningful debates. He also said there was a proposal to construct a legislators’ residential complex on the lines of the Vidhana Soudha legislators’ quarters to provide better accommodation. The proposal would be discussed with the Chief Minister before taking a decision. Another proposal was to hold one House committee meeting every month at the Suvarna Vidhana Soudha to ensure greater utilisation of the building. Mr. Ahmed said the session would provide an opportunity for comprehensive discussions on the State’s development, with particular emphasis on the problems of North Karnataka. Both the ruling party and the Opposition should work together to find solutions to public issues and ensure meaningful proceedings, he said. While protests were an essential part of democracy, they should not affect the functioning of the House. Officials had been directed to hold discussions with those concerned and explore solutions before protests were organised. He said the subjects to be taken up for discussion would be decided after consultations with leaders of the ruling party and the Opposition. Steps would also be taken to improve the attendance of legislators during the session.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Ahmed said the proposal for a legislators’ residential complex was under consideration and a decision would be taken after detailed discussions.

Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Winter Session of the Karnataka Legislature, scheduled to be held at the Suvarna Vidhana Soudha in Belagavi from December 2 to 11, will prioritise discussions on development and issues concerning North Karnataka, with the Assembly Speaker G.S. Patil and Legislative Council Chairman Saleem Ahmed calling for meaningful debates and smooth conduct of proceedings. Mr. Patil and Mr. Ahmed issued directions to officials at a preparatory meeting held in Belagavi on Saturday. Speaking to press persons later, Mr. Patil said arrangements relating to accommodation, food, transport, security, electricity and internet connectivity were being reviewed to ensure that the session proceeded without any disruption. All departments and committees had been asked to coordinate and discharge their responsibilities effectively. Emphasising the need to make the session more engaging, he announced plans to organise a book fair, yoga sessions for schoolchildren, interactive programmes using artificial intelligence (AI) for students and cultural events. On protests during the session, Mr. Patil said officials had been instructed to examine and resolve issues that could be addressed at the district and taluk levels. This would help prevent avoidable disruptions to legislative proceedings. He said priority would be given to discussions on development-related issues and necessary steps would be taken to ensure meaningful debates. He also said there was a proposal to construct a legislators’ residential complex on the lines of the Vidhana Soudha legislators’ quarters to provide better accommodation. The proposal would be discussed with the Chief Minister before taking a decision. Another proposal was to hold one House committee meeting every month at the Suvarna Vidhana Soudha to ensure greater utilisation of the building. Mr. Ahmed said the session would provide an opportunity for comprehensive discussions on the State’s development, with particular emphasis on the problems of North Karnataka. Both the ruling party and the Opposition should work together to find solutions to public issues and ensure meaningful proceedings, he said. While protests were an essential part of democracy, they should not affect the functioning of the House. Officials had been directed to hold discussions with those concerned and explore solutions before protests were organised. He said the subjects to be taken up for discussion would be decided after consultations with leaders of the ruling party and the Opposition. Steps would also be taken to improve the attendance of legislators during the session.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Ahmed said the proposal for a legislators’ residential complex was under consideration and a decision would be taken after detailed discussions.

articles.title: Rahul putting India’s identity, developmental journey at stake to seize power: Anurag Thakur
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The BJP MP accused Rahul Gandhi of “playing a dangerous gamble” after his remarks on the economy at Columbia University, and said he says things “India’s adversaries, especially Pakistan, like to hear”

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) MP Anurag Thakur on Saturday (November 21, 2026) criticised Rahul Gandhi, alleging that the Congress leader was playing a “dangerous gamble” by putting India’s “identity and developmental journey” at stake to seize power, after failing to gain it through democratic means. “Rahul Gandhi’s current state is like that of a child at a fair who, upon failing to get the toy he desires, starts crying, throwing tantrums and speaking ill of everyone,” Mr. Thakur told reporters in New Delhi, taking a swipe at the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha. “Rahulji, power is not gained through a gamble, it is earned through service,” the former Union Minister said, adding, “(Prime Minister) Narendra Modi has rendered that service. He came to power through penance, austerity and sacrifice and is serving the people.” His remarks came against the backdrop of Mr. Gandhi’s “compromised PM” jibe at Mr. Modi and his remarks on the government’s policies during a recent visit to the United States. Speaking at a fireside chat at Columbia University in New York earlier this week, Mr. Gandhi said India was sitting on an “economic disaster”, with massive unemployment, a broken manufacturing base and deep-rooted problems in its education system, warning that the country risked getting into serious trouble if it continued on the current economic path. He also claimed India’s economic model “stopped giving results almost a decade ago”, and criticised initiatives such as “Make in India” and “Start-up India”, claiming they had failed to revive the country’s “broken” economic backbone. Mr. Thakur criticised Mr. Gandhi for “abusing India and speaking ill of it” during his foreign visit. “Having failed to attain power through democratic means, Rahul Gandhi is resorting to cheap tactics to seize it,” he said. In a post on X, he said: “In his pursuit of power, Rahul Gandhi is playing a dangerous gamble in which he has staked the nation’s identity, its developmental journey, and the trust of 1.40 crore Indians.” Citing data to underscore India’s progress under Mr. Modi’s leadership, Mr. Thakur said: “One statistic after another shows that the world looks towards India and India’s prime minister with hope. But while opposing Modiji, Rahul Gandhi has started opposing India. He has started playing with India’s interests, striking at India’s pride and the trust of Indians, and wagering them in a gamble.”

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “Why does Rahul Gandhi say things that India’s adversaries, especially Pakistan, like to hear? Rahul Gandhi’s friends sitting in Pakistan must be happy hearing this, but Indians are not,” he said. He said the foundation of Mr. Gandhi’s politics was “despair”, while the foundation of Mr. Modi’s politics was “development and trust”.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #11 of 30 (21 NOV)

📰 Rahul putting India’s identity, developmental journey at stake to seize power: Anurag Thakur

📌 Published: 21 Nov 2026, 07:26:03 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The BJP MP accused Rahul Gandhi of “playing a dangerous gamble” after his remarks on the economy at Columbia University, and said he says things “India’s adversaries, especially Pakistan, like to hear”

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) MP Anurag Thakur on Saturday (November 21, 2026) criticised Rahul Gandhi, alleging that the Congress leader was playing a “dangerous gamble” by putting India’s “identity and developmental journey” at stake to seize power, after failing to gain it through democratic means. “Rahul Gandhi’s current state is like that of a child at a fair who, upon failing to get the toy he desires, starts crying, throwing tantrums and speaking ill of everyone,” Mr. Thakur told reporters in New Delhi, taking a swipe at the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha. “Rahulji, power is not gained through a gamble, it is earned through service,” the former Union Minister said, adding, “(Prime Minister) Narendra Modi has rendered that service. He came to power through penance, austerity and sacrifice and is serving the people.” His remarks came against the backdrop of Mr. Gandhi’s “compromised PM” jibe at Mr. Modi and his remarks on the government’s policies during a recent visit to the United States. Speaking at a fireside chat at Columbia University in New York earlier this week, Mr. Gandhi said India was sitting on an “economic disaster”, with massive unemployment, a broken manufacturing base and deep-rooted problems in its education system, warning that the country risked getting into serious trouble if it continued on the current economic path. He also claimed India’s economic model “stopped giving results almost a decade ago”, and criticised initiatives such as “Make in India” and “Start-up India”, claiming they had failed to revive the country’s “broken” economic backbone. Mr. Thakur criticised Mr. Gandhi for “abusing India and speaking ill of it” during his foreign visit. “Having failed to attain power through democratic means, Rahul Gandhi is resorting to cheap tactics to seize it,” he said. In a post on X, he said: “In his pursuit of power, Rahul Gandhi is playing a dangerous gamble in which he has staked the nation’s identity, its developmental journey, and the trust of 1.40 crore Indians.” Citing data to underscore India’s progress under Mr. Modi’s leadership, Mr. Thakur said: “One statistic after another shows that the world looks towards India and India’s prime minister with hope. But while opposing Modiji, Rahul Gandhi has started opposing India. He has started playing with India’s interests, striking at India’s pride and the trust of Indians, and wagering them in a gamble.”

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “Why does Rahul Gandhi say things that India’s adversaries, especially Pakistan, like to hear? Rahul Gandhi’s friends sitting in Pakistan must be happy hearing this, but Indians are not,” he said. He said the foundation of Mr. Gandhi’s politics was “despair”, while the foundation of Mr. Modi’s politics was “development and trust”.

🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Rahul putting India’s identity, developmental journey at stake to seize power: Anurag Thakur", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. The BJP MP accused Rahul Gandhi of “playing a dangerous gamble” after his remarks on the economy at Columbia University, and said he says things...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Rahul putting India’s identity, developmental jo' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Rahul putting India’s identity, developmental' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Rahul putting India’s identity, developmental' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The BJP MP accused Rahul Gandhi of “playing a dangerous gamble” after his remarks on the economy at Columbia University, and said he says things..." (Hinglish Arth: भाजपा सांसद ने कोलंबिया विश्वविद्यालय में अर्थव्यवस्था पर अपनी टिप्पणी के बाद राहुल गांधी पर "खतरनाक जुआ खेलने" का आरोप लगाया, और कहा कि वह ऐसी बातें कहते हैं जो "भारत के विरोधी, विशेष रूप से पाकिस्तान सुनना पसंद करते हैं")
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Rahul putting India’s identity, developmental journey at stake to seize power: Anurag Thakur"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Modi’s politics was “development and trust”.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Modi’s politics was “development and trust”." (Hinglish Arth: मोदी की राजनीति "विकास और विश्वास" थी।)

articles.title: India, Finland seek to deepen economic ties through startup cooperation: Envoy Mikko Kivikoski
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: "We want to engage more with the Indian startup actors. And here we see the startup sector, startup ecosystems, as an important part of that cooperation," Mikki Kivikoski said

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: “India and Finland are looking to deepen economic cooperation by strengthening ties between their startup ecosystems and promoting greater two-way investment,” Finnish Ambassador to India Mikko Kivikoski has said. "We want to engage more with the Indian startup actors. And of course, at the end of the day, this is all about advancing the economic cooperation between our countries. And here we see the startup sector, startup ecosystems, as an important part of that cooperation," Mr. Kivikoski told PTI . The Ambassador was speaking at an unconventional startup event held at the Embassy of Finland in New Delhi on Friday (November 20, 2026), where entrepreneurs stepped into an ice-cold pool to pitch their ideas, drawing on Finland's winter-swimming tradition. "We have quite a long tradition in Finland for these kinds of events," Mr. Kivikoski said. "This year has been record-high when it comes to interaction and engagement between Finland and India," he said, referring to visits by the Finnish Prime Minister and President, as well as meetings between the leaders of the two countries. The Ambassador said the two sides agreed to elevate their bilateral relationship to a Strategic Partnership in Digitalisation and Sustainability during Finnish President Alexander Stubb's state visit to India in March. Prime Minister Narendra Modi met his Finnish counterpart, Petteri Orpo, in New Delhi on the sidelines of the AI Impact Summit in February and in Oslo on the margins of the 3rd India-Nordic Summit in May. Mr. Kivikoski also referred to the visits to Finland by India's External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar and Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal during the summer. "We see India as a trusted partner when it comes to the Indo-Pacific area," he said. The Ambassador said the India-Finland relationship was increasingly moving beyond conventional trade towards a partnership involving investments and people-to-people exchanges. "What we are seeing already, and what is happening between the European Union and India and between India and Finland, is that we are now talking about partnership. It's not anymore about me selling something to you and you selling something to me," he said.

"We see India as a trusted partner when it comes to the Indo-Pacific area," he said. "What we are seeing already, and what is happening between the European Union and India and between India and Finland, is that we are now talking about partnership. It's not anymore about me selling something to you and you selling something to me," he said.

"We want to engage more with the Indian startup actors. And of course, at the end of the day, this is all about advancing the economic cooperation between our countries. And here we see the startup sector, startup ecosystems, as an important part of that cooperation," Mr. Kivikoski told PTI . The Ambassador was speaking at an unconventional startup event held at the Embassy of Finland in New Delhi on Friday (November 20, 2026), where entrepreneurs stepped into an ice-cold pool to pitch their ideas, drawing on Finland's winter-swimming tradition. Prime Minister Narendra Modi met his Finnish counterpart, Petteri Orpo, in New Delhi on the sidelines of the AI Impact Summit in February and in Oslo on the margins of the 3rd India-Nordic Summit in May. Mr. Kivikoski also referred to the visits to Finland by India's External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar and Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal during the summer. "We see India as a trusted partner when it comes to the Indo-Pacific area," he said. The Ambassador said the India-Finland relationship was increasingly moving beyond conventional trade towards a partnership involving investments and people-to-people exchanges. "What we are seeing already, and what is happening between the European Union and India and between India and Finland, is that we are now talking about partnership. It's not anymore about me selling something to you and you selling something to me," he said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: "There are more and more Finnish companies coming to the Indian market and more and more Indian companies going to the Finnish market. And of course we hope, and we are confident, that this dynamism will continue in the future," he said.

• 1. Core Context & Background: "We want to engage more with the Indian startup actors. And here we see the startup sector, startup ecosystems, as an important part of that cooperation," Mikki Kivikoski said
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: “India and Finland are looking to deepen economic cooperation by strengthening ties between their startup ecosystems and promoting greater two-way investment,” Finnish Ambassador to India Mikko Kivikoski has said. "We want to engage more with the Indian startup actors. And of course, at the end of the day, this is all about advancing the economic cooperation between our countries. And here we see the startup sector, startup ecosystems, as an important part of that cooperation," Mr. Kivikoski told PTI . The Ambassador was speaking at an unconventional startup event held at the Embassy of Finland in New Delhi on Friday (November 20, 2026), where entrepreneurs stepped into an ice-cold pool to pitch their ideas, drawing on Finland's winter-swimming tradition. "We have quite a long tradition in Finland for these kinds of events," Mr. Kivikoski said. "This year has been record-high when it comes to interaction and engagement between Finland and India," he said, referring to visits by the Finnish Prime Minister and President, as well as meetings between the leaders of the two countries. The Ambassador said the two sides agreed to elevate their bilateral relationship to a Strategic Partnership in Digitalisation and Sustainability during Finnish President Alexander Stubb's state visit to India in March. Prime Minister Narendra Modi met his Finnish counterpart, Petteri Orpo, in New Delhi on the sidelines of the AI Impact Summit in February and in Oslo on the margins of the 3rd India-Nordic Summit in May. Mr. Kivikoski also referred to the visits to Finland by India's External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar and Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal during the summer. "We see India as a trusted partner when it comes to the Indo-Pacific area," he said. The Ambassador said the India-Finland relationship was increasingly moving beyond conventional trade towards a partnership involving investments and people-to-people exchanges. "What we are seeing already, and what is happening between the European Union and India and between India and Finland, is that we are now talking about partnership. It's not anymore about me selling something to you and you selling something to me," he said.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: "There are more and more Finnish companies coming to the Indian market and more and more Indian companies going to the Finnish market. And of course we hope, and we are confident, that this dynamism will continue in the future," he said.

articles.title: Finland detects drone attack on Russian cargo ship in Baltic
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The Finnish Defence Ministry did not specify who was behind the drone strike, but Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said in a message “War is spilling over into our immediate vicinity... Ukraine has the right to fight back against the aggressor”

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Finland’s military detected a drone attack on Saturday morning (November 21, 2026) on a Russian cargo ship in the eastern Baltic Sea, which caused the vessel to catch fire, the Nordic country’s authorities said. The Finnish Defence Ministry did not specify who was behind the drone strike, but Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said in a message on X: “War is spilling over into our immediate vicinity... Ukraine has the right to fight back against the aggressor.” Fighting off a Russian invasion now in its fifth year, Ukraine has stepped up its long-range barrages against Russia far beyond the front lines. “On Saturday morning, the Finnish Defence Forces detected a drone attack against a Russian cargo vessel west of Suursaari, in the eastern Gulf of Finland, in international waters,” the Ministry said in a statement. According to Finnish border guards dispatched to the scene the ship caught fire and began drifting towards Finnish waters after the strike. “The situation currently poses no danger to other vessels,” the border service said in a press release. Authorities gave no immediate details of the boat’s crew. Finland immediately informed NATO of the strike, the Defence Ministry said. It said temporary restrictions were enforced in the airspace and maritime area of the eastern part of the Gulf.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Baltic Sea has become a potential flashpoint in the wake of Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine, with Western countries accusing Moscow of conducting a “hybrid war” in the strategic waterway.

articles.title: U.S. court dispatches summonses to Doval, Goel in Pannun case
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The Indian Code of Civil Procedure permits summonses issued by foreign civil courts designated by notification of the Central Government of India to be transmitted to Indian courts and served as though issued by those courts

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A U.S. court has dispatched summonses to National Security Adviser Ajit Doval and former Research and Analysis Wing (RAW) Director Samant Goel to be served through Indian courts in connection with a case involving an alleged murder plot against Khalistani separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun. Pannun, legal counsel for the banned organisation Sikhs for Justice (SFJ) who is wanted in India on several terror charges, has filed the civil lawsuit seeking damages over an alleged attempt on his life. The clerk of the Southern District Court of New York said that the summonses were sent through courier company FedEx to the Patiala House Court, Tis Hazari Court, and the Dwarka District Court in New Delhi on Friday (November 20, 2026). The Southern District Court of New York had ordered earlier this month that summonses be issued to Mr. Doval and Mr. Goel after noting that Pannun’s earlier attempts to personally serve notices on the two were blocked. “The Court respectfully requests the assistance of receiving Indian courts in effecting service of process upon the defendants in this civil action pending before this court,” read an order by Judge Katherine Polk Failla. The judge cited the Hague Convention and relevant sections of the Indian Code of Civil Procedure to state that foreign courts can serve summonses on Mr. Doval and Mr. Goel through Indian courts. The Indian Code of Civil Procedure permits summonses issued by foreign civil courts notified by the Union government to be transmitted to Indian courts and served as though issued by those courts. The order states that standard service through India's central authority under the Hague Convention was attempted but rejected. The Court then authorised alternative service under Article 19 of the Hague Convention and relevant sections of the Code of Civil Procedure. The U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation’s (FBI) inquiry into the alleged the assassination plot against Pannun in June 2023 had pointed to Indian businessman Nikhil Gupta, and to conversations with senior Indian intelligence officials, including Vikash Yadav, regarding a conspiracy to hire a hitman to kill Pannun in New York.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Gupta, 55, was sentenced to 235 months in prison by a U.S. court on Friday (November 20, 2026) after pleading guilty earlier this year to charges of murder-for-hire, conspiracy to commit murder-for-hire, and conspiracy to commit money laundering.

📰 U.S. court dispatches summonses to Doval, Goel in Pannun case

📌 Published: 21 Nov 2026, 08:35:10 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The Indian Code of Civil Procedure permits summonses issued by foreign civil courts designated by notification of the Central Government of India to be transmitted to Indian courts and served as though issued by those courts

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A U.S. court has dispatched summonses to National Security Adviser Ajit Doval and former Research and Analysis Wing (RAW) Director Samant Goel to be served through Indian courts in connection with a case involving an alleged murder plot against Khalistani separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun. Pannun, legal counsel for the banned organisation Sikhs for Justice (SFJ) who is wanted in India on several terror charges, has filed the civil lawsuit seeking damages over an alleged attempt on his life. The clerk of the Southern District Court of New York said that the summonses were sent through courier company FedEx to the Patiala House Court, Tis Hazari Court, and the Dwarka District Court in New Delhi on Friday (November 20, 2026). The Southern District Court of New York had ordered earlier this month that summonses be issued to Mr. Doval and Mr. Goel after noting that Pannun’s earlier attempts to personally serve notices on the two were blocked. “The Court respectfully requests the assistance of receiving Indian courts in effecting service of process upon the defendants in this civil action pending before this court,” read an order by Judge Katherine Polk Failla. The judge cited the Hague Convention and relevant sections of the Indian Code of Civil Procedure to state that foreign courts can serve summonses on Mr. Doval and Mr. Goel through Indian courts. The Indian Code of Civil Procedure permits summonses issued by foreign civil courts notified by the Union government to be transmitted to Indian courts and served as though issued by those courts. The order states that standard service through India's central authority under the Hague Convention was attempted but rejected. The Court then authorised alternative service under Article 19 of the Hague Convention and relevant sections of the Code of Civil Procedure. The U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation’s (FBI) inquiry into the alleged the assassination plot against Pannun in June 2023 had pointed to Indian businessman Nikhil Gupta, and to conversations with senior Indian intelligence officials, including Vikash Yadav, regarding a conspiracy to hire a hitman to kill Pannun in New York.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Gupta, 55, was sentenced to 235 months in prison by a U.S. court on Friday (November 20, 2026) after pleading guilty earlier this year to charges of murder-for-hire, conspiracy to commit murder-for-hire, and conspiracy to commit money laundering.

articles.title: European Union proposes tax on Big Tech to boost budget
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: European Council president Antonio Costa unveiled a new spending proposal that slashes by 204 billion euros a plan initially put forward by the European Commission

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The European Union (EU) put forward plans to tax the world's biggest digital companies to fund its next budget on Saturday (November 21, 2026), as it seeks to bridge divisions among member states over the bloc's long-term funding. European Council president Antonio Costa unveiled a new spending proposal that slashes by 204 billion euros ($224 billion) a plan initially put forward by the European Commission, which some countries had slammed as too onerous. "I believe this proposal can bring us closer to a final agreement," Mr. Costa told a press conference in Brussels. EU countries have been squabbling over the size of the next budget, with Germany leading calls for major cuts after the Commission last year proposed a two-trillion-euro budget for the 2028-2034 period. Berlin criticised a revised proposal published last month that suggested slashing the bloc's future seven-year budget by 140 billion euros. Mr. Costa, who represents the EU's 27 states, is seeking to reach a deal by the end of the year balancing contributions from member states with new sources of revenue for the bloc. Among these could be a tax on digital firms that the draft Mr. Costa presented on Saturday says will concern companies with an annual turnover for digital activities of at least 50 million euros in the EU as well as a global turnover of more than 750 million euros. They would be subjected to "an annual contribution corresponding to 3% of the annual net turnover from online advertising, digital intermediation services and user-generated data", according to documents shared by the council. The plan is likely to provoke U.S. President Donald Trump's ire since his administration has reacted angrily to EU fines and moves against Big Tech under its content and competition rules in recent years. The draft also includes plans for a levy on electronic waste and higher tobacco taxes.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The document will be at the centre of hours of fraught talks when EU leaders meet in Brussels next week.
