🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #11 of 30 (21 NOV)

📰 Shared civilisational knowledge should be harnessed by nations: Shekhawat

📌 Published: 21 Nov 2026, 11:12:14 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Historical connections have played a significant role in bringing countries closer, the Union Culture Minister says at the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Union Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat on Saturday (November 21, 2026) said shared civilisational knowledge and heritage should be harnessed by nations to advance collective efforts through dialogue, institutional partnerships, cultural exchange and cooperation. While chairing the first and second joint sessions on ‘Civilisational and Cultural Expressions’ on the second day of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum, Mr. Shekhawat said historical connections had played a significant role in bringing countries closer. They also highlighted the potential of cultural cooperation in fostering mutual understanding, trust and friendship, he said. Civilisations were not merely legacies of the past but “living traditions whose knowledge continues to illuminate our present and inspire future generations”, the Minister said, expressing confidence that the forum would deepen connections among SCO member States. Pakistan’s Federal Minister for Climate Change and Environmental Coordination, Musaddiq Masood Malik, who is leading his country’s delegation, said dialogue took place amid diversity and that it was important to recognise that distinct identities had their own significance. Referring to archaeological remains from different periods discovered during excavations at the historic Purana Qila, where the forum is being held, he said the fort in which the delegates were seated was, in itself, a story. Its foundation was laid by Humayun, who belonged to the Timurid dynasty and had arrived from Central Asia. Its construction was further carried forward by Sher Shah Suri, who came from Afghanistan. Thus, within a single wall, one could find the art of two different rulers, two cultural layers and traces of two traditions, Mr. Masood Malik said, adding that this was the very diversity that the delegates had been invited to celebrate. He appreciated the description of the event as ‘Tehzeeb Ki Guftagu’, or ‘Dialogue of Civilisations’. “Delhi has not been diminished by civilisations and people coming from outside; rather, it has grown stronger,” he said, adding that dialogue took place amid diversity. Referring to his conversation with Mr. Shekhawat the previous day, he said the layers of history and culture had been an integral part of the region’s way of life for thousands of years. The participants had gathered to bring together multiple voices and identities and facilitate the free flow of ideas among them, the Pakistan Minister said. Mr. Masood Malik was addressing one of the numerous sessions held on the second day of the forum, including those on art and architecture, and trade relations. Ministers, senior representatives, academicians, historians and experts from SCO member States and dialogue partner countries participated.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The SCO Civilisational Forum is being organised by the Ministry of Culture and the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA). The Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts is the knowledge partner for the event.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Environmental (Adjective)
पर्यावरण, प्रकृति और हमारे पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र (Ecosystem) से संबंधित।
✓ Syn: Ecological, Biospheric, Natural  |  ✖ Ant: Industrial, Polluting, Synthetic
Institutional (Adjective)
संस्थागत — देश की संवैधानिक या सरकारी संस्थाओं के नियमों और ढांचे से जुड़ा हुआ।
✓ Syn: Systemic, Organizational, Constitutional  |  ✖ Ant: Individual, Informal, Unorganized
Civilisational (Adjective)
सभ्यतागत — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Civilisational' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Archaeological (Adjective)
पुरातत्व — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Archaeological' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Shared civilisational knowledge should be harnessed by nations: Shekhawat", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Historical connections have played a significant role in bringing countries closer, the Union Culture Minister says at the SCO Civilisational...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Shared civilisational knowledge should be harnes' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Shared civilisational knowledge should be har' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Shared civilisational knowledge should be har' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Historical connections have played a significant role in bringing countries closer, the Union Culture Minister says at the SCO Civilisational..." (Hinglish Arth: केंद्रीय संस्कृति मंत्री ने एससीओ सभ्यता संवाद मंच में कहा कि ऐतिहासिक संबंधों ने देशों को करीब लाने में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाई है)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Shared civilisational knowledge should be harnessed by nations: Shekhawat"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. The Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts is the knowledge partner for the event.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "The Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts is the knowledge partner for the event." (Hinglish Arth: इंदिरा गांधी राष्ट्रीय कला केंद्र इस आयोजन का ज्ञान भागीदार है।)

articles.title: Odisha government orders inquiry into foreign visits by former CM Naveen Patnaik, aide Pandian
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Social activists allege that RTI replies concerning the visits to Japan and Italy were suspicious, unclear and incomplete

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Odisha government on Saturday (November 21, 2026) ordered an inquiry into visits by former Chief Minister Naveen Patnaik and his close aide, retired IAS officer V.K. Pandian, to Japan and Italy during 2022-23 and 2023-24. As per the directions issued by Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi, the Principal Secretary of the General Administration Department will conduct the investigation. The inquiry was ordered after social activists alleged that the expenditure details relating to the visits to Japan and Italy were suspicious, unclear and incomplete, the Chief Minister’s Office (CMO) said here on Saturday (November 21, 2026). Based on information obtained through various Right to Information (RTI) applications, activists had filed a complaint alleging that Biju Janata Dal chief Mr. Patnaik, IAS officer Mr. Pandian and IPS officer Ravikant had undertaken several foreign visits during 2022-23 and 2023-24, when Mr. Patnaik was the Chief Minister. The CMO further said that the activists had alleged that information regarding these visits was deliberately kept confidential, resulting in inconsistencies and discrepancies in the available records. “In view of these allegations, Mr. Majhi has directed an investigation to ascertain the facts and bring the truth to light,” the CMO said. “We had sought details of the visits by former CM Mr. Patnaik, Mr. Pandian and Mr. Ravi Kant, who was then Resident Commissioner for Odisha government and posted at Delhi to Rome from June 20 to 25 in 2022,” said RTI activist Pradip Pradhan, who had filed a complaint with the State government regarding the foreign visit. “We got suspicious about the visit because ₹83 lakh was spent from the State exchequer. The bill for the visit was generated by office of Odisha’s Resident Commissioner, New Delhi and it was footed by Parliamentary Affairs department of the State,” he said. “A group of RTI activists including me had moved General Administration, Home Department, Transport Department and Parliamentary Affairs of Odisha Government. Even information was sought from Indian Embassy at Rome. None of them had provided any information stating that the report regarding the visits were not available with them,” Mr. Pradhan alleged.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The complaint stated that the State had decided to send a delegation of senior functionaries to Japan, led by former Chief Minister Mr. Patnaik, to attract investments. Odisha’s industrial promotion body, IPICOL, was entrusted with coordinating the programme.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #12 of 30 (21 NOV)

📰 Odisha government orders inquiry into foreign visits by former CM Naveen Patnaik, aide Pandian

📌 Published: 21 Nov 2026, 11:05:50 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Social activists allege that RTI replies concerning the visits to Japan and Italy were suspicious, unclear and incomplete

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Odisha government on Saturday (November 21, 2026) ordered an inquiry into visits by former Chief Minister Naveen Patnaik and his close aide, retired IAS officer V.K. Pandian, to Japan and Italy during 2022-23 and 2023-24. As per the directions issued by Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi, the Principal Secretary of the General Administration Department will conduct the investigation. The inquiry was ordered after social activists alleged that the expenditure details relating to the visits to Japan and Italy were suspicious, unclear and incomplete, the Chief Minister’s Office (CMO) said here on Saturday (November 21, 2026). Based on information obtained through various Right to Information (RTI) applications, activists had filed a complaint alleging that Biju Janata Dal chief Mr. Patnaik, IAS officer Mr. Pandian and IPS officer Ravikant had undertaken several foreign visits during 2022-23 and 2023-24, when Mr. Patnaik was the Chief Minister. The CMO further said that the activists had alleged that information regarding these visits was deliberately kept confidential, resulting in inconsistencies and discrepancies in the available records. “In view of these allegations, Mr. Majhi has directed an investigation to ascertain the facts and bring the truth to light,” the CMO said. “We had sought details of the visits by former CM Mr. Patnaik, Mr. Pandian and Mr. Ravi Kant, who was then Resident Commissioner for Odisha government and posted at Delhi to Rome from June 20 to 25 in 2022,” said RTI activist Pradip Pradhan, who had filed a complaint with the State government regarding the foreign visit. “We got suspicious about the visit because ₹83 lakh was spent from the State exchequer. The bill for the visit was generated by office of Odisha’s Resident Commissioner, New Delhi and it was footed by Parliamentary Affairs department of the State,” he said. “A group of RTI activists including me had moved General Administration, Home Department, Transport Department and Parliamentary Affairs of Odisha Government. Even information was sought from Indian Embassy at Rome. None of them had provided any information stating that the report regarding the visits were not available with them,” Mr. Pradhan alleged.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The complaint stated that the State had decided to send a delegation of senior functionaries to Japan, led by former Chief Minister Mr. Patnaik, to attract investments. Odisha’s industrial promotion body, IPICOL, was entrusted with coordinating the programme.

Administration (Noun)
प्रशासन — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Administration' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial

articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: Social activists allege that RTI replies concerning the visits to Japan and Italy were suspicious, unclear and incomplete
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Odisha government on Saturday (November 21, 2026) ordered an inquiry into visits by former Chief Minister Naveen Patnaik and his close aide, retired IAS officer V.K. Pandian, to Japan and Italy during 2022-23 and 2023-24. As per the directions issued by Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi, the Principal Secretary of the General Administration Department will conduct the investigation. The inquiry was ordered after social activists alleged that the expenditure details relating to the visits to Japan and Italy were suspicious, unclear and incomplete, the Chief Minister’s Office (CMO) said here on Saturday (November 21, 2026). Based on information obtained through various Right to Information (RTI) applications, activists had filed a complaint alleging that Biju Janata Dal chief Mr. Patnaik, IAS officer Mr. Pandian and IPS officer Ravikant had undertaken several foreign visits during 2022-23 and 2023-24, when Mr. Patnaik was the Chief Minister. The CMO further said that the activists had alleged that information regarding these visits was deliberately kept confidential, resulting in inconsistencies and discrepancies in the available records. “In view of these allegations, Mr. Majhi has directed an investigation to ascertain the facts and bring the truth to light,” the CMO said. “We had sought details of the visits by former CM Mr. Patnaik, Mr. Pandian and Mr. Ravi Kant, who was then Resident Commissioner for Odisha government and posted at Delhi to Rome from June 20 to 25 in 2022,” said RTI activist Pradip Pradhan, who had filed a complaint with the State government regarding the foreign visit. “We got suspicious about the visit because ₹83 lakh was spent from the State exchequer. The bill for the visit was generated by office of Odisha’s Resident Commissioner, New Delhi and it was footed by Parliamentary Affairs department of the State,” he said. “A group of RTI activists including me had moved General Administration, Home Department, Transport Department and Parliamentary Affairs of Odisha Government. Even information was sought from Indian Embassy at Rome. None of them had provided any information stating that the report regarding the visits were not available with them,” Mr. Pradhan alleged.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The complaint stated that the State had decided to send a delegation of senior functionaries to Japan, led by former Chief Minister Mr. Patnaik, to attract investments. Odisha’s industrial promotion body, IPICOL, was entrusted with coordinating the programme.

articles.title: Iran wants diplomacy to end war, says Araghchi as U.S. rejects terms
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Tehran needs guarantees that Washington is serious about negotiations, says Iran’s Foreign Minister; highly enriched uranium should be kept inside Iran, he says, adding that ‘a fair solution’ could be reached; U.S. denies Iran fired at an F-16

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran still hoped diplomacy could end its war with the United States, while U.S. President Donald Trump said Iran wanted a deal but one that was not acceptable to him. Mr. Araghchi told the state-owned Iran newspaper that Tehran was seeking “an agreement that would ensure there was no further war” and wanted guarantees that Washington was serious about negotiations before proceeding further, adding that Iran had discussed with mediators the form and nature of confidence-building measures. The remarks came as diplomatic efforts continued to try to end a conflict that has destabilised the West Asia, disrupted shipping, driven up global energy prices and drawn in countries across the region. The Foreign Minister said Iran’s red lines included keeping enriched uranium in the country, though he added that he believed “a fair solution” could be reached. “They want to make a deal, but they don’t want to make a deal that’s acceptable to me,” Mr. Trump said at a press conference on Friday. The United States and Israel attacked Iran on February 28, prompting Tehran to strike Israel and Gulf states hosting U.S. military bases. Qatari and Iranian officials met on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) in talks aimed at “bridging perspectives and narrowing the gap between proposals presented on the ground,” a spokesperson for Qatar’s Foreign Ministry said. U.S. Central Command on Saturday (November 20, 2026) denied an Iranian account that its forces had fired a missile at a U.S. F-16 fighter jet over the Gulf, damaging the aircraft and forcing it to make an emergency landing. Iranian state media earlier reported that the country’s air defence systems targeted the aircraft on Friday evening, causing it to abort its mission and land at a nearby airport.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “Iran did not attack a US F-16 fighter aircraft yesterday — at all,” Central Command said in a statement.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #22 of 30 (21 NOV)

📰 Iran wants diplomacy to end war, says Araghchi as U.S. rejects terms

📌 Published: 21 Nov 2026, 11:23:45 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Tehran needs guarantees that Washington is serious about negotiations, says Iran’s Foreign Minister; highly enriched uranium should be kept inside Iran, he says, adding that ‘a fair solution’ could be reached; U.S. denies Iran fired at an F-16

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran still hoped diplomacy could end its war with the United States, while U.S. President Donald Trump said Iran wanted a deal but one that was not acceptable to him. Mr. Araghchi told the state-owned Iran newspaper that Tehran was seeking “an agreement that would ensure there was no further war” and wanted guarantees that Washington was serious about negotiations before proceeding further, adding that Iran had discussed with mediators the form and nature of confidence-building measures. The remarks came as diplomatic efforts continued to try to end a conflict that has destabilised the West Asia, disrupted shipping, driven up global energy prices and drawn in countries across the region. The Foreign Minister said Iran’s red lines included keeping enriched uranium in the country, though he added that he believed “a fair solution” could be reached. “They want to make a deal, but they don’t want to make a deal that’s acceptable to me,” Mr. Trump said at a press conference on Friday. The United States and Israel attacked Iran on February 28, prompting Tehran to strike Israel and Gulf states hosting U.S. military bases. Qatari and Iranian officials met on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) in talks aimed at “bridging perspectives and narrowing the gap between proposals presented on the ground,” a spokesperson for Qatar’s Foreign Ministry said. U.S. Central Command on Saturday (November 20, 2026) denied an Iranian account that its forces had fired a missile at a U.S. F-16 fighter jet over the Gulf, damaging the aircraft and forcing it to make an emergency landing. Iranian state media earlier reported that the country’s air defence systems targeted the aircraft on Friday evening, causing it to abort its mission and land at a nearby airport.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “Iran did not attack a US F-16 fighter aircraft yesterday — at all,” Central Command said in a statement.

✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Diplomatic (Adjective)
कूटनीतिक — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Diplomatic' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Conference (Noun)
सम्मेलन — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Conference' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🌐 International & Geopolitics passage on "Iran wants diplomacy to end war, says Araghchi as U.S. rejects terms", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Tehran needs guarantees that Washington is serious about negotiations, says Iran’s Foreign Minister; highly enriched uranium should be kept inside...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Iran wants diplomacy to end war, says Araghchi a' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Iran wants diplomacy to end war, says Araghch' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Iran wants diplomacy to end war, says Araghch' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Tehran needs guarantees that Washington is serious about negotiations, says Iran’s Foreign Minister; highly enriched uranium should be kept inside..." (Hinglish Arth: ईरान के विदेश मंत्री का कहना है कि तेहरान को इस बात की गारंटी चाहिए कि वाशिंगटन बातचीत को लेकर गंभीर है; उनका कहना है कि अत्यधिक संवर्धित यूरेनियम को ईरान के अंदर ही रखा जाना चाहिए, साथ ही उन्होंने कहा कि 'एक उचित समाधान' तक पहुंचा जा सकता है; हम।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Iran wants diplomacy to end war, says Araghchi as U.S. rejects terms"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. “Iran did not attack a US F-16 fighter aircraft yesterday — at all,” Central Command said in a statement.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "“Iran did not attack a US F-16 fighter aircraft yesterday — at all,” Central Command said in a statement." (Hinglish Arth: सेंट्रल कमांड ने एक बयान में कहा, "ईरान ने कल अमेरिकी एफ-16 लड़ाकू विमान पर बिल्कुल भी हमला नहीं किया।")

articles.title: Sri Lanka's organised crime bill gets Supreme Court nod
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: In Sri Lanka, citizens can challenge a Bill's constitutionality in the Supreme Court within one week of its introduction in Parliament. The Bill had earlier faced 20 petitions in the Supreme Court challenging its constitutionality

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Sri Lanka's proposed Prevention of Organised Crimes Bill has received the Supreme Court's nod, which ruled that its provisions are "not inconsistent" with the Constitution, Speaker Jagath Wickremaratna told Parliament on Saturday (November 21, 2026). The Bill, tabled in Parliament on October 20, has drawn criticism from local and international rights groups concerned that its provisions could undermine fundamental rights and grant sweeping powers to law enforcement agencies. In Sri Lanka, citizens can challenge a Bill's constitutionality in the Supreme Court within one week of its introduction in Parliament. The Bill had earlier faced 20 petitions in the Supreme Court challenging its constitutionality. The Speaker on Saturday (November 21, 2026) confirmed the Supreme Court's nod for the Bill and listed the clauses it directed Parliament to amend. "The clauses in the Bill are not inconsistent with the Constitution and may be passed by a simple majority of Parliament, subject to making the amendment at the committee stage," Mr. Wickremaratna said. He said Clause 6, which allowed the prosecution of an individual who is not a member of a criminal gang, should be deleted, citing the Court's directions. Criticism of the Bill has centred on its broad definition of organised crime and provisions that could allow authorities to identify individuals as gang members based on their appearance or associations. Sri Lanka's Human Rights Commission called for the Bill's withdrawal, while the Bar Association of Sri Lanka raised concerns about its impact on fundamental rights and safeguards for judicial oversight. Rights body Amnesty International also called for its complete withdrawal, while the New York-based Human Rights Watch said the proposed legislation fell short of international human rights standards.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Rights groups have also raised concerns over extended detention, the admissibility of confessions made to senior police officers, restrictions on bail, police surveillance and searches and arrests without warrants.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #23 of 30 (21 NOV)

📰 Sri Lanka's organised crime bill gets Supreme Court nod

📌 Published: 21 Nov 2026, 10:50:32 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: In Sri Lanka, citizens can challenge a Bill's constitutionality in the Supreme Court within one week of its introduction in Parliament. The Bill had earlier faced 20 petitions in the Supreme Court challenging its constitutionality

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Sri Lanka's proposed Prevention of Organised Crimes Bill has received the Supreme Court's nod, which ruled that its provisions are "not inconsistent" with the Constitution, Speaker Jagath Wickremaratna told Parliament on Saturday (November 21, 2026). The Bill, tabled in Parliament on October 20, has drawn criticism from local and international rights groups concerned that its provisions could undermine fundamental rights and grant sweeping powers to law enforcement agencies. In Sri Lanka, citizens can challenge a Bill's constitutionality in the Supreme Court within one week of its introduction in Parliament. The Bill had earlier faced 20 petitions in the Supreme Court challenging its constitutionality. The Speaker on Saturday (November 21, 2026) confirmed the Supreme Court's nod for the Bill and listed the clauses it directed Parliament to amend. "The clauses in the Bill are not inconsistent with the Constitution and may be passed by a simple majority of Parliament, subject to making the amendment at the committee stage," Mr. Wickremaratna said. He said Clause 6, which allowed the prosecution of an individual who is not a member of a criminal gang, should be deleted, citing the Court's directions. Criticism of the Bill has centred on its broad definition of organised crime and provisions that could allow authorities to identify individuals as gang members based on their appearance or associations. Sri Lanka's Human Rights Commission called for the Bill's withdrawal, while the Bar Association of Sri Lanka raised concerns about its impact on fundamental rights and safeguards for judicial oversight. Rights body Amnesty International also called for its complete withdrawal, while the New York-based Human Rights Watch said the proposed legislation fell short of international human rights standards.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Rights groups have also raised concerns over extended detention, the admissibility of confessions made to senior police officers, restrictions on bail, police surveillance and searches and arrests without warrants.

Enforcement (Noun)
सख्ती से कानून लागू करना — किसी नियम या आदेश का ज़मीनी स्तर पर पालन करवाना।

संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप।
✓ Syn: Statutory, Legitimate, Lawful  |  ✖ Ant: Unconstitutional, Illegal, Arbitrary
International (Adjective)
अंतरराष्ट्रीय — इस अनुच्छेद में 'International' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Admissibility (Noun)
स्वीकार्यता — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Admissibility' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial

A. In Sri Lanka, citizens can challenge a Bill's constitutionality in the Supreme Court within one week of its introduction in Parliament.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Sri Lanka's organised crime bill gets Supreme Co' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Sri Lanka's organised crime bill gets Supreme' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Sri Lanka's organised crime bill gets Supreme' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "In Sri Lanka, citizens can challenge a Bill's constitutionality in the Supreme Court within one week of its introduction in Parliament." ✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. articles.title: Yemen's Houthis launch strikes after Saudi coalition's 'special operation'
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The strikes came after the Houthis vowed revenge for the coalition's attack on the Red Sea port city of Hodeida and other targets on November 20

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Yemen's Houthis launched strikes on the Saudi capital Riyadh on Saturday (November 21, 2026), after vowing reprisals for a "special operation" by the Saudi-led coalition fighting them. Saudi Arabia has been battling a surge in attacks since fighting reignited in neighbouring Yemen's civil war this summer, where Riyadh backs the internationally recognised government against the Houthis. An AFP journalist reported hearing two explosions shortly after authorities issued an alert, later lifted, saying the city was "under a hostile aerial threat". The coalition later said it had "intercepted and destroyed" three Houthi ballistic missiles headed for the capital. The Iran-backed Houthis said on X that they were striking targets across Saudi Arabia, including in Riyadh. The strikes came after the Houthis vowed revenge for the coalition's attack on the Red Sea port city of Hodeida and other targets on Friday (November 20, 2026). The "special operation" hit smuggling and weapons-transporting operations in Hodeida, the coalition said. It also involved attacks on Sanaa, Saada and Taiz governorates, marking an uptick in violence after months of hostilities. The Houthis had vowed to hit the Saudi city of Jeddah and other Red Sea ports if Hodeida was attacked, while warning airlines that Saudi airspace was "unsafe". The group also threatened Riyadh's financial district and a power station in Al-Shuqaiq.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki said its forces had "targeted operational capabilities at Hodeida port that were used in smuggling operations and the transport of weapons and ballistic missiles".

📰 Yemen's Houthis launch strikes after Saudi coalition's 'special operation'

📌 Published: 21 Nov 2026, 10:44:14 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The strikes came after the Houthis vowed revenge for the coalition's attack on the Red Sea port city of Hodeida and other targets on November 20

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Yemen's Houthis launched strikes on the Saudi capital Riyadh on Saturday (November 21, 2026), after vowing reprisals for a "special operation" by the Saudi-led coalition fighting them. Saudi Arabia has been battling a surge in attacks since fighting reignited in neighbouring Yemen's civil war this summer, where Riyadh backs the internationally recognised government against the Houthis. An AFP journalist reported hearing two explosions shortly after authorities issued an alert, later lifted, saying the city was "under a hostile aerial threat". The coalition later said it had "intercepted and destroyed" three Houthi ballistic missiles headed for the capital. The Iran-backed Houthis said on X that they were striking targets across Saudi Arabia, including in Riyadh. The strikes came after the Houthis vowed revenge for the coalition's attack on the Red Sea port city of Hodeida and other targets on Friday (November 20, 2026). The "special operation" hit smuggling and weapons-transporting operations in Hodeida, the coalition said. It also involved attacks on Sanaa, Saada and Taiz governorates, marking an uptick in violence after months of hostilities. The Houthis had vowed to hit the Saudi city of Jeddah and other Red Sea ports if Hodeida was attacked, while warning airlines that Saudi airspace was "unsafe". The group also threatened Riyadh's financial district and a power station in Al-Shuqaiq.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki said its forces had "targeted operational capabilities at Hodeida port that were used in smuggling operations and the transport of weapons and ballistic missiles".

articles.title: The Rohingya | Vindication for a persecuted people
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The International Court of Justice’s ruling that Myanmar committed genocide during its 2017 ‘clearance operations’ offers a measure of justice for the ethnic and religious minority, but the court has no means of enforcing its judgment

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: In a first of a kind ruling, the International Court of Justice held on November 19 that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya in northern Rakhine State during the military’s “clearance operations” in 2017. This was the first time the ICJ found a state responsible for committing genocide. Nine judges against six voted in favour of the ruling, in a case brought in 2019 by The Gambia. The court also found that Myanmar failed to prevent genocide by civilians who joined its forces, failed to punish the perpetrators, never enacted the laws that the Genocide Convention requires, and destroyed evidence in breach of the court’s 2020 interim order. It also rejected, by 14 votes to one, the charge that Myanmar directly and publicly incited private persons to commit genocide, but declined to order citizenship for the Rohingya. The judgment holds the state of Myanmar to account but does not convict any individual. It is final and cannot be appealed. The court ordered Myanmar to investigate and, if warranted, prosecute those responsible, guarantee that the violations will not recur, allow the “safe, voluntary and dignified” return of the displaced, restore their property and compensate the Rohingya. The amount of compensation is to be fixed later, after Myanmar reports back to the court within two years. The Rohingya are a predominantly Muslim people who speak an Indo-Aryan language close to the Chittagonian dialect. The 2014 Census in Myanmar estimated over a million Rohingya in the country, concentrated in Maungdaw, Buthidaung and Rathedaung along the Bangladesh border. Muslims have lived in Rakhine or Arakan from the time of the Mrauk U kingdom (15th to 18th century). In 1799, the British physician Francis Buchanan recorded that Muslims “long settled in Arakan” called themselves the “Rooinga”.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Many joined them, coming from Chittagong during colonial rule. Historian Jacques Leider has said the “Rohingya” took on a political and ethnic meaning in the late 1950s, when Muslim leaders adopted it to claim the status of a “national race”. In 1961, Brig. Aung Gyi of the Burmese Army publicly accepted them as an ethnic group. But this was before the coup by General Ne Win in 1962 which heralded decades of rule by the military junta in the country.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #24 of 30 (21 NOV)

📰 The Rohingya | Vindication for a persecuted people

📌 Published: 21 Nov 2026, 11:50:18 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The International Court of Justice’s ruling that Myanmar committed genocide during its 2017 ‘clearance operations’ offers a measure of justice for the ethnic and religious minority, but the court has no means of enforcing its judgment

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: In a first of a kind ruling, the International Court of Justice held on November 19 that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya in northern Rakhine State during the military’s “clearance operations” in 2017. This was the first time the ICJ found a state responsible for committing genocide. Nine judges against six voted in favour of the ruling, in a case brought in 2019 by The Gambia. The court also found that Myanmar failed to prevent genocide by civilians who joined its forces, failed to punish the perpetrators, never enacted the laws that the Genocide Convention requires, and destroyed evidence in breach of the court’s 2020 interim order. It also rejected, by 14 votes to one, the charge that Myanmar directly and publicly incited private persons to commit genocide, but declined to order citizenship for the Rohingya. The judgment holds the state of Myanmar to account but does not convict any individual. It is final and cannot be appealed. The court ordered Myanmar to investigate and, if warranted, prosecute those responsible, guarantee that the violations will not recur, allow the “safe, voluntary and dignified” return of the displaced, restore their property and compensate the Rohingya. The amount of compensation is to be fixed later, after Myanmar reports back to the court within two years. The Rohingya are a predominantly Muslim people who speak an Indo-Aryan language close to the Chittagonian dialect. The 2014 Census in Myanmar estimated over a million Rohingya in the country, concentrated in Maungdaw, Buthidaung and Rathedaung along the Bangladesh border. Muslims have lived in Rakhine or Arakan from the time of the Mrauk U kingdom (15th to 18th century). In 1799, the British physician Francis Buchanan recorded that Muslims “long settled in Arakan” called themselves the “Rooinga”.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Many joined them, coming from Chittagong during colonial rule. Historian Jacques Leider has said the “Rohingya” took on a political and ethnic meaning in the late 1950s, when Muslim leaders adopted it to claim the status of a “national race”. In 1961, Brig. Aung Gyi of the Burmese Army publicly accepted them as an ethnic group. But this was before the coup by General Ne Win in 1962 which heralded decades of rule by the military junta in the country.

Enforcement (Noun)
सख्ती से कानून लागू करना — किसी नियम या आदेश का ज़मीनी स्तर पर पालन करवाना।
✓ Syn: Implementation, Execution, Administration  |  ✖ Ant: Neglect, Abandonment, Waiver
Accountability (Noun)
जवाबदेही — अपने फैसलों और काम का जनता तथा संविधान को हिसाब देने की बाध्यता।
✓ Syn: Responsibility, Answerability, Liability  |  ✖ Ant: Immunity, Exemption, Irresponsibility
International (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'International' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Compensation (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Compensation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial

D. The author contends that 'The Rohingya | Vindication for a persecuted p' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.

articles.title: Going public on AI: On Anthropic IPO
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: India can no longer afford its silence on the multi-trillion dollar AI arms race

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Initial Public Offering (IPO) of Anthropic , PBC is a mile marker in the arms race to develop superintelligent systems driven by generative AI . Traders valued the firm at $1.27 trillion, a denomination that is bound to become more and more familiar in an industry backed by an endless appetite for capital and unprecedented forms of financialisation. Anthropic’s statements emphasise warnings on the safety of its systems and the consequences of unbridled development of advanced systems. In the history of the development of this technology, this PR spin may just be a blip. After all, their testing has led to AI agents that have broken out of sandboxes and infected unsuspecting organisations’ internal systems: a deluge of agentic chaos that is already a reality has led to little signs of the firm backing its words with action. A familiar trend is playing out, with open source LLMs showing frontier capabilities that can back their erratic impulses, appearing in the space of just months, or sometimes weeks. Advocates of pacing the frontier and managing these emerging risks have been marginalised in a way that has little precedent in this century. It is time for governments to get involved, and specifically, for India to raise its voice on these risks, loudly and unequivocally.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: While India’s AI industry is nascent, its positions on international forums carry the weight of a sixth of humanity. A mix of cynical calculations and practical considerations have blunted the use of that voice, for example in the U.S.’s hugely destabilising war of choice against Iran, and Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza. In taking a strong position on what could be the defining transformation of this decade, India has little to lose, and a lot to contribute. India’s AI policies are geared towards diffusion and research of helpful capabilities that can trickle down to the common citizen. The capabilities that the Union government and State governments seek to boost by leveraging AI are removed from the frontier research wreaking havoc within the information security profession around the world. Out-of-control AI agents promise, moreover, significant disruption to outdated government and private systems online. While India has little commercial leverage to curb San Francisco’s accelerationism, its voice is sure to be noticed. India’s focus on AI in international fora, such as the AI Impact Summit in Delhi, has been on consensus. This approach must change. India cannot be silent amid a U.S.-China technological race which could lead to catastrophic damage. New Delhi must not allow the U.S. to stop it from pushing for AI safety.

hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — आख़िरकार, उनके परीक्षण ने एआई एजेंटों को जन्म दिया है जो सैंडबॉक्स से बाहर निकल गए हैं और बिना सोचे-समझे संगठनों के आंतरिक सिस्टम को संक्रमित कर दिया है: एजेंटिक अराजकता की बाढ़ जो पहले से ही एक वास्तविकता है, ने फर्म के अपने शब्दों को कार्रवाई के साथ समर्थन करने के बहुत कम संकेत दिए हैं।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'International' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'International' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — एक परिचित प्रवृत्ति चल रही है, जिसमें ओपन सोर्स एलएलएम अग्रणी क्षमताएं दिखा रहे हैं जो उनके अनियमित आवेगों को वापस कर सकते हैं, जो कुछ महीनों या कभी-कभी हफ्तों के अंतराल में दिखाई देते हैं।।

hinglishTracks.en: Advocates of pacing the frontier and managing these emerging risks have been marginalised in a way that has little precedent in this century.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — सीमा पर तेजी से आगे बढ़ने और इन उभरते जोखिमों के प्रबंधन की वकालत करने वालों को इस तरह से हाशिए पर डाल दिया गया है, जिसकी इस सदी में बहुत कम मिसाल है।।

✍️ Editorial & Opinion Paragraph #3 of 30 (21 NOV)

📰 Going public on AI: On Anthropic IPO

📌 Published: 21 Nov 2026, 11:17:20 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: India can no longer afford its silence on the multi-trillion dollar AI arms race

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Initial Public Offering (IPO) of Anthropic , PBC is a mile marker in the arms race to develop superintelligent systems driven by generative AI . Traders valued the firm at $1.27 trillion, a denomination that is bound to become more and more familiar in an industry backed by an endless appetite for capital and unprecedented forms of financialisation. Anthropic’s statements emphasise warnings on the safety of its systems and the consequences of unbridled development of advanced systems. In the history of the development of this technology, this PR spin may just be a blip. After all, their testing has led to AI agents that have broken out of sandboxes and infected unsuspecting organisations’ internal systems: a deluge of agentic chaos that is already a reality has led to little signs of the firm backing its words with action. A familiar trend is playing out, with open source LLMs showing frontier capabilities that can back their erratic impulses, appearing in the space of just months, or sometimes weeks. Advocates of pacing the frontier and managing these emerging risks have been marginalised in a way that has little precedent in this century. It is time for governments to get involved, and specifically, for India to raise its voice on these risks, loudly and unequivocally.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: While India’s AI industry is nascent, its positions on international forums carry the weight of a sixth of humanity. A mix of cynical calculations and practical considerations have blunted the use of that voice, for example in the U.S.’s hugely destabilising war of choice against Iran, and Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza. In taking a strong position on what could be the defining transformation of this decade, India has little to lose, and a lot to contribute. India’s AI policies are geared towards diffusion and research of helpful capabilities that can trickle down to the common citizen. The capabilities that the Union government and State governments seek to boost by leveraging AI are removed from the frontier research wreaking havoc within the information security profession around the world. Out-of-control AI agents promise, moreover, significant disruption to outdated government and private systems online. While India has little commercial leverage to curb San Francisco’s accelerationism, its voice is sure to be noticed. India’s focus on AI in international fora, such as the AI Impact Summit in Delhi, has been on consensus. This approach must change. India cannot be silent amid a U.S.-China technological race which could lead to catastrophic damage. New Delhi must not allow the U.S. to stop it from pushing for AI safety.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Financialisation (Noun)
वित्तीयकरण — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Financialisation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Transformation (Noun)
परिवर्तन — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Transformation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
International (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'International' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Technological (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Technological' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above ✍️ Editorial & Opinion passage on "Going public on AI: On Anthropic IPO", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. India can no longer afford its silence on the multi-trillion dollar AI arms race.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Going public on AI: On Anthropic IPO' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Going public on AI: On Anthropic IPO' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Going public on AI: On Anthropic IPO' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "India can no longer afford its silence on the multi-trillion dollar AI arms race." (Hinglish Arth: भारत अब खरबों डॉलर की एआई हथियारों की होड़ पर अपनी चुप्पी बर्दाश्त नहीं कर सकता)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Going public on AI: On Anthropic IPO"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. to stop it from pushing for AI safety.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "to stop it from pushing for AI safety." (Hinglish Arth: इसे एआई सुरक्षा पर जोर देने से रोकने के लिए।)

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The core sector performance in October is a good example of how statistical distortions can create incorrect assessments of the economy. The 10.9% growth rate, a series high, has been celebrated as a sign of the Indian economy’s strength and resilience. There is, no doubt, an aspect of this has been reflected in the numbers, especially to do with infrastructure creation. However, the much more impactful factor behind the high core sector growth was a low base effect. The overall Index of Core Industries grew just 0.8% in October 2025 and so, in relation, the performance in October 2026 looked that much faster. This low base effect is even starker when looking at individual sectors within the index. The coal sector grew at a blistering 23% in October, more than twice its growth rate in the previous month. Yet, a large part of this was propelled by the fact that the sector had contracted nearly 8.5% last October. The rest of the sector’s growth was driven by demand of the electricity and iron ore sectors, or so the data show. The electricity sector also grew at a series high of nearly 22% in October, but on the back of a near-7% contraction in October last year. This base effect anomaly is likely down to the fact that the festive season starts at different but similar points every year. As such, a more accurate reading of the economy will be possible once the data for November are available.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The construction-related sectors seem to have seen genuine growth, a reflection of the government’s ongoing infrastructure push. The iron ore sector’s growth rate accelerated to a three-month high of 26.4% in October 2026 as compared to a growth of 8.7% in the same month last year. Steel grew at 7.3% versus 9.5% last year, and cement by 15.4% versus 5.2%. The economy’s dependence on government spending is not going to ease in the near future, and might even intensify as higher costs eat into companies’ profit margins. The core sector data once again highlighted a major reason for these higher costs — the oil and gas sectors. The crude oil sector shrank by 4.1%, its 22nd consecutive month of contraction. The natural gas sector, similarly, contracted 7.6%, a series-worst performance and the 28th straight month of contraction. A major reason behind high inflation in India is the underperformance of these two sectors and the resultant dependence on imported fuel. It is time the Petroleum Ministry candidly explains — to Parliament in December or to the public directly — why India’s fuel output has been continuously falling. If it is a matter of a lack of resources underground, that is one thing, but the underperformance of oil and gas public sector undertakings is quite another. Accountability needs to be set.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Climate action has to be timely, with adequate resources and monitoring

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: That all was not well with the Green India Mission was clear even before its approval. After the UPA-I government announced it in 2008, the Ministry of Rural Development had objected to its financial design much before the Union Cabinet approved it in 2014. But the Environment Ministry proceeded anyway and retained largely the same arrangement when it revised the Mission in 2021. Following the Comptroller and Auditor General’s report, on November 19, the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) upbraided the Ministry for the Mission’s virtual failure and for still not having issued the implementation guidelines for the revised form. The original 10-year vision was to expand forest and tree cover by 5 million hectares (mha), improve forest quality on another 5 mha, improve forest-related livelihoods for 3 million households, and sequester up to 60 million tonnes of carbon dioxide a year. The outlay was ₹46,000 crore. In 2014, the Cabinet approved ₹13,000 crore for 1.4 mha each of the first two objectives by 2018, but to be supported to the tune of 81.5% by Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority (CAMPA), National Afforestation Programme (NAP), and MGNREGS funds. In 2021-22, the Ministry folded the NAP into the Mission and, in mid-2025, unveiled a revised version with an allocation of ₹12,190 crore to improve forest cover on 25 mha by 2030, including 24 mha through other schemes. The government had thus expanded the primary target but left the Mission responsible for only 1 mha.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Together with the CAMPA, NAP, and MGNREGS funds never materialising, it is no surprise that the programmes to improve forest quality and forest cover have respectively fallen short by 91.8% and 97.5% vis-à-vis the 2014 target. The Environment Ministry had assembled a large programme around resources that it knew it could not control. Pro-climate work in practice ought to span government schemes to deliver action and justice, and the Ministry ought to have formalised the division of responsibilities and accounting system. The PAC’s new demand that the Ministry submit an implementation timetable is insufficient. From the Jal Shakti Abhiyan in 2019 to the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan in 2024, the government has often floated new programmes banking significantly on funds from existing schemes — an untenable policy when the latter also have their own obligations. And if the VB-G RAM G scheme was to also advance climate justice, the government should not have undermined the erstwhile demand-driven funding model and shifted more financial responsibility to the States. Climate action has to be timely, for which the Union government must dedicate adequate resources and proactively ensure that its initiatives are implemented.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: India can no longer afford its silence on the multi-trillion dollar AI arms race

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Initial Public Offering (IPO) of Anthropic , PBC is a mile marker in the arms race to develop superintelligent systems driven by generative AI . Traders valued the firm at $1.27 trillion, a denomination that is bound to become more and more familiar in an industry backed by an endless appetite for capital and unprecedented forms of financialisation. Anthropic’s statements emphasise warnings on the safety of its systems and the consequences of unbridled development of advanced systems. In the history of the development of this technology, this PR spin may just be a blip. After all, their testing has led to AI agents that have broken out of sandboxes and infected unsuspecting organisations’ internal systems: a deluge of agentic chaos that is already a reality has led to little signs of the firm backing its words with action. A familiar trend is playing out, with open source LLMs showing frontier capabilities that can back their erratic impulses, appearing in the space of just months, or sometimes weeks. Advocates of pacing the frontier and managing these emerging risks have been marginalised in a way that has little precedent in this century. It is time for governments to get involved, and specifically, for India to raise its voice on these risks, loudly and unequivocally.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: While India’s AI industry is nascent, its positions on international forums carry the weight of a sixth of humanity. A mix of cynical calculations and practical considerations have blunted the use of that voice, for example in the U.S.’s hugely destabilising war of choice against Iran, and Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza. In taking a strong position on what could be the defining transformation of this decade, India has little to lose, and a lot to contribute. India’s AI policies are geared towards diffusion and research of helpful capabilities that can trickle down to the common citizen. The capabilities that the Union government and State governments seek to boost by leveraging AI are removed from the frontier research wreaking havoc within the information security profession around the world. Out-of-control AI agents promise, moreover, significant disruption to outdated government and private systems online. While India has little commercial leverage to curb San Francisco’s accelerationism, its voice is sure to be noticed. India’s focus on AI in international fora, such as the AI Impact Summit in Delhi, has been on consensus. This approach must change. India cannot be silent amid a U.S.-China technological race which could lead to catastrophic damage. New Delhi must not allow the U.S. to stop it from pushing for AI safety.

1. Core Context & Background: U.S., China, Russia must draw up a roadmap for talks on nuclear weapons

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The first trilateral summit between the Presidents of China, the U.S. and Russia , held in Shenzhen on November 19, reflected both the changing global order and the leaders’ shared desire to remain engaged with one another in an increasingly unpredictable world. For U.S. President Donald Trump, the summit was a platform where he could push for joint talks between the world’s three largest nuclear powers on reducing nuclear warheads. After the New START treaty between the U.S. and Russia expired in February 2026, Moscow had signalled that it was ready for talks, but Mr. Trump wanted to involve China as well. For President Xi Jinping, the summit reinforced China’s position as a peer competitor to the U.S. While Russia seeks to deepen partnership with China, the U.S. is looking to build strategic stability. And for Russian President Vladimir Putin, whom the West sought to isolate after he launched the invasion of Ukraine, the summit offered a seat at the high table. The decision to start trilateral talks on nuclear arms and the joint declaration, which stated that ‘a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought’, are steps in the right direction. But much will depend on what follows.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Many had compared the meet to the 1945 Yalta Conference, when Russian leader Joseph Stalin, U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt and British Prime Minister Winston Churchill met to discuss the future of post-War Europe. But Shenzhen was not a summit of the victors of a major war. This was more about three great powers setting terms of engagement in a changing world. The summit failed to achieve any breakthrough on any of the issues on the agenda — nuclear arms reduction, non-proliferation or the Ukraine war — or even offer a road map for the future. Moreover, it is not clear if the Shenzhen spirit could be sustained in the medium to long-term as another President in the U.S. could take a very different approach towards Russia and China. The three leaders have called for reform of the UN. While it is a welcome move, any attempt to reform the international system and institutions must also involve other powers, particularly rising middle powers such as India, South Africa and Brazil. But the Shenzhen framework could bring greater stability and predictability to great-power relations. This is important given that two of the Big Three are currently waging two separate wars. The leaders should draw up a clear road map for nuclear talks and other key issues outlined in the Shenzhen declaration, with realistic and achievable objectives. Otherwise, the summit would amount to little more than another diplomatic photo-op.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: The ECI offers relief to a section of deleted electors but SIR’s flaws remain

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Following the Special Summary Revision (SSR) by the Election Commission of India (ECI) in some States that had undergone the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) , mostly in Phases 1 and 2, some 74 lakh names were added onto the electoral rolls. This meant that the electorate in those 13 States, that had shrunk from 49.61 crore to 45.22 crore after the SIR, has now gone up to 45.96 crore. The ECI has extended the SSR to States and UTs in Phase 3. As before, it requires no proof of citizenship or mapping to older rolls, and insists on personal notice before any deletion other than of the dead. It also directs Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) to cross-verify deletions personally wherever they exceed 2% of a polling station’s electors. Draft deletions in Phase 3 of the SIR averaged 17% , and reached 32.8% in Delhi . The ECI also offered another opportunity to electors deleted by the SIR in the seven States and UTs where it is still underway, such as Delhi and Maharashtra, to return to the rolls. Electors who did not return their forms can do so now, explaining the delay, and those who moved within the State can return through the enumeration form with proof of their new address. EROs will process these forms under Rule 21(1) of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and restore the elector’s old EPIC number. These “corrective” measures follow the Supreme Court’s observation on October 28 that forcing deleted electors to re-enrol through Form 6, meant for new voters, was an “error”. The ECI’s use of remedies that existed in the registration rules is a tacit admission that it went wrong during the SIR. But the measures are limited. They reach roughly 4.5 crore of the 13.37 crore struck off the draft rolls and do not cover electors who moved out of their States. Electors in States where the SIR has concluded, including Bihar and West Bengal, which have already voted on the SIR rolls, can return only through the SSR, by filing Form 6 as new voters, with fresh EPIC numbers and no record that they were ever on the roll. In essence, the structure of the SIR remains intact. Electors must still provide details from “the last SIR”, and those whose details are unavailable or do not match will be asked for documents in a manner that amounts to a citizenship test. The legality of the ludicrous “logical discrepancy” checks remains unaddressed. The 2002-03 special revision offered a better way. Those who had shifted homes were enumerated door to door at their new addresses. The Supreme Court must direct the ECI to return to that model.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Election Commission of India / Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls / election / India

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Europe must be part of any settlement on the Ukraine war

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The trilateral negotiations in Abu Dhabi between Russia, Ukraine and the U.S. earlier this month failed to produce a major breakthrough or bridge the wide gap between Kyiv and Moscow. Yet, they were a good beginning towards finding a political settlement to Europe’s longest war since the Second World War . In the two-day talks, hosted by the U.S., the warring sides agreed on some humanitarian measures, including prisoner exchange. U.S. representatives Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow after the talks to discuss the proposal. In the next stage, U.S., Ukrainian and European officials will meet in Berlin to discuss a coordinated European and Ukrainian position towards the peace process. As of now, Russian and Ukrainian positions remain far apart. Russia demands Ukraine withdraw from the territories of Donbas it still controls to stop attacks. Russia also wants to introduce limits to Ukrainian military capabilities and Kyiv to declare neutrality (give up its NATO ambitions). Ukraine, on the other hand, has rejected making any territorial concessions for a settlement and asked for security guarantees from the West so that Russia would not attack the country again. That Ukraine survived Russia’s invasion and continued to resist Russian forces for almost five years is no small feat. But it has also paid a huge price for its resistance. The country has lost more than 20% of its territory. Millions have fled, while men of fighting age are being drafted into the military . Ukraine’s economy is kept afloat by European support, while its military continues to rely on NATO for weapons and other supplies. Until recently, the West stood united in its support for Ukraine against Russia, but that unity has since begun to fray. U.S. President Donald Trump, who has lifted sanctions on Russian diesel, is seeking to reset Washington’s ties with Moscow . European leaders, who initially sought to isolate Russia, have also started reestablishing contacts with the Kremlin. In October, Finnish and Norwegian leaders held direct talks with Mr. Putin. To be sure, Ukraine’s long-range strikes can hurt Russia, as the recent attack on the Kerch Bridge demonstrated. But such strikes are unlikely to change the Kremlin’s thinking about the war. As the conflict drags on, Ukraine’s position is weakening, and its allies are growing increasingly divided. After almost five years, Russia has failed to take a decisive victory. Ukraine does not have a credible path towards victory either. A diplomatic settlement, therefore, is the only way forward. The Abu Dhabi talks recognised this reality. But for the process to be meaningful, Europe must also be brought to the negotiating table.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: World / Ukraine / USA / Russia-Ukraine Crisis / war / war

The corporation attributed the growth in fare-box collections primarily to higher passenger ridership following the commissioning of the 19.15-km Reach-5 Yellow Line between RV Road and Bommasandra in August 2025. BMRCL reported that trains operated with a punctuality rate of 99.85% during the financial year. Services commenced at 5 a.m. on Mondays to cater to passengers travelling early in the morning, while the last train services operated until 11.30 pm. The corporation also reported an operational profit of ₹417.42 crore and a cash profit of ₹209.66 crore during 2025–26. dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: A Bench headed by CJI Surya Kant made absolute its interim order staying any coercive measures over 31.37 acres of government land allegedly encroached upon by the Thanjavur university

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Supreme Court on Monday (November 23, 2026) admitted an appeal filed by Shanmugha Arts Science Technology and Research Academy (SASTRA), a deemed university based in Thanjavur, against a Madras High Court direction to the Tamil Nadu government to evict it from 31.37 acres of public land in its occupation for nearly 40 years. The Court had already stayed the eviction of the university in an order passed on January 15, 2026, and had allowed the institution to carry out its activities without any hindrance. At that hearing, the Court asked the State government to consider three options of alternative lands offered by the university, instead of the land occupied and already utilised by it, represented by senior advocate Mukul Rohatgi. A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant had found the three options “just and fair”, and asked the State to consider the offer “sympathetically and take an appropriate decision by ensuring that no loss is caused to the public exchequer”. It also suggested that a high-powered committee of three senior officers of the State government accord a personal hearing to the university to “explain all the attending circumstances and also to persuade the authorities to accept one of the three options”. On August 10, 2026, the Court gave the State, represented by senior advocate Jaideep Gupta and Tamil Nadu Additional Advocate General Haripriya Padmanabhan, a “free hand in determining the actual market value of land” under dispute, with the university obligated to pay. The August order also recorded the university’s offer to pay the sale price of any land the State required for a public purpose, in this case the establishment of a prison, for which it wanted the disputed 31.37-acre property. The Court asked the State to take a “reasonably fair decision and apprise this court”. However, at the next hearing on September 21, 2026, the State sought more time to “consider the different options”. At the September 21 hearing, the Court noted that the land in dispute was used by an educational institution serving a public purpose, and asked why the State was so “obstinate” on eviction and demolition of the institution.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The State government had contended that the alternate parcels were inferior to the disputed land in terms of value, accessibility and contiguity, and that settling for alternative land could amount to putting a premium on encroachment.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Declining to directly examine the allegations, the Supreme Court asked the petitioner to approach the jurisdictional High Court, saying that every alleged violation of a Supreme Court judgment cannot be brought directly before the apex court

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Supreme Court on Monday (November 23, 2026) declined to entertain a plea alleging that the demolition of a 100-year-old mosque in Uttar Pradesh's Saharanpur district violated the demolition guidelines laid down by it in a landmark 2024 judgment on the use of bulldozers . A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana was hearing a plea filed by Imran Ahmad against Uttar Pradesh Chief Secretary Shashi Prakash Goyal, alleging non-compliance with the apex court's directions. Declining to undertake a direct examination of the allegations, the Bench asked the petitioner to approach the jurisdictional High Court, saying that every alleged violation of a Supreme Court judgment cannot be brought directly before the apex court. "Every order violating a Supreme Court judgment cannot come back to the Supreme Court itself. You have to go to the respective high court," CJI said. The Bench said determining whether the demolition guidelines had been violated would require an examination of the specific facts and circumstances surrounding the alleged demolition, a task more appropriately undertaken by the jurisdictional High Court. "We have laid down the principles, but then wherever these principles have been violated, in what factual context and background? Please go to the concerned high court, establish your case on facts, and if the high court doesn't grant you necessary relief, then come to us," the CJI said. The Bench further clarified that it could not undertake a factual inquiry into the allegations in the contempt proceedings. ALSO WATCH Watch: How the Supreme Court clamped down on ‘bulldozer’ demolitions | Explained However, the Bench made it clear that if the High Court, upon examining the matter, finds that the Supreme Court's directions have been violated, appropriate consequences would follow.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The petitioner was asked to approach the jurisdictional High Court and seek appropriate relief.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Demands are growing to stop such heavy machines in the ecologically fragile region

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A viral video of an earthmover operating at Sheshnag — the high-altitude and inaccessible glacial lake located 11,780 feet above sea level in south Kashmir’s Pahalgam — evoked outrage from political parties and locals on Monday (November 23). Demands are growing to stop such heavy machines in the ecologically fragile region. The undated video shows an earthmover filling a site at the lake's edge, which spans 1.1 kilometres in length and 0.7 kilometres in width. Sheshnag is a stopover for pilgrims heading to the annual Amarnath Yatra in south Kashmir’s Anantnag. A macadamised road for the pilgrims ends at Chandanwari. In the past, pilgrims trekked 12 to 13 kilometres on an unpaved mountain track to reach the lake. The Amarnath cave is 18-20 km from the stopover. Opposition People’s Democratic Party (PDP) spokesman Mohit Bhan said Sheshnag was not just another lake in the mountains of Kashmir. “In Hinduism, it is the sacred landscape where Lord Shiva is believed to have left behind the serpents before proceeding towards the Amarnath Cave to narrate the Amar Katha to Goddess Parvati. There is a profound contradiction in invoking Hindu faith while allowing the very landscape associated with that faith to be disturbed through unnecessary construction, road cutting and surface levelling,” said Mr. Bhan. The visuals and reports of heavy machinery operating near the pristine Sheshnag Lake, in the glacial zone of Pahalgam are very disturbing, raising serious concern among people about the ecological impact of construction in this fragile Himalayan region. With our glaciers already retreating, and recent devastating glacier-related floods in neighbouring Nepal reminding us of the growing vulnerability of the Himalayas, such activities raise alarm. Kashmir has always warmly welcomed Amarnath Yatra pilgrims, and improving facilities for them has never been an issue. But not at the cost of our fragile ecosystem. Those governing owe answers to people for the serious environmental concerns created by such "developmental projects"! Our precious mountains, glaciers and water bodies need protection not plunder, for now and for the future generations. So this must be immediately stopped. He said what is being projected as development must not come at the cost of a fragile alpine ecosystem and a landscape deeply embedded in Hindu religious belief. “Faith and ecology are not competing interests. Both demand protection. You cannot celebrate the sanctity of a pilgrimage while disregarding the sanctity of the landscape through which it passes. If we cannot respect Sacred Sheshnag, what exactly are we preserving in the name of the Amarnath Yatra?” he said. Kashmir’s chief cleric Mirwaiz Umar Farooq said the visuals and reports of heavy machinery operating near the pristine lake, in the glacial zone of Pahalgam, were “very disturbing”, “raising serious concern among people about the ecological impact of construction in this fragile Himalayan region”. “With our glaciers already retreating, and recent devastating glacier-related floods in neighbouring Nepal reminding us of the growing vulnerability of the Himalayas, such activities raise alarm. Kashmir has always warmly welcomed Amarnath Yatra pilgrims, and improving facilities for them has never been an issue. But not at the cost of our fragile ecosystem. Those governing owe answers to people for the serious environmental concerns created by such ‘developmental projects’! Our precious mountains, glaciers and water bodies need protection, not plunder, for now and for future generations. So, this must be immediately stopped,” said the Mirwaiz. Many commented on the video, which went viral on social media platforms in the past 24 hours. “Sheshnag Lake is one of the 14 officially identified high-risk glacial lakes in J&K for GLOF (glacial lake outburst flood). Heavy machinery is being run on its shoreline with zero transparency on environmental clearance or risk assessment. This is not development. This is deliberate endangerment of a fragile alpine ecosystem and downstream communities,” said Suhail Ahmed Khan, from Kashmir.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Raja Muzaffar Bhat, a prominent environmentalist and activist, termed the earthmover at the high-altitude lake a “disaster”. “How does such a heavy machine reach our glaciers of Kashmir?” he asked.
